outcome.refusal_reason: The mechanism, as written, does not do what it says for the target shape, and the formula can be read two ways. Read from the anchor code: for Q8_0, blocks_per_iter = MMQ_ITER_K/qk = 256/32 = 8 (mmq.cuh:9, :991), and ssm_alpha/beta have blocks_per_ne00 = 5120/32 = 160. mul_mat_q rounds each CTA's kbc down to a multiple of 8 (mmq.cuh:997-998). So the current 104-CTA grid already has only 20 non-empty CTAs, and each covers exactly one [8b, 8b+8) iteration. If 'kblocks' means blocks_per_ne00, the cap is ceil(160/8) = 20. That reproduces the same 20 k-ranges, the same 19 partials written to tmp_fixup, and the same backward summation order in mul_mat_q_stream_k_fixup. The result would be bit-identical: no change to partial-buffer traffic and no change to partial-sum grouping, which contradicts the 'tolerance-class' declaration. Its only effect is to shorten the fixup CTA's serial walk from 103 to 19 iterations; the 84 iterations removed only skip empty CTAs and do int64 kbc divides (mmq.cuh:1179). It would also launch 84 fewer no-op CTAs. That saving is probably a fraction of the 31.6 µs per call and may fall inside the serving floor. A null there would wrongly close the stream-k-cap mechanism. If 'kblocks' instead means ITER_K iterations (20, as in the brief's H11), the cap is 3 CTAs. Each would run 6-7 serial, single-buffered load/sync/MFMA iterations, so the main kernel (10.5 µs today) grows while the fixup collapses. That version is genuinely tolerance-class and needs pricing. To refine: (1) define the cap in code units, e.g. ceil(blocks_per_ne00 / (blocks_per_iter * k_iters_per_cta)), and state the resulting CTA count and partial count for 160 blocks; (2) declare bit-exactness correctly: the 20-CTA variant is bit-exact, fewer CTAs is tolerance; (3) price the main-kernel slowdown against the fixup saving (fixup family 3.97% plus the 1.32% main kernel today), preferably choosing about 4-7 CTAs with 3-5 iterations each; (4) keep the condition limited to the J=16 single-tile fallback launch, ntiles_dst == 1, which in this model is only the 48-row ssm_alpha/beta (all other Q8_0 ne01 are multiples of 128). The falsifier and the target are otherwise sound.

outcome.refusal_reason: This diff is byte-identical to the patch the correctness gate has already refused twice ('MUL_MAT failed on ROCm0'). Both authoring retries abstained without changing it. Resubmitting it unchanged cannot give a different deterministic result, and it would spend another build plus the MUL_MAT suite for nothing. The mechanism itself looks sound in source. For ssm_alpha/beta (blocks_per_ne00 = 160, blocks_per_iter = 8) the 5-CTA grid gives ranges [0,32), [32,64), [64,96), [96,128) and [128,160). CTAs 0-3 take the fixup=true tail into tmp_fixup[0..3]. CTA 4 takes the full-tile while-loop and writes dst. In mul_mat_q_stream_k_fixup only CTA 4 survives the early-return checks; it walks bidx 3 down to 0 and adds the four partials to dst. When the cap is 1 (K <= 1024), fixup_needed = 1 % 1 = 0, and the single CTA writes dst directly. The kbc round-down at mmq.cuh:997-998 and :1162-1163 stays consistent for blocks_per_ne00 that are not multiples of 8. tmp_fixup and the fixup grid are sized from block_nums_stream_k.x. So either the failure comes from a case this trace does not cover, or it does not come from this hunk: the sibling akm-gfx90a-q8-tiny-streamk-cap failed the same way, so check that the anchor passes the same seeded MUL_MAT suite. To make progress, recover the failing test-backend-ops case (type, m, n, k, batch) from the gate receipt and confirm the anchor passes it. Then either change the patch to address that case, or show the refusal was a harness fault. Do not rebuild this same diff.

outcome.refusal_reason: The route's correctness gates can never run the proposed branch, so a defect in it would reach serving unseen. ggml_graph_plan reserves per-thread copies only when src1 has exactly one row (ggml-cpu.c:3439-3441). For any multi-row MUL_MAT it sizes wdata as one shared converted src1 plus CACHE_LINE_SIZE*n_threads, and params->wsize equals that planned size (ggml-cpu.c:3601-3609, ggml-cpu.cpp:181-188). The proposed eligibility test, wsize >= nth * (all converted rows), therefore fails in a single-op graph whenever the converted input is more than about 128 bytes. That covers every realistic shape at widths 2-8: K >= 256 Q8_0/Q4_K/Q5_K/F16 needs at least 544 B. The cpu_mul_mat_body gates (the native MUL_MAT suite, the scalar Q8_0/Q4_K/Q5_K/F16 fixture at widths 1-8, and the GDB entry hit on ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat) would all execute HEAD's shared path and pass however the new code is written. The branch would only switch on in serving graphs, where other nodes such as FLASH_ATTN_EXT scratch inflate wsize. This route has no model_identity gate and the serving A/B measures only tok/s, so a wrong slice offset or layout would be kept unseen. ggml_graph_plan is outside this route, so the patch cannot fix the sizing. To resubmit, make the branch independent of wsize slack, so the existing fixture runs it at widths 2-8 with K >= 256. One way: a bounded private buffer owned by the mul_mat body itself, with an explicit byte cap and HEAD as the fallback, plus a statement of which fixture cases take it. Alternatively, name the fixture cases that provably execute the branch. Also state which served nodes are eligible. With ggml_is_numa() false, nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1 holds at N=3 only when ceil(ne01/16) < 4*nth, i.e. ne01 <= 3056. Larger dense projections would keep the barrier. Price that against the cost of 48-fold redundant conversion, for example 48 x 120 KB F16 for hc_mixes. The rest of the hypothesis checks out against the source: the mechanism is in scope for the route, absent from HEAD, not yet measured in this epoch, and bit-exact as described. tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX partitions statically; float tinyBLAS::gemm initializes its own chunk counter and has its own barrier; from_float is block-local.

The N=1 split-KV path also calls _one_chunk with one head at a time (ops.cpp:10033-10036). An interleave confined to _one_chunk would never activate in serving. outcome.refusal_reason: The hypothesis targets a graph path the selected serving launch never builds. Even on the unfused path, the sinkhorn CONT reads `ggml_permute(comb, 1, 0, 2, 3)`, which is a non-contiguous src0. outcome.refusal_reason: The mechanism is source-consistent and fits the route. cpu_graph_sync admits a TOL fusion in ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops plus new static helpers. HEAD fuses only RMS_NORM->MUL (ggml-cpu.c:4327-4344). RMS_NORM is not tiny-solo (ggml-cpu.c:2743-2768), so the whole team reaches try_fuse_ops. build_hc_mixes emits RESHAPE, RMS_NORM, MUL_MAT consecutively. As written, though, the only gate that runs this pair could pass without ever executing the fused branch, and the A/B would then time HEAD. cpu_graph_sync has no entry witness (cpu_route_witness.py: op=None, breakpoint=None). No native case builds the pair. HEAD's unfused path sits at <1% of cpu_fusion_reference's bound, so a patch that never engages passes. Close three traps before authoring. (1) Eligibility. 'Output width small relative to the thread team' holds in serving (M=24, nth=48), but the fixture runs M=24 on 8 and 13 threads and M=7 on 6 threads (cpu_fusion_reference.py CASES). Any natural reading such as M < nth skips every case. State the exact predicate. It must depend only on graph metadata and nth, so every thread decides the same way. Name the cases that take it. Example: HEAD's float-tinyBLAS job count < nth. That count is 3 for M=24 and 1 for M=7, so the predicate holds for hc_mixes_nt1-3 (8 threads), odd_team_pos (13) and small_signed (6), and fails for single_thread_pos. (2) Matching. Do not copy the ggml_can_fuse idiom. ggml_can_fuse_ext requires ggml_are_same_shape(prev, node) (ggml-impl.h:690), and [K, nt] vs [24, nt] fails, so the copied idiom would never fuse. Use ggml_node_has_n_uses(cgraph, node_n, 1), which also rejects views and OUTPUT tensors. Also check: nodes[node_n+1] is MUL_MAT with src[1] == node and the COMPUTE flag; src0 is contiguous F16 in a plain CPU buffer, not an extra/repack buffer; ne12 == ne13 == 1; nt <= 8. (3) Scratch. ggml_graph_plan sizes this node's wdata as row_size(F16, K*nt) + 64*nth when nt >= 2 (ggml-cpu.c:3433-3445, 3607-3608). That is 123,392 B for the fixture's K=20480, nt=3, 8-thread case. Keeping HEAD's full F16 src1 in wdata and appending the nth*M*nt float partials (2,304 B) needs 125,184 B. The capacity check would then fail in the fixture's single-pair graph, so the fixture would run the fallback while serving (where FLASH_ATTN_EXT inflates wsize) runs the new code. This is the trap that rejected akm-ds41-small-batch-private-conversion. Name the layout, for example per-thread K-slice F16 conversion in a bounded local buffer with only the partials in wdata. Show the check passes for every engaging fixture case. Also say how each thread gets the row scale before F16 rounding. Option (a): per-thread partial sums of squares, combined in thread order after an in-op ggml_barrier. This is legal because neither node is solo. Option (b): every thread recomputes the full row. The measured serial chain is 10.7 us per [20480] row, so about 32 us per thread at nt=3; price that. Add one line on why K-slices avoid the overhead that sank the three settled plan variants: each thread reads about 20 KB of weights and only its slice of x, instead of the whole 123 KB F16 B per job. The TOL statement, the fixed-order combine and the falsifier are otherwise sound.

statement: Extend ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops under cpu_graph_sync to fuse a single-consumer RMS_NORM -> MUL_MAT pair when the input is contiguous F32, weights are contiguous F16, output width is small relative to the thread team, and token count is at most 8. The inspected build_hc_mixes emits this pair for hc_mixes; current fusion handles only RMS_NORM -> MUL. A new static helper partitions K across threads, computes normalized values locally, preserves the intermediate F32 scaling and F16 conversion, and combines partial dots in a fixed order using existing scratch with a capacity-checked fallback. This recovers idle threads in the served narrow-M projection and removes intermediate materialization and conversion dispatch. It is TOL, not bit-exact: split-K changes dot accumulation order. This targets work imbalance within dense MUL_MAT rather than repeating the rejected unreachable Sinkhorn solo-run change or the settled tile-plan variants. Sampled libgomp cycles motivate investigating imbalance but do not establish recoverable wall time.

outcome.refusal_reason: The stated predicate does not engage two of the fixture cases the hypothesis says it engages, and those are the only cases that test the partition serving uses. Checked against cpu_fusion_reference.py CASES and sgemm.cpp:494-532. (1) odd_team_pos is K=4100, nt=5, M=24 on 13 threads. 4100 % 16 = 4, so the 'K divisible by 16' clause sends it to HEAD. (2) small_signed is K=1024, nt=4, M=7 on 6 threads. 7 is divisible by neither 8 nor 4. HEAD's float tinyBLAS::matmul also returns false for it, so 'unsupported plans fall back' sends it to HEAD too. That leaves four engaging cases: hc_mixes_nt1/nt2/nt3_pos and nt3_signed. All four use K=20480, M=24 and an 8-thread team, so the 1280 sixteen-element slices split evenly, 160 per thread. Serving runs nth=48, where 1280/48 is not an integer and the slices split unevenly (26 or 27 per thread). The uneven split, the remainder bounds and the fixed-order combine across a non-power-of-two team are therefore never run by any gate. A dropped, doubled or misindexed tail slice would pass all four cases. The native suites have no case that builds this pair, the scalar quant suite never touches it, and cpu_graph_sync has no model_identity gate, so such a defect would reach serving unseen. That is a correctness risk the existing gates cannot resolve. To resubmit: (a) Drop or relax K % 16. For example, split into 16-element slices plus a final 4-aligned tail slice (the fixture guarantees K % 4 == 0), so K=4100 engages. On 13 threads that gives 257 slices, an uneven split like serving's. (b) Replace 'HEAD's tinyBLAS job count' with a metadata-only predicate defined for every M, e.g. M % 8 == 0 ? M/8 : (M % 4 == 0 ? M/4 : 1) jobs, compared with nth, or simply M <= some bound. small_signed (M=7, 6 threads) then engages, and single_thread_pos still falls back. (c) Recheck the workspace for the widened cases. odd_team_pos needs 13*5*8 + 13*24*5*4 = 6,760 B against its plan's row_size(F16, 4100*5) + 64*13 = 41,832 B. small_signed needs 864 B against 8,576 B. Both fit, so show that. (d) State the per-thread slice-range formula and say that the engaging cases include an uneven split. The rest is sound and can be reused: matching via ggml_node_has_n_uses(cgraph, node_n, 1) with src[1] == node, COMPUTE flag, contiguous plain-buffer F16, ne12 == ne13 == 1, nt <= 8; nth*nt double and nth*M*nt float partials in wdata with a 256-element local F16 buffer; the in-op barrier (legal because RMS_NORM is not solo); scaling in F32 before F16 rounding; fixed thread-order combines; the TOL declaration; the falsifier.

statement: Extend ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops with a TOL RMS_NORM -> F16 MUL_MAT split-K fusion for the inspected build_hc_mixes pair. The statement relies on DS41's shared-expert up and gate Q8_0 MUL_MATs being adjacent nodes that share src1. They are not adjacent. The anchor's node profile (node-profiles/run-60201abbc00ec384566cd531c75b89f2) shows exactly this order in every layer: 753 ffn_gate-4 q8_0 MUL_MAT, 754 ffn_gate_clamped-4 CLAMP, 755 ffn_up-4 q8_0 MUL_MAT, and likewise 887/888/889 for layer 5. 'No intervening bias or scale nodes' is true, but it misses this intervening CLAMP. The other Q8_0 MUL_MATs that share an input are also not adjacent: qr-N (772) and the wkv projection (781) both read norm-N, but an RMS_NORM, another MUL_MAT and a ROPE sit between them. Across the whole profiled verify graph, only 7 MUL_MAT nodes are directly followed by another MUL_MAT. Getting gate and up adjacent needs either a graph or builder edit in llama-graph.cpp or deepseek41.cpp, which no route admits, or out-of-order execution of up ahead of CLAMP(gate). Out-of-order execution is a scheduling change: it needs the cpu_graph_sched route, its use_ref fallback and its model_identity race gate, and none of these appear in the hypothesis. (1) ggml_clamp is always a view of its input (ggml.c:4532, `result = ggml_view_tensor(ctx, a)`). (1) Reachability/build: dispatch at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:2833/2837 still instantiates mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T only with DequantizerQ4K_AVX2/DequantizerQ5K_AVX2, so the new #ifdef HAVE_FANCY_SIMD block (active in this build: iqk_config.h:58-60 defines HAVE_FANCY_SIMD under -march=native AVX-512, confirmed by zmm vpdpbusd in the anchor DSO) calls deq.prepare64(i,0)/(i,1) at lines 892/896 on dequantizers with no prepare64 member; the new DequantizerQ4K_X4T/Q5K_X4T are never instantiated, and their prepare64(int) (795/824) has the wrong arity for those calls regardless. The new code also uses intrinsics GCC does not provide: _mm512_set_m128 (888/890/904), _mm512_extractf128_ps (889), _mm512_inserti128_si512 (878/882) - verified absent from gcc-13/14/15 avx512fintrin.h (only _mm512_inserti32x4 / _mm512_extractf32x4_ps exist; existing file idiom uses _mm512_inserti32x8). (2) Correctness: line 901's (const __m512i*)y.qs+64 is byte offset 4096 inside a 144-byte block_q8_2_x4 (qs is int8_t[128], ggml-common.h:280-283), an out-of-bounds read far past the row; the second 64 bytes are y.qs+64 bytes. Even with that fixed, values[0]/values[1] = low/high nibbles of qs bytes 0..63 are paired against y.qs[0..63]/[64..127] without the permute1/permute2 reorder the Q8_2_X4 interleave requires (AVX2 sibling pairs y chunk k with values[k]: low(0..31)/high(0..31)/low(32..63)/high(32..63)), so weights and activations are mispaired. The epilogue at 912-915 double-counts the low half: sum256 already includes acc256, then hsum_float_8(acc256+sum256) yields 2*sum(low)+sum(high) instead of the full 16-lane sum - not bit-identical to the AVX2 path. DequantizerQ4K_X4T also never loads qs[64..127] (only prepare64), so half the weights would be dropped. (3) Scope: the claimed Q4_K/Q5_K 512-bit selection is false without editing the selector at :2833/:2837, which the admitted route explicitly refuses.

statement: The hot Q4_K dot kernel mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:795; profiled specialization <DequantizerQ4K_AVX2,1> = 19.43% of sampled user cycles, Q4_K total ~25.35%, the largest addressable kernel) is hardwired to 256-bit: per 128-element weight sub-block it issues 2x32B loads + 4 and + 2 srli unpack, then per activation row 4x32B y loads + 4x _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 + 5 int adds (lines 838-865). The same file already contains a 512-bit sibling for the identical Q4_K/Q5_K dequantizer family against the Q8_K y-format (mul_mat_qX_K_q8_K_AVX512, lines 380-421, with zmm Q4Bits prepare64 + permute1/2 shuffles at lines 307-331), but no 512-bit variant exists for the Q8_2_X4 y-format that dispatch actually selects for Q4_K/Q5_K. Mechanism: add a #ifdef HAVE_FANCY_SIMD 512-bit inner loop to the Q4_K/Q5_K-only template body plus Q4_K/Q5_K-specific zmm nibble dequantizers (new structs mirroring the file's existing zmm Q4Bits idiom; the shared Q4Bits_AVX2 at line 754, also used by Q6_K, is untouched): per sub-block 1x64B weight load + 2 mask/shift unpacks, 2x64B y loads, 2x _mm512_dpbusd_epi32, 4-add reduction, with the existing float scale/min epilogue (d8 + scales[2] fmadd, lines 821-836/862-864) byte-for-byte unchanged. This halves unpack+dpbusd instructions and load instructions per weight byte on this AVX-512 Zen 4/5 host (avx512f/vl/bw/dq/vnni present in /proc/cpuinfo; GGML_NATIVE=ON -> HAVE_FANCY_SIMD defined). Integer dots are exact in int32 regardless of lane grouping (same 16-element partition, |sum| << 2^31) and the float epilogue is unchanged, so outputs are bit-identical; the dense path streams at 176 GB/s = 83% of the 220 GB/s host read ceiling, so the ~17% residual gap on that path is the recoverable headroom if the ny=1 256-bit inner loop is load-port/issue-bound.

statement: Answers the rejection: the verify batch is N=3, which is exactly why this hypothesis targets gemm4xN<3> — the N=3 kernel itself (23.93% of sampled periods; dense MUL_MAT ≈ 40% of decode cycle, operator correction-2's largest kernel lever) — instead of the sync path. Anchor disassembly (libggml-cpu.so.0 0x23d950, gemm4xN<3>) shows ~111 instructions per block: ~25 are per-block shared overhead — 4 d-word loads + shift/or + vcvtph2ps, 3 fp16-table B-delta lookups + vperm2f128, loop add/cmp/jne, and one spilled accumulator (vfmadd213ps + vmovaps at [rsp-0x20]) — and only 4 A-block loads (136 B) are in flight per iteration (B loads are already CSE'd). outcome.refusal_reason: The patch is live, incorrect and reads out of bounds — not a shippable variant of the accepted 512-bit inner loop. (1) OOB/wrong load: iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:849 does `_mm512_loadu_si512((const __m512i*)y.qs + 8)` = byte offset 512 from `qs` (int8_t[128]; block_q8_2_x4 is 16+128 = 144 B, ggml-common.h:280-284). The upper half is `y.qs + 1` (bytes 64..127), so this reads 384 B past the block/row end (UB for the last block of a row) and consumes unrelated memory as chunk 3. (2) The reduction is mathematically wrong, so outputs are not even close, let alone bit-identical. The AVX2 base reduction (the lines this diff deletes) yields per 128-bit lane [p0.even, p1.even, p2.even, p3.even | p0.odd, p1.odd, p2.odd, p3.odd], where each pm is the 8 dpbusd dwords of chunk m and even/odd = dwords {0,2,4,6}/{1,3,5,7}; the unchanged epilogue (lines 868-870) multiplies that by d4d8 = [s0*dy0, s1*dy1, s2*dy2, s3*dy3] duplicated, so each lane holds exactly one chunk's 16-byte half under that chunk's own weight and activation scale. The new code destroys that alignment before scaling: eA[m]=pA[m]+pA[m+8]=p0_dm+p1_dm, aA=eA+rotate4(eA)=p0_dm+p1_dm+p0_d[m+4]+p1_d[m+4], then emits [aA0,aA1,aB0,aB1,aA2,aA3,aB2,aB3] — every output lane sums two different chunks at two different byte groups and is then multiplied by a single per-lane scale. Numeric counterexample: p0=[1..8], p1=[10..80], p2=[100..800], p3=[1..8] gives candidate total 176*S0+220*S1+1616*S2+2020*S3 versus correct 36*S0+360*S1+3600*S2+36*S3; with the 4 Q4_K scales generally distinct this is wrong output (consistent with the recorded 79/130 op-test ERR=1.0), so the correctness-risk gate applies. (3) The stated mechanism is also not implemented: no Q4_K/Q5_K-private zmm nibble dequantizers/structs are added (the accepted statement's `prepare64`+permute idiom), the AVX2 Q4Bits_AVX2 256-bit unpack is merely reinterpreted via inserti32x8, and the claimed unpack-instruction halving never happens. The broken branch is the one compiled and selected in this build: HAVE_FANCY_SIMD is set from __AVX512F__/VNNI/VL/BW/DQ (iqk_config.h:54-60) on this host, and dispatch instantiates mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T<DequantizerQ4K_AVX2|Q5K_AVX2> at 2719/2723. Scope itself is fine (edits stay in the Q4_K/Q5_K template body), so this is a correctness rejection, not a boundary refusal.

outcome.refusal_reason: Rejected: the new 512-bit inner loop is numerically wrong, so it is not a bit-identical implementation of the accepted mechanism. (1) Mispaired dot product. get q4_K mapping from dequantize_row_q4_K (ggml-quants.c:1541-1548): elements 0-31 = low nibbles of qs[0..31], 32-63 = high nibbles of qs[0..31], 64-95 = low nibbles of qs[32..63], 96-127 = high nibbles of qs[32..63]. block_q8_2_x4 stores four consecutive 32-element activation blocks (y4[i4].qs + 32*ir, iqk_quantize.cpp:912-913), i.e. y.qs[0..63] = sub-blocks 0 then 1. Q4BitsZ_AVX2 values[0] = low nibbles of qs[0..63] = weight sub-blocks 0 then 2, so p0 bytes 32..63 multiply sub-block 2 weights by sub-block 1 activations; p1 bytes 0..31 multiply sub-block 1 weights by sub-block 2 activations. Only sub-blocks 0 and 3 happen to align. (2) Broken scale alignment. p0+alignr_epi32(p0,8) (and the same for p1) adds dwords belonging to different sub-blocks into one 32-bit lane, and the unchanged epilogue then multiplies that lane by one sub-block scale (d4d8 = [s0*dy0,s1*dy1,s2*dy2,s3*dy3], lines 896-898). The 256-bit dpbusd path this replaces guarantees each 128-bit lane slot m carries only chunk-m partials; here each lane sums up to four sub-blocks under one arbitrary scale, so outputs differ from the AVX2 path even before the pairing error. (3) Q5_K hbits. prepare_z does values[0] |= ((h512<<4)|(h512<<2)) & 0x10 and values[1] |= ((h512<<3)|(h512<<1)) & 0x10 on a register whose two 256-bit halves are the same qh bytes; both halves therefore get bit0-OR-bit2 and bit1-OR-bit3 of every qh byte, whereas scalar/AVX2 use bit0 for the low-nibble sub-block and bit2 for the following one (ggml-quants.c:1750-1753, x[i].qh bit s per sub-block s; apply_hbits at iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:801-804), so the 5th bit is corrupted unless the two hbits coincide. This is the same class of defect that already produced the recorded 79/130 ERR=1.0 op-test failure for this mechanism.

Mechanism: add 4 __builtin_prefetch calls inside the gemm4xN k-loop, one per A weight row (ii..ii+3), 8 blocks (l+8, guarded l+8<k) ahead, locality 1 — the same idiom the sibling f32 tinyBLAS class already uses at sgemm.cpp:3103-3107 (distance 1). This raises per-core in-flight weight bytes from ~136 B (one block-set) to ~1.4 KB, roughly 8x the Little's-law requirement (target BW x latency ~= 176 B/core), so blocks are fetched well before use. outcome.refusal_reason: It does not implement the stated mechanism in its cross-row branch. deq.bx is the byte row stride (BaseDequantizer::bx, iqk_common.h:393-394; new_row is (const char*)vx + bx*ix, iqk_common.h:389), so (const char*)deq.x + deq.bx correctly reaches the next row, but the added `i + 8 - nb` is a block count added as bytes: for the wrap iterations (i = nb-8 .. nb-1) the target is next_row + (i+8-nb) bytes, i.e. always the same first ~192 bytes of the next row, not the block 8 ahead that the statement writes as deq.x + nb + (i+8-nb) (the linear continuation). At the serving shape (n=5120 -> nb=20, 2880-byte Q4_K rows) the else branch runs for 8 of every 20 block iterations, so blocks 2..7 of every row are never prefetched and the eight wrap iterations redundantly re-touch the same 3 lines; the promised uniform 8-block lookahead is not what this diff implements. The hunk is otherwise in-scope (Q4_K/Q5_K-only template body, single file, no selector/dequantizer edits) and prefetch-only, so there is no numeric risk, but the cross-row address must be corrected to (const char*)(deq.x + nb) + (i + 8 - nb)*sizeof(*deq.x) (equivalently deq.bx + (i+8-nb)*sizeof(*deq.x)) before build/measurement, otherwise the measured effect belongs to a different prefetch geometry than the accepted statement.

statement: In the Q4_K/Q5_K-only template body of mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:795-876, the kernel carrying 28.7% of sampled user cycles and 40.5% of decode wall as MUL_MAT_ID), add at the top of the per-256-element-block loop (line 814) a 3-line read prefetch (three __builtin_prefetch at byte offsets 0/64/128 of the 144/160-byte block, T0) of the weight block this thread consumes 8 blocks later: deq.x[i+8] when i+8 < nb, else deq.x + nb + (i+8-nb) when ix+1 < nrc_x. The cross-row target is valid because every caller hands the template a contiguous same-expert row range with row stride exactly nb blocks (new_row: x = vx + bx*ix, iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:3159; iqk_mul_mat_moe_rows and iqk_mul_mat_moe both pass contiguous slabs, iqk_mul_mat.cpp:863,910; the slab partition spans at most two experts per thread via separate calls, iqk_dispatch.cpp:503-525). Mechanism: the expert weight row is the DRAM-streaming operand — each thread streams a contiguous run of ~570-700 rows x 2880 B (~1.6-2 MB) per call — and today it is fetched demand-only, so per-thread memory-level parallelism is capped by the outstanding-miss queue at ~100-150 ns DRAM latency; an 8-block (~1.1 KB, ~18 lines) lookahead issued while the current block's dpbusd work executes overlaps fetch latency with compute. This is the same pattern the already-kept akm-ds41-dense-q8-tb-prefetch (champion c0ef39613, sgemm.cpp:1540, +3.440% on the full target) applies to the dense Q8 sibling kernel. The activation stream (q8.y) is deliberately not prefetched: it is small and reused across all rows, so it is L1/L2-resident. Prefetches change only cache state, not arithmetic: outputs are bit-identical to HEAD. Edit is confined to this one template body; no dequantizer, selector, header or other-file changes.

Math error: the edit is not bit-exact as claimed. In this tree `updot(u,s)` (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp:1814-1824) lowers to `_mm256_dpbusd_epi32` / `_mm256_maddubs_epi16`, where the FIRST operand is unsigned bytes and the second signed. HEAD's `_mm256_sign_epi8(avec_i, avec_i)` (= |a|) exists precisely to supply that non-negative unsigned operand, with `_mm256_sign_epi8(load(B...), avec_i)` = b*sign(a), so |a|*b*sign(a)=a*b. `load()` for q8_0 returns raw signed int8 qs (sgemm.cpp:1744-1746; q4_0 is (qs&15)-8 at :1756-1758), so passing raw `avec_i` as the unsigned half computes (a mod 256)*b, differing from a*b by 256*b on every negative byte. There is no signed x signed byte dpbusd here (AVX512-VNNI/AVX-VNNI are unsigned x signed), so the mechanism as stated changes MUL_MAT numerics; only the offset trick (A^0x80 plus a compensating -128*sum(b) lane seed; inbox note 41 item 2) is integer-exact, and that is a different mechanism with its own pre-pass. The 'outputs are bit-identical, no tolerance to spend' premise is false, and falsifier check (1) (zero vpsignb) can be satisfied while the loop is numerically wrong. Revise to the offset-trick form before authoring.

Mechanically: for every instantiation (block_q4_0/q5_0/q8_0), load() already returns signed int8 weights (Q4_0: (qs&15)-8 in [-8,7]; Q5_0: denibble|bittobyte in [-16,15]; Q8_0: raw int8), so the sign dance computes the exact integer sum |a_i|*(b_i*sign(a_i)) = a_i*b_i per byte, which is byte-identical to what a plain signed dpbusd(avec_i, bvec) computes (4 products per int32 lane, |a_i*b_i|<=127^2, no overflow in either form). The dpbusd int32 lanes are therefore identical, cvtepi32_ps and every downstream FMA are untouched, and outputs are bit-identical to HEAD for all shapes — no tolerance to spend. Why faster: objdump of the anchor-gen-004 DSO shows the gemm4xN<3> hot loop (24 vpdpbusd per k-block per 4x3 tile) carries 32 vpsignb (8 CSE'd A-signs + 24 B-signs that GCC cannot CSE because each depends on avec_i) — ~19% of the loop's ~170-instruction vector stream — plus the ymm/zmm pressure of keeping four per-i B-sign vectors live. gemm4xN<3> is 19.99% of sampled user cycles and dense MUL_MAT is 40.89% of cycle wall; per the operator's corrected ceiling analysis this kernel runs at ~254 GB/s on compute against a ~400 GB/s read ceiling, i.e. it is NOT DRAM-saturated, so a ~19% cut in the hot loop's vector instructions on this kernel is the single cheapest bit-exact instruction-stream reduction available in the largest patchable family (the spill-fix rung of the gemm ladder is already dead: the same disassembly shows zero zmm->stack stores).

statement: In class tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX, body of gemm4xN (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp:1524-1634, the type-generic template whose <3> and <2> specializations are the hot dense-Q8_0 verify GEMM, 19.99% + 3.86% of sampled user cycles), replace the sign-operand VPSIGNB pair at every updot call site (sgemm.cpp:1556-1569, 1583-1596, 1612-1625) with the integer-exact offset form, inlining the dpbusd in the gemm4xN body (updot itself, sgemm.cpp:1814, is not edited): (1) the A operand becomes load(A)^0x80 (= a+128 as unsigned), computed once per A block row and reused across all j; (2) the B operand is the raw load(B) (sgemm.cpp:1744-1746 returns raw signed q8_0 qs), no sign; (3) the per-(j,l-block) int32 accumulator is seeded with S = -128 * lane_sums(B_qs), where lane_sums is one _mm256_dpbusd_epi32(ones, B_qs) (unsigned-ones x signed gives the per-8-byte-lane byte sum) times -128, instead of zero. The three added #else blocks (sgemm.cpp:1584-1601, 1644-1661, 1706-1723) feed the offset operand into HEAD's sign trick: updot(sign(a^0x80,a^0x80), sign(b,a^0x80)) with updot = madd(1, maddubs(u,s)) (sgemm.cpp:1911-1921). outcome.refusal_reason: risks correctness: the wait at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:625-635 is a lost-wakeup race, not a barrier. A thread stores its own generation, then spins on every other slot until it reads `== gen`. But nothing gates departers: once thread j has seen all slots at gen it legitimately passes and runs the next node, and if it reaches the next barrier before a slower poller i has finished scanning, j overwrites its slot with gen+1. Since a slot only advances, i can never again read gen on slot j and spins forever - one blocked thread then stalls every subsequent barrier of the team (hang, not a wrong number). The window is real here: i must scan 47 cross-NUMA lines (~5-15 us) while a short node completes (~2-10 us), so the scheme is not merely at risk, it cannot be made correct by any ordering argument as written; the accepted mechanism needs a monotone/sense condition (e.g. (int32_t)(load - gen) < 0) or a release phase where departers wait until all arrivals are observed, and the diff has neither. Secondary, the diff also does not implement the declared mechanism: `__attribute__((aligned(64)))` on the array (ggml-cpu.c:620) leaves the 64 uint32 slots at 4-byte stride, so 16 threads share each line and the claimed 'n cache-line-aligned slots / no cross-node bounce' is false, and the state is not keyed by (threadpool, n_threads) - it is a process-global static indexed by omp team id, so a second team/threadpool (or any team whose membership/team size changes, which ggml-cpu.c:4884 permits by resetting n_threads from omp_get_num_threads()) desynchronizes the per-thread generation counters and deadlocks every thread.

statement: In the OpenMP build, ggml_barrier (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:599-613) lowers to `#pragma omp barrier`. libgomp's barrier serializes all 48 arrivals on ONE atomic counter cache line (48 dependent RMWs per barrier) and releases via one flag line; with OMP_PROC_BIND=spread across the 4 NPS4 nodes that line bounces cross-node on every barrier. The champion pays ~5355 such barriers per 101 ms verify cycle (operator note 40: ~3.1 us/barrier ~= 16 ms/cycle; node-profile wall-compute gap 21.4 ms/cycle; perf profile: libgomp 34.21% of sampled user cycles). Mechanism: inside the ggml_barrier body only (OpenMP branch), replace the `#pragma omp barrier` with a per-thread arrival-flag barrier: n cache-line-aligned uint32 slots in a function-local static keyed by (threadpool, n_threads), falling back to `#pragma omp barrier` if state is unavailable or n>64; each thread release-stores its own monotonically increasing generation (static __thread counter) into its own slot, then acquire-polls the n slots until every slot shows its generation. Arrivals become n parallel stores to n distinct lines (no serialized RMW, no cross-node bounce) and release is n-1 shared acquire loads (each slot line written once per barrier). Bit-exact: no arithmetic is touched. Ordering argument: every thread's node-k writes are sequenced-before its release store to its slot; any thread's acquire load of its generation from slot u synchronizes-with u's release store, so before any thread starts node k+1 it sees all threads' node-k writes - the same release/acquire contract the current full-fence `#pragma omp barrier` provides; all threads run the identical node loop, hence the identical barrier sequence, so generations stay in lockstep. Why faster: removes the serialized-arrival cost (~1-2 us of the measured ~3.1 us/barrier at 48 spread threads) x 5355 barriers ~= 4-9 ms of the 101 ms cycle (4-9%); the pessimistic split (only release latency saved, ~0.4 us/barrier) is ~2 ms (~2%). This is distinct from the idle-spin/wait-policy and thread-count knobs retired on 2026-09-23 under the 220 GB/s premise that operator note 40 (2026-09-26) explicitly contradicted and re-priced the per-node sync floor as the second lever; the cpu_graph_sync route admitting ggml_barrier was granted the same day.

outcome.refusal_reason: Does not implement the accepted per-thread-generation barrier, and it can hang. (1) The accepted mechanism stores each thread's own monotone generation (equal across the lockstep team); this diff instead derives gen from a shared arrival counter (atomic_fetch_add(&bar->seq,1)+1 at ggml-cpu.c:650), so every thread stores a distinct generation at each barrier. With distinct generations, polling until every slot >= my gen is satisfiable within the barrier only for the earliest arrival (all other slots hold this round's smaller gens); every other thread i can pass barrier k only after the i-1 earlier arrivals have reached barrier k+1, i.e. finished the following node. The release is therefore staggered, every node's work is serialized in arrival order behind the next barrier, and the statement's identical-generation lockstep ordering argument is false for this code, so the claimed parallel release cannot occur. (2) The re-base (ggml-cpu.c:642-649) is executed independently by every thread when bar->n != nth with relaxed stores and no once-guard, so on the first barrier of a pool (or any cgml n_threads change) many threads reset concurrently: a late reset can wipe a slot whose generation was already published and rewind seq (e.g. C stored gen 5, A wipes it and stores gen 1); A then waits for C's slot >= 1 and C waits for A's slot >= 5, each on the other's next store - a mutual-wait hang - and a wiped arrival can also release a thread before all arrivals, breaking the ordering contract. Fix: use the declared per-thread generation (or a single shared round value read once per barrier) and initialize the per-threadpool state once (leader/CAS) before any poll.

statement: In the OpenMP build, ggml_barrier (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:599-613) lowers to `#pragma omp barrier`. libgomp's barrier serializes all 48 arrivals on ONE atomic counter cache line (48 dependent RMWs per barrier) and releases via one flag line; with OMP_PROC_BIND=spread across the 4 NPS4 nodes that line bounces cross-node on every barrier. The champion pays ~5355 such barriers per 101 ms verify cycle (operator note 40: ~3.1 us/barrier ~= 16 ms/cycle; node-profile wall-compute gap 21.4 ms/cycle; perf profile: libgomp 34.21% of sampled user cycles). Mechanism: inside the ggml_barrier body only (OpenMP branch), replace the `#pragma omp barrier` with a per-thread arrival-flag barrier: n cache-line-aligned uint32 slots in a function-local static keyed by (threadpool, n_threads), falling back to `#pragma omp barrier` if state is unavailable or n>64; each thread release-stores its own monotonically increasing generation (static __thread counter) into its own slot, then acquire-polls the n slots until every slot shows its generation. Arrivals become n parallel stores to n distinct lines (no serialized RMW, no cross-node bounce) and release is n-1 shared acquire loads (each slot line written once per barrier). Bit-exact: no arithmetic is touched. Ordering argument: every thread's node-k writes are sequenced-before its release store to its slot; any thread's acquire load of its generation from slot u synchronizes-with u's release store, so before any thread starts node k+1 it sees all threads' node-k writes - the same release/acquire contract the current full-fence `#pragma omp barrier` provides; all threads run the identical node loop, hence the identical barrier sequence, so generations stay in lockstep. Why faster: removes the serialized-arrival cost (~1-2 us of the measured ~3.1 us/barrier at 48 spread threads) x 5355 barriers ~= 4-9 ms of the 101 ms cycle (4-9%); the pessimistic split (only release latency saved, ~0.4 us/barrier) is ~2 ms (~2%). This is distinct from the idle-spin/wait-policy and thread-count knobs retired on 2026-09-23 under the 220 GB/s premise that operator note 40 (2026-09-26) explicitly contradicted and re-priced the per-node sync floor as the second lever; the cpu_graph_sync route admitting ggml_barrier was granted the same day.

outcome.refusal_reason: Risks correctness: the lazy init can hang the team's first barrier. A peer that loads init_state while the CAS winner is still zeroing the 64 slots reads 1, and because the outer test is `if (init == 0)` (ggml-cpu.c:631-646) it skips both the CAS and the wait-for-2 path, then release-stores its arrival into its own slot while the winner's relaxed zeroing loop may still be writing that slot. Nothing orders the winner's zeroing after the CAS (B's acquire load of 1 synchronizes only with the CAS store, not with the later loop), so the wipe is possible; the owner then spins forever on `(int32_t)(slot - s) < 0` and every peer waiting on that slot stalls with it - the same lost-arrival failure class as the previous two rounds, now on the first barrier of every process rather than in a re-base. Fix: wait whenever init_state != 2 (only the CAS winner may skip), or drop the lazy init outright - the statics are already zero-initialized at load, and the once-only zeroing loop buys nothing. Secondary, the diff still does not implement the declared state: the accepted mechanism keys the slots by (threadpool, n_threads) and falls back when state is unavailable, but this is one process-global array indexed by omp_get_thread_num() with per-OS-thread __thread generations, so any second team whose membership or size differs (llama-server attaches separate threadpool and threadpool_batch, src/llama-context.cpp:1108-1114; the n_threads==1 path at ggml-cpu.c:4929-4931 bypasses the team entirely) leaves some threads' gen counters ahead of others, and the sense test then either releases a thread before all arrivals or stalls it permanently. The sense-reversing condition, the per-thread generation and the struct-level 64-byte padding are the requested fixes and are correct; the init protocol is not.

statement: In ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat_id's multi-row branch (ids->ne[1] >= 2, i.e. the N=3 serving verify; the single-token mmid_batch1 slab is gated on ids->ne[1]==1 and never runs there), the used experts are dispatched as one iqk_mul_mat_moe(..., Ny=cne1, ith, nth) call per expert, so every thread re-runs MulMat::prepare and re-partitions each expert 1/nth into a thin ~ne01/nth row stripe, ~n_groups times per op. When every used expert is routed exactly one activation row (cne1==1, the common verify case: 3 tokens rarely collide on one expert; groups with cne1>1 keep the existing call), apply the flat (expert,row) slab partition that the single-token path already uses: build group starts over the already-built matrix_rows map, set units_total = (ne01/slab_gran)*n_groups, hand thread ith the contiguous unit range [units_total*ith/nth, units_total*(ith+1)/nth) and dispatch each segment via iqk_mul_mat_moe_rows(..., Ny=1, ...). Each thread then streams one long contiguous run of one expert's weight rows (crossing at most two adjacent expert slabs) and pays prepare/tile setup O(1) instead of once per expert, removing the per-expert 1/nth stripe overhead that the B3-k keep already measured and removed for the single-token path. Bit-identical: with cne1==1 the kernel is Ny=1 funcs[0] before and after (is_dequant_better(Q4_K,1)==Q4_K), DataInfo/row_mapping are built identically, each output row accumulates over the same blocks in the same order independent of the computing thread or 64-row tile boundary, and dst rows stay disjoint per (id, token).

Mechanism: the 2x-unroll keep (+4.535% serving) and the two prefetch keeps (+3.440% dense, +5.683%+1.074% Q4_K) show both dominant GEMMs on this anchor are latency-coverage-limited, not instruction-limited; the dense Q8_0 path streams at 213 GB/s aggregate (52% of the measured 410 GB/s full-screen ceiling) while the expert path on the same host/interleave reaches 335-385 GB/s (82-94%). 4x unrolling doubles the A loads in flight per j-iteration (8 to 16 ymm loads, 256B to 512B) before the first dpbusd use, roughly doubling in-flight bytes beyond the existing 8-block-ahead prefetch, which should push dense streaming toward the expert-path efficiency; at the expert-path rate the 8.7 GB/cycle dense bytes drop from 40.9 ms to ~23-26 ms, i.e. 13-18% of the ~101 ms cycle, and even half that clears the floor. Bit-exactness: each Cv[j][i] still receives its madds in strictly ascending l order with the identical integer dot/seed/cvt arguments, so per-element FP operation order is unchanged and the output is bit-identical to HEAD (no tolerance spent); the tile partition, prefetch distance (kept at l+8) and epilogue are untouched. Register-pressure risk is real (the anchor-gen-005 disassembly of gemm4xN<3> shows the allocator already needed a stack slot pre-unroll), so the candidate DSO disassembly is part of the gate, not an afterthought.

statement: In the admitted iqk_dense_dispatch route, make iqk_q8_0_enabled() a compile-time true instead of an env probe, so DS41's dense Q8_0 MUL_MAT nodes are handled by ik's 512-bit Q8_0 kernel instead of tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX<block_q8_0,block_q8_0,float>::gemm4xN<2|3>. Evidence: the sampled CPU profile puts gemm4xN<3> at 17.83% and gemm4xN<2> at 3.00% of user cycles, and the node-profile sibling shows the dense-MUL_MAT complex at 40.61% wall but only ~213 GB/s wall / ~254 GB/s compute versus the Q4_K MoE path's 335-385 GB/s against the same ~410 GB/s ceiling; that gap is instruction-width bound (256-bit _mm256_dpbusd_epi32), not a byte bound, so a 512-bit kernel that does twice the MACs per instruction is the mechanism. Price it: the activations then quantize to Q8_2_X4, so outputs are NOT bit-identical to tinyBLAS (routing Q8_0 into iqk changes the activation quantization type) and the route's scalar Q8_0 widths-1-8 reference plus the dense ACTIVE marker are the wiring proof, not a bit-identity proof.

outcome.refusal_reason: The loop already rejected this exact diff at post-build verification: route entry was hit, but the sole selected case/reference did not pass, so the Q8_0 reroute has no passing independent agreement and is a fast-but-unproven candidate that must be discarded. The edit is in-scope (inside iqk_q8_0_enabled, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_dispatch.cpp:58-60, declared path, no other file), but it knowingly reroutes dense Q8_0 through Q8_2_X4 activations, which is not bit-identical to tinyBLAS and is the known-dangerous activation-quant-type class whose failure mode the op gate cannot see; the offered GDB-entry/dense-ACTIVE wiring markers cannot substitute for the failed scalar Q8_0 widths-1-8 reference. The unconditional flip also changes Q8_0 eligibility in the MUL_MAT_ID hook (:390) as well as the dense hook (:235), which the dense-only mechanism statement did not analyze.

statement: Flip the default of iqk_q8_0_enabled() from OFF to ON in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_dispatch.cpp (line 61: 'return s && atoi(s) != 0;' -> 'return s == nullptr || atoi(s) != 0;', the same default-ON pattern as the adjacent iqk_mmid_slab_enabled), keeping the GGML_IQK_Q8_0=0 opt-out. This clears the Q8_0 early-returns at the dense gate (line 239) and MoE gate (line 394) of ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat, so dense Q8_0 MUL_MAT (the non-MoE GEMMs of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q4) routes to the already-compiled AVX-512 VNNI iqk kernels mul_mat_qX_1_q8_2_T<Q8_0_1_Unpacker, nq> (nq=1..8) instead of the llamafile tinyBLAS gemm4xN path. Mechanism: the iqk kernel reads Q8_0 weights via the +127 unsigned offset (dpbusd VNNI) against dual-scale block_q8_2 activations (bf16 scale + int16 sub-scale + 32 int8, 36 B/32, quantized by quantize_row_q8_2_x4) - a different GEMM design than current tinyBLAS. Why it should win: dense Q8_0 GEMM is the largest untried patchable GEMM family (~21% sampled / ~40% wall in the anchor profile); the kernel is confirmed compiled and present in the anchor DSO (all nq 1-8 specializations, mul_mat_qX_1_q8_2_T<Q8_0_1_Unpacker,1..8>); the architect-bench prior on a Q8_0 model is +58% (stale, directional only). The whole iqk path is already engaged in the serving runtime (the Q4_K iqk keeps are live in the champion, so GGML_IQK is set); only the Q8_0 sub-gate blocks Q8_0. Numerics are NOT bit-identical to the current path: the activation quantizer changes from single-scale block_q8_0 (float d) to dual-scale block_q8_2 (bf16 d + int16 s), and the weight side uses the +127 offset with a different accumulation order - same 8-bit precision class, so correctness must be priced via a scalar Q8_0 fixture with analytic tolerance plus the serving A/B. Fallback if the integrity scanner re-flags the env line (as it did for akm-ds41-dense-q8-iqk): instead delete the Q8_0 clause at lines 239/394 (no env probe in the diff; loses the GGML_IQK_Q8_0 opt-out).

outcome.refusal_reason: The narrow-M branch is inside tinyBLAS::matmul and in route (only calls mnpack, no forbidden tokens), and for the DS41 target shape it works (m=24, n=3, nth=48 -> sn=2, xblock split -> gemm<1,2,1>, 48 jobs). But the plan it passes is geometrically invalid for a reachable set of shapes, so it risks correctness. The branch passes SIZE_N = sn<6?sn:6 with sn=ceil(n/nbloc) (sgemm.cpp:504-514 and :539-549), while gemm's x-block mapping is only valid when n >= ceil(n/RN)*(RN-1) - the invariant the HEAD value BLOCK_SIZE<RN>(n) guarantees. gemm computes jj_RN = xtiles - (xtiles*RN - n) (sgemm.cpp:624-625) and uses BLOC_POS(jr0, jj_RN, RN) as the first column (:648); with the 6-cap, jj_RN goes negative for n in {7,8,9,13,14,19}. Concrete reachable case: the route's own reference cohort - 40 rows on an 8-thread team, widths 1-8 - at n=8: m%4==0, rows=8, xt=ceil(8/BLOCK_SIZE<6>(8))=2<12 so njobs=5<8 -> trigger; nbloc=1, sn=8 -> SIZE_N=6; then xtiles=2, jj_RN=-2, jj0=-2, jj2=3, jj1=-12, so the only column loop executes gemm_bloc<1,5>(ii,-2), which loads B at negative row offsets and writes C[ldc*(-2+j)+ii] for j=0,1: out-of-bounds read and write before both buffers. The ith==0 assert at sgemm.cpp:634 checks only the BN mapping and does not catch it. n=7 and n=9 behave identically (jj_RN=-3,-1), as do n=13,14,19 when nbloc=1, and the branch fires for every float GEMM with m%4==0 and m/rows < nth, i.e. exactly the narrow-M regime this route targets. The VECTOR_REGISTERS==16 hunk is safe (RN<=3 always satisfies the invariant), but the __AVX512F__ hunk (sgemm.cpp:66-70, the DS41 path where the profiled tinyBLAS<16,...,unsigned short,unsigned short,float> runs) is not. Fix: keep RM=1/BM=1 and the BN split for the job count, but derive SIZE_N with the existing balanced BLOCK_SIZE<6>(n) (or clamp to the largest RN with n >= ceil(n/RN)*(RN-1), or assert jj_RN>=0 before returning); for hc_mixes that still gives 24 jobs (RN=3, xtiles=1) and the safe 48-job variant (nbloc=2, sn=2, RN=2) remains available. Re-author with that bound.

statement: In the float `class tinyBLAS` `matmul` body, change only the tile plan so that a narrow-M GEMM with fewer y-tiles than threads is re-planned to roughly one job per thread. DS41's `hc_mixes` (F16 hc_fn [20480,24] x F32 rms_norm output, nt=2-3, 80 nodes/verify graph) currently selects `mnpack<4,6,2>`-class blocking and yields m/(RM*BM)=24/8=3 jobs, so threads 0-2 each stream ~320 KB of A plus all of B while threads 3-47 go straight to the in-gemm barriers; the kernel is not slow per active thread (its per-thread rate matches the 48-thread-contended node_513 rate), it is purely under-parallelised (45/48 idle). Re-planning to a finer mnpack/SIZE_N/BN (e.g. SIZE_N=2, BN=1 -> 24 rows x 2 x-blocks = 48 jobs) spreads the same 983 KB weight stream across all 48 threads. This is row/work partitioning, and it is bit-exact because gemm_bloc accumulates every output element as a single Cv=madd(A_i,B_j,Cv) chain over k whose operation sequence does not depend on RM, RN, BM, x/y blocking or the executing thread; the fp32 summation order is unchanged for every shape and float type. Evidence separating this from the exhausted local dot-kernel family: the node streams at only 14-17 GB/s against ~300 GB/s for dense Q8_0 while its active-thread rate is normal, i.e. the defect is job count on 48 threads, not per-thread dot throughput; the sampled CPU profile corroborates it with the actual plan kernel `tinyBLAS<...unsigned short,unsigned short,float>::gemm_bloc<4,3>` at 1.78% and the F32 instantiation at 0.98%.

statement: In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:2711-2766) widen the multi-row solo predicate: raise the `ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_rows` bound the predicate uses from 1 to the DS41 serving verify graph's row count (nrows <= 3-4, i.e. the ~3-token block plus margin), keeping the element caps (ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_max=4096 and the multi-row rows_max) unchanged. The champion already implements the barrier-elision machinery (ggml-cpu.c:4445-4508): a maximal run of solo nodes is executed on thread 0 with nth=1 and closed by ONE ggml_barrier instead of one barrier per node. Today that gate is `nrows==1`, so on the N=3 verify graph every small F32 elementwise/row node (ADD 136/eval, MUL 64, CLAMP 55, UNARY 62, CONT 47, CPY/GLU/DUP) still pays a full barrier. Widening the row bound to 3-4 activates the existing, already-audited collapse for the serving shape. Bit-exactness by construction (the route's ordering argument): the whitelisted kernels (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/SCALE/CLAMP/FILL/SQR/SQRT/LOG/SIN/COS/SUM_ROWS/UNARY/GLU, and contiguous CPY/CONT/DUP) all partition output by rows via get_thread_range, so running all R rows on thread 0 performs the identical per-element arithmetic in the identical order; only thread 0 writes inside a solo run, so no other thread can observe an intermediate write before the run-closing barrier, and no whitelisted op calls ggml_barrier internally (barrier-calling ops remain excluded). Why faster, and why this is graph scheduling not a kernel edit: the sampled CPU profile puts 37.2% of user cycles in libgomp [unknown] and the node profile shows these tiny ops are barrier-wait domated, not compute dominated (compute/wall ADD 0.111, UNARY 0.188, CONT 0.365, MUL 0.418, CLAMP 0.454, DSV4_HC_POST 0.581) with ~5355 barriers/cycle; because the DS41 verify tensors carry 3 tokens the nrows==1 gate never fires there, so a faster kernel body cannot recover a barrier that is paid even when the node has almost no work. The tree's own comment (ggml-cpu.c:2676-2690) names this exact inertness ('the whole lever is inert exactly where the serving config spends its time').

statement: Work-partitioning fix, not a dot-kernel change: DS41's hc_mixes (F16 [20480,24] x F32 [20480,nt], m=24, n=2-3, 80 nodes/verify graph) reaches tinyBLAS<16,...,unsigned short,unsigned short,float>::matmul with m%8==0, so matmul picks RM=4,BM=2 -> ytiles=m/(RM*BM)=3 and nb_job=ytiles*NB_BN=3; three of 48 threads stream 320 KB each while 45 spin at the in-gemm barriers. The node table shows hc_mixes at 4.6-5.2% of cycle wall streaming only 14-17 GB/s, yet its per-active-thread rate matches a fully-loaded node (perf: gemm_bloc<4,3> 1.78% of cycles), so the diagnosis is thread idleness / poor job partitioning, distinct from the exhausted local quant-dot family (no inner loop, dtype, or dot helper is touched). Fix: add a plan branch in matmul taken when m/(RM*BM) < params->nth that calls mnpack<1,RN,1>(m,n,SIZE_N,BN) with RM=1/BM=1 (ytiles=m) and BN chosen so nb_job>=nth, deriving SIZE_N from the existing balanced BLOCK_SIZE<RN>(n) so the invariant n >= ceil(n/RN)*(RN-1) that the earlier raw 6-cap violated for n in {7,8,9,13,14,19} is preserved by construction (n=3: RN=3/BN=1 gives 24 jobs, RN=2/BN=2 gives 48). Only which mnpack<> specialization is called changes; gemm_bloc accumulates every output element as the identical hsum(madd(A_i,B_j,Cv)) chain over l in the same order regardless of RM/RN/BM or thread, so the result is bit-identical to HEAD.

statement: In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:2712-2765) the solo predicate only admits whitelisted row-partitioned F32 nodes with ggml_nrows(dst)<=1 and nrows(src[0])<=1 (ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_rows=1). The selected serve is the DSpark verify graph at nt=3-4, so its small-op family (ADD 136 calls/eval compute/wall 0.111, CONT 46.7 calls 0.365, MUL 64.3 0.418, CLAMP 54.9 0.454, UNARY 61.8 0.188 per the node profile) has nrows=3-4, is never solo-eligible, and every node therefore pays the unconditional per-node graph barrier -- the rank-1 mechanism family in the request-scoped CPU profile is thread-synchronization-and-work-balance at 37.20% sampled user cycles, all in libgomp barrier code. Mechanism: inside the existing function body, relax the row bound for the already-whitelisted row-partitioned elementwise/contiguous ops (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/SCALE/CLAMP/SQR/UNARY/GLU/CPY/CONT/DUP) from <=1 to a small multi-row cap, keeping the all-F32 and is_contiguous guards and keeping the total-element bound so serialized work stays bounded. The graph loop (ggml_graph_compute_thread, :4440) then collapses maximal runs of these 3-4 row nodes into ONE ggml_cpu_node_is_solo run executed on thread 0, deleting the inter-node barriers. Bit-exact by the code's own construction argument (:2690-2696): the whitelisted kernels partition by rows, no cross-row accumulation is reordered, and the closing barrier still publishes the run before any multi-threaded consumer; eligibility stays conservative (no column-partitioned op, no op with an internal ggml_barrier). This is strictly a scheduling/partition change, not a local dot-kernel edit: the dot kernels are already at 82-94% of the measured 410 GB/s ceiling, whereas the 37.2% sync share is the unaddressed cost. Note: the two prior rows on this idea (akm-ds41-verify-solo-barrier-collapse, akm-ds41-tinysolo-rows-verify) were refused only by the test-backend-ops empty-CPU-suite harness fault (explicitly 'NOT evidence about the patch') plus, for the first, a hunk at :2677 outside every admitted body; the hunk here is confined to the ggml_cpu_node_is_solo body (:2712-2765), an admitted cpu_graph_sync body.

outcome.refusal_reason: Reject: the ordering argument does not hold against the selected tree, so the run is not bit-exact by construction as the cpu_graph_sync route requires. The whitelisted ops do not share one per-thread partition, contrary to the statement's claim that every kernel 'partitions by the identical row range'. In this tree ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/binary-ops.cpp:64) and SQR/SQRT/SIN/COS/LOG/UNARY (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/unary-ops.cpp:125,213,297) enumerate (row, column-chunk) tasks through get_rowcol_split (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/common.h:155-192), which chunks columns whenever nth>1 && nrows<nth && ne0>=512 (default min 512, GGML_ROWCOL_SPLIT default ON) - exactly the DS41 verify shape (3 rows, 48 threads). SCALE (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:4880-4885) and GLU/SWIGLU (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:3502-3507) instead use contiguous row ranges, and CLAMP (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:6471) uses a strided enumeration (j=ith; j+=nth). Same row count and ne[0] therefore does not imply identical element ownership: in a chained run such as MUL then CLAMP, CLAMP's thread 0 reads all columns of row 0 while under MUL row 0's chunks were written by threads 0..15 - a cross-thread read with no intervening barrier, invisible to the per-op test-backend-ops oracle. The allowance 'consumes ... the immediately preceding node in the run' is also too weak: a small broadcast src1 produced in-run is read whole by every thread though the producer's split assigned its elements to a subset of threads. Fix before authoring: make eligibility an ownership-identity test - every node in the run must enumerate the same per-element tasks for the same (nrows, ne0, esz, ith, nth), i.e. partition runs by split class (rowcol vs contiguous-row vs strided-row) rather than by shape alone - and permit an in-run tensor to be consumed only as the same-shape, same-ownership output of the immediately preceding node. The prior solo/tiny-solo objection does not apply to this full-team form (params.nth stays 48), and the target body, route and falsifiers are otherwise admissible; a revised statement carrying these two constraints can be re-reviewed.

statement: Extend in-backend fusion in ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops (ggml-cpu.c:4312) from its single RMS_NORM+MUL pair to a maximal consecutive run of F32 elementwise nodes (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/SCALE/CLAMP/SQR/UNARY/GLU) that are mutually partition-compatible: each has contiguous F32 operands, the same effective row count and ne[0], uses the standard get_thread_range row split, and consumes only tensors published before the run or the immediately preceding node in the run. Execute each node in the run once with the existing full-team params (params.nth unchanged), then return the run length so ggml_graph_compute_thread advances node_n and pays ONE trailing graph barrier for the whole run instead of one barrier per node. Bit-exact by construction: binary-ops.cpp and unary-ops.cpp contain no internal ggml_barrier, every kernel in the run is pure per-element and partitions by the identical row range, so thread i's output rows for node k are exactly the rows it already produced for node k-1 and it reads no row another thread wrote mid-run; the closing barrier still publishes every result before any later node, and no arithmetic or summation order changes. Why it should be faster: the CPU profile's top family is thread-synchronization-and-work-balance at 37.2% (libgomp barrier spin), and the node profile shows the small elementwise nodes spend almost none of their wall computing -- ADD 1.55% of wall at compute/wall 0.111, MUL 1.29% at 0.418, CLAMP 0.90% at 0.454, UNARY 0.67% at 0.188 -- i.e. these nodes are ~90% barrier/straggler, whereas the big GEMMs sit at 0.88-0.90. The distinguishing evidence from the exhausted local quant/dot family is exactly this compute/wall split: the wait is per-node barrier propagation around cheap nodes, not the dot kernel. Fusing each run into a single barrier interval reclaims most of that ~3% of wall. This is not the existing solo-run collapse (:4445-4510 runs nth=1 on thread 0, and is inert at nrows>1) and not ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_rows: it keeps the whole team working on the same partition, so it does not serialize rows onto thread 0.

outcome.refusal_reason: The revised class map is still not an ownership-identity map, so the bit-exact-by-construction claim fails for pairings the class admits. CPY/CONT/DUP do not share the SCALE/GLU task enumeration: ggml_compute_forward_cpy/cont both dispatch to ggml_compute_forward_dup (ops.cpp:545-553, 5124-5135), and a same-type pair contiguous on both sides goes to ggml_compute_forward_dup_same_cont (ops.cpp:355-357), which enumerates FLAT BLOCKS - nk = ggml_nelements/blck, dr = ceil(nk/nth), k0 = dr*ith (ops.cpp:51-55) - not rows. At the DS41 verify shape (ne0=5120, nrows=3, nth=48, F32 blck=1) SCALE gives thread 0 the whole of row 0 (nr = ggml_nrows(src0), dr = ceil(3/48) = 1; ops.cpp:4874-4885; GLU likewise ops.cpp:3491-3507) while dup_same_cont gives thread 0 only flattened columns 0-319 and thread 1 flattened columns 320-639 of that same row; an admitted SCALE->DUP (or DUP->SCALE) run therefore has thread 1 read elements thread 0 wrote with no interior barrier - the same cross-thread read defect that sank the shape-only form, and invisible to the per-op oracle. Even the non-contiguous dup paths partition ne01 rows inside every (i02,i03) plane (ops.cpp:365-371), not the global ggml_nrows used by SCALE/GLU, so 3-D/4-D pairings differ again; (op, nrows, ne0, esz, nth) captures neither distinction. Fix before authoring: define run membership by each kernel's actual task-enumeration function - keep CPY/DUP/CONT out of the SCALE/GLU class unless that exact path is proven to enumerate the identical (nrows, ne0, esz, ith, nth) task set, give dup_same_cont's flat-block enumeration its own class, and key SCALE/GLU membership on nrows(src0) as their kernels do. Also close the channel the no-cross-thread-hazard claim omits: a run node may read a pre-run temporary non-elementwise (broadcast src1, GLU's row halves, non-contiguous dup cursor) while a later in-run output reuses that temporary's freed bytes (ggml-alloc free_block/best_reuse, ggml-alloc.c:109-269), so every non-predecessor input in the run needs elementwise/same-owner reads or an address-range non-overlap check against run outputs. The full-team/no-serialization distinction from the shipped thread-0 tiny-solo collapse (ggml-cpu.c:4445-4508, sp.nth=1) is real, so the idea is not merely already present; the rejection is that the eligibility test as written is not yet an ownership-identity test.

statement: In ggml_graph_compute_thread, keep the full 48-thread team (params.nth stays 48, no serialization onto thread 0) but replace the per-node graph barrier with one barrier per maximal run of execute nodes that share a single per-element ownership partition. Eligibility is an ownership-identity test, not a shape test: classify each node from op type plus (nrows, ne0, esz, nth) into the rowcol class (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/SQR/SQRT/SIN/COS/LOG/UNARY, which enumerate (row, column-chunk) tasks through get_rowcol_split), the contiguous-row class (SCALE/GLU/CPY/DUP/CONT) or the strided class (CLAMP, j=ith; j+=nth); a run admits only nodes of one class with identical shape/esz, and an in-run tensor may be consumed only as the same-shape, same-ownership output of the immediately preceding node. With identical ownership, thread t writes exactly the elements it later reads, so no cross-thread hazard exists and the interior barriers carry no publication ordering: k consecutive barriers collapse to 1. Every thread still executes every node with HEAD's identical per-element arithmetic in the identical order, so the change is bit-exact; only synchronization changes. This is the sync lever for the 37.2% libgomp sampled share and the node-profile wall-minus-compute (~21% of the verify cycle, ~5355 barriers/cycle), which the shipped tiny-solo run-collapse cannot reach on this serving shape because its gate requires ggml_nrows==1 while every DS41 verify tensor has nrows=3, leaving GGML_TINY_SOLO_ROWS inert. It is a graph-scheduling-only edit, distinct from the exhausted local quant/dot kernel family and from the already-settled plain tiny-solo/GGML_TINY_SOLO_ROWS widening.

statement: In `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:ggml_compute_forward_rms_norm_f32` the parallelism domain is rows only (`for (int64_t i01 = ith; i01 < ne01; i01 += nth)` at :4115), so the ~2 norm ops per layer are executed by at most `min(ne01, nth)` threads: at decode N=1 only 1 of 48 threads participates and at speculative verify N=3 only 3 of 48 participate, leaving the rest of each call serialized behind one row's full scalar sum/reduce plus scale/mul store over ne00. Extend the partition to columns as well when `ne01 < nth`: give each thread a contiguous column-block of length `ceil(ne00 / ceil(nth/ne01))` for every row it co-owns, reduce the squared-sum in a fixed contiguous-block order (deterministic tree by block index, `bsum = bsum + block_sum` in ascending block order), publish the per-row `scale` via a per-row slot, then run the element-wise scale (or fused `x*scale*w`) over the same blocks. This turns the norm nodes from row-serial into row+column-parallel across all threads, shrinking the serial fraction of the graph (RMS_NORM ~3.17% of sampled cycles) without touching the exhausted local quant/dot or barrier families.

The VNNI seed scratch layout is half the required size and corrupts the precomputed seeds, so gemm4xN returns wrong results. The seed mullo(dpbusd(0,1,b),-128) for one 32-byte B block is 8 int32 (32 bytes; _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 yields 8 dwords, a zmm pair 16 dwords/64 bytes), but gemm4xN_seedbuf allocates only rn*k*4 int32 and every address uses (j*k+l)*4, i.e. 16 bytes per block. The 64-byte pair stores at l+=2 therefore step only 32 bytes, so each store overwrites the previous store's odd-block half and odd-indexed block seeds are never retained: the zmm pair load reads [seed(l), seed(l+2)] instead of [seed(l), seed(l+1)], and odd-offset 256-bit loads read mixed halves of two adjacent seeds, changing the correction term and producing values that differ from the removed inline seeds. The last row's pair store also writes 32 bytes past the rn*k*4 allocation (out-of-bounds). A correct layout needs 8 int32 per block (rn*k*8).

outcome.refusal_reason: As written, this change cannot reduce the reduction instruction count, which is the mechanism it claims. The falsifier ('candidate disassembly must show fewer integer reduction instructions') would therefore trigger before any build is useful. Source check at iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:864-872: each (iy, j) step does 2 vpdpbusd, then per operand two levels of vpshufd+vpaddd (0xb1, then 0x4e), which is 4 shuffles and 4 adds, then one vpermt2d with sumi_perm. The output is [A0,A2,B0,B2,A1,A3,B1,B3], where A_k/B_k is the sum of the four dword lanes of 128-bit lane k of pA/pB. (1) AVX-512 has no horizontal or pairwise add: VPHADDD has no EVEX/512-bit form. VPADDQ is a vertical 64-bit add. Every reduction level still needs one data-movement op (vpshufd, vpsrlq or valignd) to bring the partner lane into place, followed by one add. Level 1: a qword add cannot sum the two dwords inside its own lane without a shift, so it is shift+add versus shuffle+add. Level 2: vpshufd 0x4e + vpaddq versus vpshufd 0x4e + vpaddd. The count is the same. The existing lane selection is also kept, so a per-operand reduction plus vpermt2d stays at 9 ops. (2) There is no signedness problem to solve. Each dpbusd lane is bounded well inside int32 (u8 0..31 times s8, four products), and vpaddd wraps mod 2^32, so the current sums are already exact. A 'sign-preserving' vpaddq path needs sign extension (vpmovsxdq, or vpsllq+vpsraq), which adds instructions and doubles register width. The hypothesis also gives no concrete instruction sequence showing how the count falls. Refine it into a mechanism that actually removes ops, for example by combining the two operands before reducing: t = add(unpacklo_epi32(pA,pB), unpackhi_epi32(pA,pB)); t = add(t, shuffle_epi32(t, 0x4e)). That puts A_k in lane 4k and B_k in lane 4k+1. Then take the low 256 bits of _mm512_permutexvar_epi32 with indices {0,8,1,9,4,12,5,13}. That is 6 ops instead of 9 per (iy, j), and it is bit-identical because integer adds are exact and associative mod 2^32. State the exact sequence and the before/after op count, and keep the scale, FMA order and activation quantization unchanged.

HEAD source (sgemm.cpp:1528-1532) gives each thread duty = ceil(tiles/nth) tiles. For 256 tiles on 48 threads that is 6 tiles each on threads 0-41, 4 tiles on thread 42 and none on threads 43-47. outcome.refusal_reason: Rejected on three grounds: scope creep, a correctness hazard, and not implementing the accepted mechanism. (1) Scope. The cpu_graph_sync route admits hunks only inside the bodies of ggml_barrier, ggml_cpu_node_is_solo, ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops and ggml_graph_compute_thread. This diff also adds a file-scope #define (near line 64), a new struct ggml_barrier_flag type, new bflags/bround fields in struct ggml_threadpool, initialisation code in ggml_threadpool_new_impl, and a reset block plus an extra `#pragma omp barrier` in ggml_graph_compute. The gate will refuse every one of these hunks. (2) It does not implement the accepted mechanism. That mechanism places all state in a function-local static inside the ggml_barrier body, keyed by (threadpool, n_threads). This patch moves the state into the threadpool struct and adds rebasing logic in ggml_graph_compute. The extra `#pragma omp barrier` also follows an `omp single` that already ends in an implicit barrier, so it adds one more libgomp barrier per graph for nothing. (3) Correctness. Neither tools/server, common nor src calls ggml_threadpool_new or llama_attach_threadpool for this recipe. Every ggml_graph_compute therefore builds a disposable threadpool (ggml-cpu.c:4906-4911), whose bround starts at 0 and is bumped to 1. After the first region, every thread's __thread my_round is already 1, so the 'my_round != r' rebase never fires again, and the comment's claim that gen is 're-based to 0 on every new region' is false in the served configuration. From then on, my_round is keyed only by thread, not by threadpool, and gen keeps counting across regions, graphs and contexts (target and DSpark drafter). Barrier lockstep then rests on an unproven invariant: every pooled OpenMP thread must have executed exactly the same total number of ggml_barrier calls across all prior regions. A single region with a different team size, or a graph computed from a different master OS thread (libgomp keeps one thread pool per master), breaks it. If a peer's gen is lower, a thread spins forever on that peer's slot: a hang at the end of the region. If a peer's gen is higher, `(int32_t)(slot - s) >= 0` passes before that peer has finished its node-k writes, which is a data race and silent non-bit-exact output. The ordering argument in the mechanism holds only while generations are in lockstep, and this patch does not guarantee that. outcome.refusal_reason: The arithmetic is correct, but the route gate will refuse this patch before the build, exactly as it refused the prior one. I checked the arithmetic and found no problem. The paired zmm stores and the ymm tail stores both use 8 int32 per block at (j*k+l)*8. The prepass splits at (k/8)*8, which matches l8. Every seed load at l, l+1, l+2, l+3 and k-1 matches the B block that its bvec0/bz loads. The highest index is RN*k*8-1, so the buffer is not overrun. Iterating first..end in steps of xtiles visits each job in [start,end) exactly once, and the tiles write disjoint parts of C, so the output stays bit-identical. The defect is structural. gates.py `_brace_deltas`/`_cpu_route_bounds` count braces line by line and ignore preprocessor branches. The diff opens the job loop twice: `for (int64_t job = first; job < end; job += xtiles) {` under `#if` (sgemm.cpp:1571) and `for (int64_t job = start; job < end; ++job) {` under `#else` (:1574). Together with the x loop's `{` (:1543), the naive count sees three opening braces. It sees only two closing braces: the existing one at :2077 and the `#if`-guarded one at :2079. With one brace left unclosed, the `class tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX` block never closes, and the admitted window runs to the end of the file. The window then holds four `void mnpack(int64_t m0, int64_t m, int64_t n0, int64_t n) {` markers (:1376, :2505, :3332, :4050). That is verbatim the refusal already returned for this mechanism ("marker ... occurs 4 times inside the admitted window"). Re-anchoring did not fix it, because the cause is this split loop header, not the anchor. Fix: make the braces balance on every preprocessor branch. For example, use the x-major loop order unconditionally, `for (int64_t x = 0; x < xtiles; ++x) { first = ...; if (first >= end) continue; jj = n0 + x*RN; <#if VNNI: seed prepass #endif> for (int64_t job = first; job < end; job += xtiles) { ii = ...; ... } }`. That keeps a single job-loop header and a single closing brace for each loop outside any `#if`. It is bit-exact in every build, because tile order does not affect any output. Keep the `#if` only around the seedbuf allocation, the prepass and `delete[]`. Optionally, allocate seedbuf once per call on the stack or as a thread_local instead of calling new[] every time, but that only affects speed.

The champion pays ~5355 such barriers per 101 ms verify cycle (operator note 40: ~3.1 us/barrier ~= 16 ms/cycle; node-profile wall-compute gap 21.4 ms/cycle; perf profile: libgomp 34.21% of sampled user cycles). Mechanism: inside the ggml_barrier body only (OpenMP branch), replace the `#pragma omp barrier` with a per-thread arrival-flag barrier: n cache-line-aligned uint32 slots in a function-local static keyed by (threadpool, n_threads), falling back to `#pragma omp barrier` if state is unavailable or n>64; each thread release-stores its own monotonically increasing generation (static __thread counter) into its own slot, then acquire-polls the n slots until every slot shows its generation. Arrivals become n parallel stores to n distinct lines (no serialized RMW, no cross-node bounce) and release is n-1 shared acquire loads (each slot line written once per barrier). Bit-exact: no arithmetic is touched. Ordering argument: every thread's node-k writes are sequenced-before its release store to its slot; any thread's acquire load of its generation from slot u synchronizes-with u's release store, so before any thread starts node k+1 it sees all threads' node-k writes - the same release/acquire contract the current full-fence `#pragma omp barrier` provides; all threads run the identical node loop, hence the identical barrier sequence, so generations stay in lockstep. Why faster: removes the serialized-arrival cost (~1-2 us of the measured ~3.1 us/barrier at 48 spread threads) x 5355 barriers ~= 4-9 ms of the 101 ms cycle (4-9%); the pessimistic split (only release latency saved, ~0.4 us/barrier) is ~2 ms (~2%). This is distinct from the idle-spin/wait-policy and thread-count knobs retired on 2026-09-23 under the 220 GB/s premise that operator note 40 (2026-09-26) explicitly contradicted and re-priced the per-node sync floor as the second lever; the cpu_graph_sync route admitting ggml_barrier was granted the same day.

statement: In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:2711-2766) widen the multi-row solo predicate: raise the `ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_rows` bound the predicate uses from 1 to the DS41 serving verify graph's row count (nrows <= 3-4, i.e. the ~3-token block plus margin), keeping the element caps (ggml_cpu_tiny_solo_max=4096 and the multi-row rows_max) unchanged. The champion already implements the barrier-elision machinery (ggml-cpu.c:4445-4508): a maximal run of solo nodes is executed on thread 0 with nth=1 and closed by ONE ggml_barrier instead of one barrier per node. Today that gate is `nrows==1`, so on the N=3 verify graph every small F32 elementwise/row node (ADD 136/eval, MUL 64, CLAMP 55, UNARY 62, CONT 47, CPY/GLU/DUP) still pays a full barrier. Widening the row bound to 3-4 activates the existing, already-audited collapse for the serving shape. Bit-exactness by construction (the route's ordering argument): the whitelisted kernels (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/SCALE/CLAMP/FILL/SQR/SQRT/LOG/SIN/COS/SUM_ROWS/UNARY/GLU, and contiguous CPY/CONT/DUP) all partition output by rows via get_thread_range, so running all R rows on thread 0 performs the identical per-element arithmetic in the identical order; only thread 0 writes inside a solo run, so no other thread can observe an intermediate write before the run-closing barrier, and no whitelisted op calls ggml_barrier internally (barrier-calling ops remain excluded). Why faster, and why this is graph scheduling not a kernel edit: the sampled CPU profile puts 37.2% of user cycles in libgomp [unknown] and the node profile shows these tiny ops are barrier-wait domated, not compute dominated (compute/wall ADD 0.111, UNARY 0.188, CONT 0.365, MUL 0.418, CLAMP 0.454, DSV4_HC_POST 0.581) with ~5355 barriers/cycle; because the DS41 verify tensors carry 3 tokens the nrows==1 gate never fires there, so a faster kernel body cannot recover a barrier that is paid even when the node has almost no work. The tree's own comment (ggml-cpu.c:2676-2690) names this exact inertness ('the whole lever is inert exactly where the serving config spends its time').
