outcome.refusal_reason: The central source premise is false, and the improvement it claims for its headline shape is already present at HEAD. In sgemm.cpp:1525-1527 with m=1024, RN=3 (xtiles=1) and nth=48, tiles4=256. That gives rows4 = 4*ceil(256/48) = 24 and rows2 = 2*ceil(512/48) = 2*11 = 22. Because rows2 < rows4, line 2048 runs run<2>, with ytiles=512 and duty=ceil(512/48)=11 two-row tiles. The maximum is therefore already 22 rows, not 24. That came from the kept akm-ds41-dense-q8-two-row-tail-tiles (+1.716%). The statement says it accounts for the two-row selector but gets its arithmetic wrong, so the claim that the maximum goes from 24 to 22 restates what HEAD already does. More generally, HEAD's maximum is min(4*ceil(m/(4*nth)), 2*ceil(m/(2*nth))). The two-row term is never more than ceil(m/nth)+1, so HEAD is always within one output row of the best possible ceil(m/nth). A bulk-plus-row-tail partition can shave at most one row per call. It can only do that on shapes where the selector keeps RM=4 because rows2 == rows4: m=512 goes from 12 to 11, m=1280 from 28 to 27, m=2048 from 44 to 43, m=5120 from 108 to 107, and m=8192 from 172 to 171. On shapes where RM=2 is already optimal (m=1024, 4096, 16384) the critical path does not shorten at all. There the change only swaps two-row tiles for four-row bulk plus single rows, which is a reuse change the hypothesis neither states nor argues. To refine it: (1) restate the premise with HEAD's real selector arithmetic. Name the DS41 dense Q8_0 m values that actually take the RM=4 path, and frame the target as that one-row bound on those shapes. (2) Say what happens on shapes where RM=2 is already optimal: either keep HEAD's path or justify four-row bulk as a reuse mechanism. (3) Say how single-row tasks are made safe. The current lambda always loads A row ii+1 (lines 1569-1573, 1619-1623 and onward), so an RM=1 task on the last row would read out of bounds unless every row-1 load and Cw/Cv[.][1] update is guarded. The per-output FMA chain and the bit-identity argument are otherwise sound, and the route and falsifier are acceptable.

statement: In tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX::gemm4xN, distribute an evenly divisible bulk of four-row tiles across threads, then distribute the residual output rows individually, retaining the existing zmm dot arithmetic for each row. Current source chooses uniformly between two-row and four-row tiles, both using ceil-sized contiguous thread ranges; for 1024 output rows on 48 threads, either choice leaves a 24-row maximum. A bulk-plus-row-tail partition reduces that maximum to 22 rows while retaining four-row weight/activation reuse in the bulk. The earlier unmeasured subtile proposal remains relevant, but its premise must account for the now-present two-row selector. This addresses dense-kernel work imbalance rather than the exhausted graph-barrier mechanisms or the regressing seed prepass. Dense Q8 accounts for 24.22% of sampled user-cycle periods; MUL_MAT has 41.26% sibling wall share, including other kernels. Neither fraction predicts a gain. Preserve activation quantization, each output's block traversal, FMA chain and reduction order for bit-identical outputs.

outcome.refusal_reason:
None of the loop's correctness gates ever runs the new code, so a wrong-output bug in the new path would reach serving timing undetected. That is a correctness risk the existing gates cannot resolve. The arithmetic itself is right. At sgemm.cpp:1525-1527/2048 with nth=48, m=512/1280/2048/5120/8192 do select RM=4 with rows2==rows4, the maximum falls 12/28/44/108/172 to 11/27/43/107/171, and m=1024 is already 22 on the RM=2 path. Bit-identity per output also holds: every output keeps the same l8/l4/k%2 FMA chain whatever RM is. Points (1) and (2) of the previous rejection are answered.

The problem is reachability. The new path only fires for RN=2 or 3, xtiles=1, HEAD choosing RM=4, and rows4 > ceil(m/nth). The independent Q8_0 oracle never meets that condition. It uses K=256 and ROWS=40 (cpu_quant_reference.py:33) on the default 4-thread team (cpu_quant_reference_probe.cpp:112-117; GGML_DEFAULT_N_THREADS=4). Widths 2, 3, 6 and 7 reach gemm4xN<2|3> with xtiles=1, tiles4=10, rows4=12 and rows2=10, so HEAD takes RM=2 at the optimal ceil(40/4)=10 and the new path stays off. Widths 1, 4, 5 and 8 reach only RN=1 or RN=4 (5 = gemm4xN<4> + gemm4xN<1>, 8 = gemm4xN<4> with xtiles=2). The native MUL_MAT suite is not independent here anyway, and it misses the path too. Its active Q8_0 cases are either m=16, where tiles4=4 is below nth so RM=2 is always chosen, or n=32 at m=512/2880, which is RN=4. The mnpack GDB witness proves only that mnpack was entered.

So the falsifier's requirement of bit-identical HEAD outputs on eligible dimensions and on single-row residual cases including the final row is not something the loop checks. Several bugs would therefore go uncaught:
- a range or tile partition that skips or double-writes rows;
- an RM=1 row that keeps HEAD's unconditional row ii+1 accesses (lines 1569-1573, 1619/1623, 1681/1684, 1739/1742, 1797/1800, 1861/1865, 1923/1926, 1983/1986), which reads row m on the last row;
- a missing #else updot-branch guard.
Only the speed A/B would run on that untested code.

To re-propose, make the new branch gate-reachable before authoring. Either (a) get an operator-admitted oracle shape that hits it, or (b) re-scope the trigger so the existing fixture runs it. For (a), examples: the same 40-row Q8_0 fixture on a 6-thread team, where tiles4=10, rows4=rows2=8 and ceil(40/6)=7, so the 7-row ranges exercise RM=1 including row 39 at widths 2, 3, 6 and 7; or an m=512, nth=48 case. If the loop cannot do either, choose another mechanism.

Advisory, not grounds for rejection: per (block, column), an RM=1 task repeats the seed dpbusd+mullo, bbs/dvec and B loads that a four-row tile amortises. Three single rows therefore cost about one four-row tile in VNNI work, so an 11-row range built as 4+4+1+1+1 saves mainly A-row bytes. A 4+4+2+1 tail, reusing the existing RM=2 instantiation, would keep more of the claimed bound. Also restrict the partition to [m0, m0+4*floor((m-m0)/4)). mnpack's recursive remainder call owns the rows past that.

statement: Refine gemm4xN only for RN=2 or 3, xtiles=1, and shapes where HEAD selects RM=4 and its maximum row ownership exceeds ceil(m/nth). Partition output rows into balanced contiguous ranges, computing four-row tiles within each range and remaining rows with guarded RM=1 tasks using the existing arithmetic. At 48 threads, eligible DS41 dense dimensions include m=512,1280,2048,5120,8192, reducing maximum ownership respectively from 12,28,44,108,172 to 11,27,43,107,171 rows. Preserve HEAD's RM=2 path, including m=1024 where HEAD already achieves 22 rows. Guard every second-row scale/load and accumulator update in every zmm and ymm branch before permitting RM=1, including the last output row. Preserve each output's block traversal, FMA chain and reduction, so outputs remain bit-identical. This targets dense-kernel straggler work within the observed 24.22% dense-Q8 sampled-cycle family and 41.26% MUL_MAT sibling wall share; neither share predicts a gain. It avoids the exhausted barrier/solo mechanisms and the regressed seed prepass: synchronization and activation arithmetic remain unchanged, with no scratch prepass. The opportunity is bounded to one fewer row on eligible calls, and reduced tile reuse may erase it.

outcome.refusal_reason: Rejected. No gate runs the code path that serving would use, and the falsifier's named independent check never executes the change. (1) The scalar Q4_K/Q5_K MUL_MAT_ID fixture never reaches the N>1 path. cpu_quant_reference_probe.cpp:96-98 builds b=[K,width,1] and ids=[width,1], so ids->ne[1]==1 at every width from 1 to 8. ggml-cpu.c:3459-3461 reserves (n_tasks-1) private activation slices whenever ids->ne[1]==1, so mmid_batch1 (iqk_dispatch.cpp:432-552) always returns before the mapping block at :563-587. The 'independent scalar comparisons at widths 1-8 in alternating and single-expert modes' therefore cannot fail because of this patch. (2) Only two gates reach the N>1 map: the native MUL_MAT_ID suite (iqk against use_ref native ggml) and the n=4 witness (n_mats=4, n_used=2; cpu_route_witness.py:68). Both run at N_THREADS = hardware_concurrency() = 192 (test-backend-ops.cpp:54 and :12389). The iqk-eligible Q4_K/Q5_K eval cases use n_mats 4 or 8 (:10651-10694). The 128-expert case (:10451) is Q8_0, which iqk refuses at :394, and no iqk-eligible eval case has n_mats > 192. So in every gated case each thread owns at most one expert, and the ownership stride 'ith, ith+nth, ...' never takes a second iteration. Serving is the opposite case: 384 experts (router [5120,384]) on 48 threads, so every thread owns 8 experts and the stride is the whole mechanism. The counts and maps live in reused wdata. A defect confined to the stride would leave stale counts for experts >= nth. Examples are zeroing or appending only the first owned expert, or a mismatch between the init and append ownership predicates. Stale counts make the expert loop index garbage map rows, which corrupts serving output or reads out of bounds, yet every gate still passes. The A/B measures only throughput. The falsifier's 'bit-identical against HEAD' is also not enforced by any gate: the native suite is an NMSE comparison against native ggml. To re-propose, get a gate that reaches multi-expert ownership on the N>1 path before authoring. For example, ask the operator to admit a Q4_K/Q5_K MUL_MAT_ID case with ids->ne[1]>1 and n_as>nth, such as the n=4 witness case on a 4-thread team with n_mats>=8, or the scalar fixture with ids [n_used, tokens>1] and more experts than threads. If that cannot be done, choose another mechanism. Advisory, not grounds for rejection: the premise overstates what becomes parallel. Every thread, including thread 0, still scans all ne11*n_ids IDs in HEAD's order, so thread 0's scan is not shortened. Only the n_as-entry count memset (~3 KB) and at most ne11*n_ids appends are distributed. That is tens of ns beside thread 0's row quantization. Stride ownership also puts 8 adjacent int64 counts, owned by 8 different threads on different CCDs, into each 64-B line. That adds false-sharing RFOs before the barrier, and HEAD's single writer has none. Thread 0's MUL_MAT_ID compute/wall of 0.839 also suggests it usually waits rather than straggles. If you re-propose, pad the owned counts to cache lines and price that cost. The plan reserves CACHE_LINE_SIZE*n_as at ggml-cpu.c:3468, which the iqk carve does not use; confirm the wsize check covers it.

At HEAD (iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:754-762 and 862-885), values[0..3] are four separate 32-weight sub-blocks, and y.qs+0 and y.qs+1 hold four separate Q8 blocks. pA lanes 0-7 are sub-block 0 and lanes 8-15 are sub-block 1. pB lanes 0-7 are sub-block 2 and lanes 8-15 are sub-block 3. HEAD's two shuffle/add stages leave one 4-lane sum in lanes 0, 4, 8 and 12 of sa and sb. sumi_perm then selects, from the 32-lane source {sa, sb}, the lanes [0,8,16,24,4,12,20,28]. That gives [sb0lo, sb1lo, sb2lo, sb3lo, sb0hi, sb1hi, sb2hi, sb3hi]. Lane k is then multiplied by d4d8 lane k = scale(4j+k%4) * d8(k%4), so each lane needs its own sub-block sum. An elementwise pA+pB adds sub-block 0 to sub-block 2 and sub-block 1 to sub-block 3. Those pairs have different weight scales and different activation d values. After two shuffle/add stages, only 4 distinct sums remain, mixed across scales, where 8 are needed. You cannot recover the 8 sums from 16 lanes reduced in groups of 4. The proposed single-source permutation is also invalid. _mm512_permutexvar_epi32 uses only the low 4 index bits, so indices 16, 20, 24 and 28 become 0, 4, 8 and 12 and duplicate lanes. Now lane 4L holds pA's 128-bit-lane-L sum and lane 4L+1 holds pB's. Finish with a single-source _mm512_permutexvar_epi32 using indices [0,8,1,9,4,12,5,13] in the low 8 lanes, then _mm512_castsi512_si256. That gives exactly HEAD's eight int32 sums in HEAD's lane order. Integer addition is exact here, since |sum| is at most 16*31*128. The op count drops from 4 shuffles + 4 adds + vpermt2d to 2 unpacks + 1 shuffle + 2 adds + vpermd. Keep all 8 lanes. statement: In the OpenMP build, ggml_barrier (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:599-613) lowers to `#pragma omp barrier`. libgomp's barrier serializes all 48 arrivals on ONE atomic counter cache line (48 dependent RMWs per barrier) and releases via one flag line; with OMP_PROC_BIND=spread across the 4 NPS4 nodes that line bounces cross-node on every barrier. The champion pays ~5355 such barriers per 101 ms verify cycle (operator note 40: ~3.1 us/barrier ~= 16 ms/cycle; node-profile wall-compute gap 21.4 ms/cycle; perf profile: libgomp 34.21% of sampled user cycles). Mechanism: inside the ggml_barrier body only (OpenMP branch), replace the `#pragma omp barrier` with a per-thread arrival-flag barrier: n cache-line-aligned uint32 slots in a function-local static keyed by (threadpool, n_threads), falling back to `#pragma omp barrier` if state is unavailable or n>64; each thread release-stores its own monotonically increasing generation (static __thread counter) into its own slot, then acquire-polls the n slots until every slot shows its generation. outcome.refusal_reason: The change is already present in the selected build, so this would be a null arm. HEAD (sgemm.cpp:1580) writes the seed as _mm512_mullo_epi32(_mm512_dpbusd_epi32(zerob, one8b, bz), m128b). It already uses dpbusd with unsigned byte ones. In GCC 15, _mm512_mullo_epi32 is defined as a generic vector multiply, `(__v16su)__A * (__v16su)__B` (avx512fintrin.h:4380-4383), so the compiler applies its usual rewrite for a multiply by a constant. A read-only objdump of the measured anchor (anchor-gen-016/bin/libggml-cpu.so.0.16.0) shows no vpmulld in either hot lambda, tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX<block_q8_0,block_q8_0,float>::gemm4xN<3>::{lambda}<4> at 0x27c8d0 or <2> at 0x27e9f0. After each seed vpdpbusd the compiler already emits `vpsubd %zmmX,%zmm6,%zmmX` (negate against zero) followed by `vpslld $0x7`: the negate and seven-bit shift the hypothesis proposes. So the premise that this 'replaces the current packed integer multiply' is false for the binary under test. Writing the shift and subtract by hand can at most reorder the same two instructions, so there is no causal mechanism behind the predicted reduction in port contention. The bit-identity argument is correct (the sums lie in [-512,508], and -128*s equals -(s<<7)), but that is only because the operation is already the same. To reopen, point to a seed or correction instruction that actually appears in this DSO's disassembly and that the edit would remove or make cheaper, for example eliminating the seed dpbusd per (j, block pair) by hoisting it or sharing it across RM rows. That mechanism must be distinct from the already-kept seed-accum and offset-vnni keeps.

outcome.refusal_reason:
None of the gates you name can ever run the new branch, so correctness would be checked only in serving. I checked this against HEAD 74ee5c502.

(1) The workspace predicate rules out every single-op graph. ggml_graph_plan is outside the cpu_mul_mat_body route, and its MUL_MAT case (ggml-cpu.c, the INF-70 D1 block) multiplies the src1 conversion size by n_tasks only when src1 has one row. For a multi-row src1 it reserves ne11*ne12*ne13*row_size, and the tail adds CACHE_LINE_SIZE*n_threads. Your branch needs nth*rows*row_size. Take the fixture's Q8_0 case: K=256, so row_size is 272 B. At ne11=2 on 4 threads the graph reserves 544+256 = 800 B, but the branch needs 2176 B. Any team of two or more threads with row_size >= 64 fails the same way. So the scalar fixture (cpu_quant_reference_probe.cpp, a one-node graph), every native test-backend-ops MUL_MAT case and the GDB witness all fall back to HEAD. Only a multi-node graph where some other node's buffer is larger, as in serving, can take the private multi-row path.

(2) The other predicates exclude the fixture as well:
- Q8_0 runs on the default 4-thread team (GGML_DEFAULT_N_THREADS; only float arms call set_n_threads(8)). At K=256 that is 8 blocks per row, which is more than nth.
- F16 at K=256 on 8 threads has 256 blocks of size 1, again more than nth.
- Under the launch env (GGML_IQK=1), ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat takes Q4_K and Q5_K before any conversion, because iqk_shape_supported accepts 40 rows.
- The cpu_mul_mat_body witness case is n=16, which is above your four-row bound.

(3) The native suite is not independent for Q8_0 or F16. use_ref only disables iqk and the hadamard hint, so both arms run the same candidate body and the same tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX code.

The new code needs a new slice layout, nth*rows*nbw1 with i12/i13 offsets, and must drop the barrier with no stale or overlapping reads. A slice-stride overlap, a wrong per-row offset or a stale cross-thread read would pass every gate and corrupt dense Q8_0 outputs in serving. Your falsifier's 'independent scalar Q8_0/Q4_K/Q5_K/F16 comparisons at widths 1-8' cannot fail because of this patch. The same defect got akm-ds41-hc-norm-mixes-splitk-fusion and akm-ds41-mmid-expert-owned-map rejected.

To re-propose, the eligible path must be reachable by an independent gate under the existing workspace sizing. Options:
- Use a private buffer that does not depend on wsize growth, if one exists within the admitted bodies.
- Get operator admission of a ggml_graph_plan sizing hunk, together with a scalar fixture case that runs the branch: Q8_0 with K/32 <= nth (for example K=128 on 4 threads, or K=256 on 8 threads) at widths 2-4, and a GDB/witness case with n <= 4.
- Choose another mechanism.

Advisory, not grounds for rejection:
- The source analysis is otherwise sound. tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX uses a static duty partition with no shared state or barrier. Float tinyBLAS::gemm sets and barriers its own chunk counter. The nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1 argument already used by mm_batch1 carries over.
- Name which served Q8_0 nodes have ne10 <= 48*32 = 1536 at nth=48. The large projections (K 4096, 5120 and 8192) are all excluded, so the eligible set may be very small.

outcome.refusal_reason: The stated mechanism fails on arithmetic. In gemm4xN (sgemm.cpp:1525-1533), with T tiles and nth=48, the ceil scheme gives the busiest thread duty=ceil(T/nth) tiles. Take T=49: ceil gives 24 threads x2, 1 thread x1 and 23 threads idle; proportional gives 1 thread x2 and 47 threads x1. The makespan is 2 tiles either way. There is no barrier between the gemm4xN<4> and gemm4xN<1> calls in mnpack, and the same totals hold when the two calls are summed per thread. So the change only moves the idle slots; it cannot shorten the critical path or reduce straggler wait if every tile costs the same. A gain is possible only if per-tile time depends on which threads are active. OMP_PROC_BIND=spread puts thread i on core 2i, so the ceil scheme leaves the high-ith threads idle, and those sit on NUMA nodes 2-3. The active streams then crowd onto the low nodes' CCD links. The profile's sync gradient fits this: 37.8% on node 0 against 53.1% on node 3, and 69-71% on TIDs pinned to CPUs 92-94. But a bandwidth model can also make proportional slower: if active threads already saturate bandwidth, the single thread holding the extra tile finishes it alone, at single-thread speed. This critic rejected the same claim for this function on 2026-10-05 (akm-cpu-q8-tile-balanced-partition). (1) Tile counts. gemm4xN (sgemm.cpp:1548-1556) now uses the kept proportional split from 802bf9ac6: [T*ith/nth, T*(ith+1)/nth). Every tile has the same cost: same k, same RN. With T tiles, nth=48 and r = T mod 48, the busiest thread gets ceil(T/48) tiles under both the proportional and the cyclic scheme, so the makespan in tiles is the same. There is no barrier between gemm4xN<5> and the m%4 remainder recursion in mnpack (sgemm.cpp:1395-1399), so summing per thread changes nothing. (2) NUMA. The recipe runs numactl --interleave=all with GGML_NOHUGEPAGE_PROCESS=1, so weight pages go round-robin over the 4 nodes at 4 KiB. A four-row Q8_0 tile is 4*(k/32)*34 bytes: about 10.9 KB at k=2560 and 43.5 KB at k=10240, which is 2.7 to 10.6 pages. Both a contiguous chunk and a set of strided tiles therefore average to about a 25% local share per thread. Spreading neighbouring tiles changes no thread's node mix, and the hypothesis names no other channel that could create or remove a straggler. (3) Remainder placement. The only systematic thing cyclic changes is where the r extra tiles go. Cyclic gives them to ith 0..r-1. Under OMP_PROC_BIND=spread with OMP_PLACES=cores over 0-95, those threads sit on cores 0..2r-2, which is node 0 (and node 1 when r > 12). So the tail phase runs crowded onto one node's CCDs while the other threads spin. That partly reverses the channel the current champion kept 802bf9ac6 for, which spreads those extra tiles across all ith and nodes. The hypothesis neither notices that it undoes a kept change nor states the expected direction under that channel, and that direction is plausibly negative. A serving A/B of the patch as stated would therefore test an unnamed placement change, not straggler reduction. outcome.refusal_reason: The census and the remainder rule are now correct. At N=5, xtiles=1, so T=m/4, and all eleven T mod 48 values check out. No m%4 pass runs. Giving the r tail tiles to HEAD's proportional extra-tile threads keeps the makespan and the per-thread NUMA mix the same as HEAD. The BE-order argument also stands. The problem is the one positive channel the hypothesis names. The source shows it is backwards, so the honest expected sign is not 'uncertain'. (1) In gemm4xN (sgemm.cpp:1548-1556) with xtiles=1, tile t is rows 4t..4t+3, a contiguous 4*(k/32)*34 = 4.25k-byte span. Under HEAD each thread runs its tiles back to back. Take a line that straddles the end of row 4t+3 and the start of row 4t+4. That happens only when the span is not 64-aligned: tensors are aligned to 32 B (TENSOR_ALIGNMENT 32), and the span is 64-misaligned outright at k=320/640. HEAD's thread reads that line in the last k step of tile t and again in the first k step of tile t+1, so the second read hits L1. The L2 streamer's overrun past row 4t+3 also lands in rows that the same thread uses next. Lines shared between threads exist only at HEAD's 47 chunk boundaries per node. (2) Under cyclic ownership, all T-1 tile boundaries become cross-core, and that includes the tail, which goes to spread threads. Thread j+1 reads the start of row 4t+4 at the beginning of a round. Thread j reads the end of row 4t+3 a whole tile-time later, on another core, and often on another CCD under spread/cores placement. The streamer overrun becomes wasted traffic. Every tile restarts its prefetch and 4-KiB TLB walk (no THP; one tile is 2.7-10.6 pages), where HEAD only steps into adjacent pages. So cyclic ownership cannot increase reuse at tile boundaries; it can only add cross-thread lines and lose continuity. With makespan and NUMA mix held at HEAD's, every channel the source supports has a sign of zero or less. A serving A/B against a 6.528% five-pair floor would therefore test a change whose net sign the source puts at or below zero, labelled as an open question. One example is instantaneous per-node demand under MPOL_INTERLEAVE: a moving contiguous 48-tile window against HEAD's chunk offsets. If you use it, quantify it against the 2-3 pages each 4-row tile already touches at once. Then state the net expected sign plainly, including the costs above. The mechanism, the BE-order argument and the safety design are sound. The problem is that no correctness gate the loop runs for this route can ever execute the new code, and the falsifier says otherwise. (1) The new path only runs when wsize >= nth * (ne11*ne12*ne13) * row_size. The hypothesis rules out a scratch-plan change, and ggml_graph_plan is outside cpu_mul_mat_body anyway. ggml_graph_plan (ggml-cpu.c:3430-3443) multiplies the MUL_MAT scratch by n_tasks only when src1 has one row. For N >= 2 it reserves a single copy, row_size(vec_dot_type, nelements(src1)), plus CACHE_LINE_SIZE*nth of padding. (2) The route's independent witness is cpu_quant_reference_probe.cpp. It builds a single-node MUL_MAT graph with K=256 and ROWS=40, on the default 4-thread team for Q8_0 and 8 threads for F16/BF16. Take Q8_0 at width 5: wsize is 5*272 + 4*64 = 1616 B, while the predicate needs 4*1360 = 5440 B. F16 at width 5 has 3072 B against 20480 B needed. Every width from 2 to 8 falls back to HEAD's shared path, and so does every single-op test-backend-ops MUL_MAT case. The fixture passes against unchanged code, and the GDB entry hit on ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat fires whatever happens. (3) Serving is different. The verify graph contains FLASH_ATTN_EXT, whose prefill scratch is about 290 KB per thread at D=256, roughly 14 MB in total. That easily holds 48 * 5 * 10880 B = 2.6 MB for hc_down's Q8_0 K=10240 rows. So the new slice indexing, the wsize bound and the llamafile B-pointer offsets would run for the first time inside the timed A/B. (4) The falsifier promises 'frozen-request model identity'. The cpu_mul_mat_body route (gates.py) sets no model_identity, and run.py adds identity_reference only for routes that set it. That gate will not run, so the correctness half of the falsifier is empty. To resubmit, make the new path reachable by the route's own witness. One way: drop the dependence on wsize slack and give each thread private scratch that does not depend on the graph's wdata. For example, use a NEW file-scope static _Thread_local buffer that grows on demand. It is scratch, not a cache: no data-pointer key and nothing carried across evaluations. The fixture's widths 2-8 on its 4- and 8-thread teams then run the new path. Alternatively, cite a route whose gate exercises it. Also fix three secondary points. (a) The nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1 condition is needed only for the generic chunk-loop fallback. tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX::gemm4xN partitions statically by ith (sgemm.cpp:1550-1553). Float tinyBLAS sets its own chunk counter behind its own barrier (sgemm.cpp:614-617). Without --numa, ggml_is_numa() is false, so this condition needlessly excludes every Q8_0 node with ne0 >= 3072. Either justify the condition or limit it to the fallback. (b) Name the eligible served nodes. Q8_0 hc_attn/ffn_down [10240->320] lose a barrier. BF16 indexer.k_proj/q_proj still pay float tinyBLAS's internal barrier, so they gain nothing. (c) State the redundant-conversion cost at K=10240: each thread quantises 5 x 10240 floats (200 KB) instead of 1/48 of that. Keep the BE argument as it is: Q8_0, BF16 and F16 conversion is per-block or per-element, so whole-row and block-range from_float produce identical bytes. Keep the n>=5 serving A/B, the DS41 peer A/B and the kernel-preservation gate.

statement: In ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, extend the existing single-row private activation-quantization path to batches of 2-5 rows, only when existing wdata holds nth complete batch copies and nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1. Each thread converts all rows into its own disjoint slice using the existing from_float function and original source strides, then consumes that slice without the internal publication barrier. outcome.refusal_reason: One defect blocks this, and no gate can catch it: the allocation-failure fallback is decided per thread, but HEAD's shared path is a team-wide protocol. Each worker grows its own _Thread_local buffer, so malloc can fail on one thread and succeed on the others. As written, a failing thread drops into HEAD's shared path. It converts only its block range [ith*ne10/bs/nth, (ith+1)*ne10/bs/nth) into params->wdata and calls ggml_barrier (ggml-cpu.c:1485-1503). The other threads have skipped that barrier. In this OpenMP build ggml_barrier is a bare `#pragma omp barrier` (ggml-cpu.c:613). libgomp matches team barriers by generation, not by source location, so the failing thread's in-node barrier pairs with everyone else's node-end barrier (ggml-cpu.c:4546). From then on: (i) that thread runs tinyBLAS on a shared wdata that nobody else filled, so its output tiles are silently wrong; (ii) every later barrier in the graph is off by one for that thread, so publication between nodes is no longer ordered; (iii) the team either races or hangs at the end of the parallel region. The native suite, the scalar Q8_0 fixture, GDB entry and serving A/B never make malloc fail, so they cannot see this. To fix it, make every branch decision depend only on values every thread shares: src0/src1 types, ne10..ne13, src1 contiguity, ggml_cpu_rowexact_batch(ne11), nth. Treat a scratch allocation failure as fatal (GGML_ABORT/GGML_ASSERT, as ggml does for its own allocations). Never fall back per thread to a path that contains a team barrier. The llamafile-declines fallback is already safe on that test: llamafile_sgemm's Q8_0/Q4_0/IQ4_NL decision on x86 depends only on n, Ctype, Atype and Btype (sgemm.cpp:4165-4170, 4386-4396), which every thread shares, so all threads reach the current_chunk store and the barrier together. Keep that. Two minor points: size the scratch from ne11*ne12*ne13 rows and keep HEAD's (i12*ne11 + i13*ne12*ne11)*row_size B offsets. State the per-thread high-water bound: widths <= 8 at the largest eligible K, e.g. 8*10240*34/32 B = 87 KB at K=10240. Everything else in the hypothesis stands, as verified in source. Reachability: Q8_0 src0 with F32 src1 declines the first llamafile call (Btype != Q8_0, sgemm.cpp:4387). Since GGML_ROWEXACT_N defaults to 0 it reaches UseGgmlGemm1, so the probe's 4-thread Q8_0 team runs the new path at widths 2-8, and mm_batch1 still owns width 1. tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX partitions tiles statically by ith and has no barrier or chunk counter (sgemm.cpp:1548-1554), so dropping the nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1 condition outside the generic fallback is right. Aliasing: MUL_MAT is not in ggml_op_can_inplace (ggml-alloc.c:22-50), so dst never aliases src1. Without the barrier, one thread writing dst while another is still reading src1 is therefore safe. ggml_call_mul_mat (ops.cpp:7575-7615) passes src1 already in vec_dot_type, so it is unaffected. The BE-order argument holds: quantize_row_q8_0 is per block, and each tile's accumulation order and store are unchanged. In the resubmission, note that every Q8_0 dense MUL_MAT at N=5 is eligible, not only hc_down, and price the redundant conversion at the common K as well as K=10240. Also expect the integrity screen to flag the added `static` mutable state (hot_path_mutable_state). Keep the falsifier as written: the scalar fixture at widths 1-8, the candidate-DSO witness, no model-identity claim, >=5 serving pairs, the DS41 peer A/B and the kernel-preservation gate.

statement: In ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, give each worker private conversion scratch through a new static helper with a grow-on-demand _Thread_local buffer. For contiguous F32 activations converted to Q8_0 at widths 2-8, recompute all activation rows into that buffer on every invocation and attempt the existing llamafile GEMM without the shared-conversion barrier. Scratch is not a cache: no data-pointer key or activation reuse across evaluations. Allocation failure retains HEAD's shared path. If llamafile declines, initialize current_chunk and execute the existing team barrier before the generic fallback; the nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1 restriction is unnecessary for tinyBLAS's static tile ownership. Eligible served sites include Q8_0 hc_attn_down and hc_ffn_down [10240->320] at verify N=5. BF16 indexer projections are excluded because float tinyBLAS retains its internal barrier. The cost is substantial: each worker converts 5x10240 floats, reading 200 KiB rather than approximately 1/48 of that input. Expected benefit is removal of shared publication and its barrier, subject to that redundant-conversion cost. BE-order: whole-row and block-range Q8_0 conversion produce identical block bytes, and each output retains the same tinyBLAS accumulation and store order. Unlike the rejected wdata-slack design, private scratch makes this path reachable in the route's independent Q8_0 widths 2-8 fixture without changing graph scratch planning.

outcome.refusal_reason: The core premise is false in the selected source. The hypothesis says ssm_beta and ssm_alpha (F32 [2560 -> 48]) 'expose only six jobs each at verify N=5 under the existing tile plan'. Six jobs was the plan before the keep. HEAD contains 385998e10 (akm-cpu-float-narrow-m-column-jobs), which added a branch to float tinyBLAS::matmul at sgemm.cpp:504-508: when m%8==0, 2<=n<=5 and m/8 < nth, it calls mnpack<4,1,1>(m, n, 1, 1). ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat (ggml-cpu.c:1409-1410) calls llamafile_sgemm with m=ne01=48 and n=ne11=5. 48/16 = 3 < 48 skips the m%16 branch, and 48/8 = 6 < 48 takes the new one. gemm<4,1,1> (sgemm.cpp:599-609) then gives ytiles = 48/4 = 12, xtiles = 5, BN = 1, NB_BN = 5, so nb_job = 60 per node on the 48-thread team. No threads sit idle for the co-group to recover; the six-job figure belongs to the pre-keep mnpack<4,6,2> plan. What co-scheduling two 60-job nodes could still change: (a) the tail, where 12 of 48 threads run a second job, against ceil(60/g) rounds on a g-thread group; (b) one graph-node barrier saved per GDN layer, 36 per graph, plus internal tinyBLAS barriers made group-local. Item (b) is barrier-count reduction, which this lane has measured as noise at O(10-100) barriers, and the synchronization/barrier family is on the diminishing-returns list. The hypothesis prices neither and argues only a work-imbalance channel that the source shows does not exist. To resubmit: (1) Pick siblings whose job count at HEAD is really below nth, and show the plan arithmetic for each. Candidates include Q8_0 or other non-float siblings in the GDN or hc chains, and the census must run on HEAD's plans, not the pre-385998e10 ones. Alternatively, state the tail and barrier channel honestly and say why it differs from the barrier nulls already measured. (2) Say how group-local sync reaches inside tinyBLAS. Float gemm calls ggml_threadpool_chunk_set/add and ggml_barrier twice, all on params->threadpool (sgemm.cpp:614, 617, 643, 646). sgemm.cpp and ggml_threadpool_chunk_* are outside the cpu_graph_sched bodies. So each group needs its own threadpool-like object passed in params.threadpool, with ggml_barrier's body branching to a per-group atomic barrier. A shared current_chunk would let one group steal the other's jobs. (3) The two siblings are not adjacent in the builder: sigmoid(beta) is built between them (qwen4exp.cpp:1007-1014), so the census must look past intervening nodes. Check the real node order in the served graph too. (4) Note that no native suite or the fusion reference ever executes a co-group, because they are single-MUL_MAT graphs. Repeated model identity on this target and its peers is the only gate that runs the new path. The BE-order argument is fine as stated: each output keeps its gemm_bloc k-order whichever thread computes it.

statement: In ggml_graph_compute_thread, co-schedule independent small float MUL_MAT siblings, initially the Q38FN ssm_beta and ssm_alpha projections, on disjoint thread subgroups. Source inspection shows both read the same cur tensor and neither depends on the other's output. Their F32 [2560 -> 48] weights expose only six jobs each at verify N=5 under the existing tile plan. Concurrent execution can recover idle threads by overlapping these separate projections rather than refining their already-kept tile plan. This addresses work imbalance in the highest-ranked unresolved family; the rejected private-quantization and Q8 ownership mechanisms do not test it. Use separate subgroup scratch, counters and group-local synchronization, preserve publication before consumers, and retain HEAD's sequential walk for use_ref and unsupported shapes. SCHED is BE-order by construction: each output retains its original dot kernel and accumulation order; only its executing thread and overlap with independent work change. The 31.73% MUL_MAT wall share supports investigating this family but does not quantify these siblings' payoff.

statement: Use the admitted cpu_fa_schedule route to interleave two query heads sharing the same KV head and query position: walk KV cells once for the pair, maintaining separate Q conversions, softmax state and accumulators. HEAD currently completes one query row's entire KV walk before starting another. For Q38FN verify N=5, pairing its 24 heads yields 60 independent jobs, enough for the 48-thread team, while bringing both heads' accesses to each K/V cell together and sharing mask traversal where mask addresses coincide. Enable this only for compatible F16 layouts, non-tiled execution with split-KV disabled, and enough paired jobs to cover the team; retain HEAD otherwise and leave use_ref unchanged. BE by construction: each output row sees exactly the original ascending KV-cell sequence and unchanged dot, exp, accumulation, sink and overflow-replay arithmetic. This attacks GQA traversal rather than the exhausted prelude/barrier mechanisms. The short-request profiles do not establish an attention gain; the admitted long-context route motivates testing it without treating production context observations as measured speedups.

outcome.refusal_reason: The hypothesis puts the grouping inside ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_f16_one_chunk, but under the selected launch that function only ever receives one query row per call, so the new walk would never run in the A/B. The source arithmetic: the dispatcher at ops.cpp:10050-10100 orders rows with ir = iq1 + neq1*(iq2 + neq2*iq3). It sets chunk_size = ceil(nr/(4*nth)) and dr = ceil(nr/nchunk). If nchunk < nth it resets nchunk to nth, and ggml_is_numa() is false because the argv has no --numa. FLASH_ATTN_EXT gets n_tasks = n_threads = 48 (ggml-cpu.c:2980-2986). (a) Q38FN verify, N=5 with 24 query heads: nr = 120, chunk_size = ceil(120/192) = 1, nchunk = 120, dr = 1. (b) MTP draft steps, N=1: nr = 24, nchunk is reset to 48, dr = 1. (c) Decode at depth: GGML_FA_SPLIT_KV=0 gives the same dr = 1. Under SPLIT_KV=1 the split path calls one_chunk with exactly one q_head per call (ops.cpp:10033-10036). So every one_chunk call on the served 48-thread team walks the KV for a single row, and a group of query heads sharing a KV head never exists. Even when chunks hold several rows, iq1 varies fastest, so they are the tokens of ONE head, not several heads. On the gate's 7-thread team, Q38FN nb=5 gives dr = 5: the 5 tokens of a single head. Only the DS41 7-thread cases (dr = 3 or 7) span heads. The serving A/B and any long-context surface would therefore time the unchanged per-row walk, and the falsifier cannot attribute anything to the mechanism. To resubmit, put the mechanism in the dispatcher body as well (it is in cpu_fa_schedule scope). Make the work unit a (KV head ik2/ik3, row group): a group of rows that all share one KV head, across iq2 and iq1. Give the census and makespan for each served shape, using the current dynamic split as the baseline. For example, at Q38FN N=5 on 48 threads, HEAD runs 120 single-row items in 3 rounds. G = ceil(nr/nth) = 3 rows per item gives 40 items in one round with the same 3 row-walks of makespan, and each thread reads K/V once instead of three times. Each KV head has 60 rows, which divides by 3. Do the same for N=1 (24 rows, which leaves threads idle) and for DS41 (64 heads with 1 KV head, N=1 and N=3), and say how G is chosen for teams of other sizes. Keep everything else from HEAD per row: the HYBRID FP16 path, inline and straight-line, with each row's own end-of-row overflow check and a solo FP32 recompute only for a row that overflowed. Keep each row's own mask pointer and its GGML_FA_MASK_RUN / -INF skips: rows in a group have different iq1 and QSA masks, so skip a cell for a row only when HEAD would skip it for that row. Keep sinks, partials and the dst write. Size the G Q_q/VKQ buffers from params->wsize/nth, not from the fixed ith*(DK+2DV+CL) stride. Leave the use_ref path and the SPLIT_KV=1 chunk boundaries as HEAD has them. The BE argument stays valid as stated: each row sees the same cells in the same order through the same kq_vec_dot/expf/ggml_vec_mad_f16 sequence. Only which thread computes a row, and how rows interleave between cells, changes. Keep the falsifier unchanged: the cpu_fa_reference bit-identity gate, model identity, at least 5 serving pairs, and decode at depth when the long-context surface is on. Note that it must now include the served 48-thread shapes.

statement: Use the admitted cpu_fa_schedule route to interleave query-head accumulators sharing one KV head: traverse KV cells once per bounded group of query heads, updating each head separately. statement: In cpu_fa_schedule, change the non-reference, non-tiled, SPLIT_KV=0 dispatcher to schedule groups of query rows sharing one K/V head, with a new static grouped walker in the same file. outcome.refusal_reason: The mechanism prices work with a cost model that the kernel source contradicts, and on the profile's own evidence the change is expected to slow the slab. The proposal weights each active expert's row units by cne1, which assumes a row's cost is proportional to cne1. In mul_mat_qX_K_q8_K_IQ_N<DequantizerIQ3S, c> (iqk_gemm_iquants.cpp:779-819) a row actually costs D + c*K. D is paid once per row and shared by every activation column. For each 128 weights, prepare(i,j) runs two IndexHelperIQ3S::make2 calls. Those are 32 scalar index loads plus 32 scalar iq3s_grid loads, four _mm256_set_epi32 builds, sign_4_values and the min add: roughly 120-140 µops. K is the per-column cost in multiply_add (iqk_common.h:401): 4 q8 loads, 4 maddubs and 4 dpwssd, about 12-14 µops plus small per-block bsums/fmadd terms. So D/K is about 10 for IQ3_S, which is the only served expert type of any size that reaches this path. IQ4_NL down-experts are not in iqk_typeA_supported, and Q8_0 experts need GGML_IQK_Q8_0, which is off. With about 48 threads over about 30-45 active experts, most threads sit inside a single expert. HEAD's makespan is then about R*(D + c_max*K). Under cne1 weighting, threads in c=1 experts get m̄ times as many rows (m̄ = Σc/n_active), so the makespan is about m̄*R*(D+K). Weighting wins only when (m̄-1)*D < (c_max-m̄)*K. At D/K = 10 that requires m̄ < 1.09 when c_max=2, and m̄ < 1.36 even when c_max=5. The supplied profile points to overlap above that: mul_mat_qX_K_q8_K_IQ_N<IQ3S,2> takes 2.57% against 7.21% for IQ_1<IQ3S>. Because D dominates, per-row costs are nearly equal, so that ratio means roughly one c=2 group per three c=1 groups, i.e. m̄ ≈ 1.25. At that point the proposal costs about 1.25*11K = 13.75K per unit of rows against HEAD's 12K, a slab that is ~15% slower. The source therefore puts the sign of the treatment as stated at or below zero. A serving A/B would be testing an overcorrection, not imbalance removal. The falsifier names this risk, but naming it does not make the design sound. To resubmit: (1) Weight each expert by its estimated cost, w(c) = D_t + c*K_t, with small integer constants per weight type. Derive them from the kernel's µop counts or from a per-row timing of IQ_1 against IQ_N<c>, and state them for IQ3_S, IQ4_XS, and DS41's Q4_K/Q5_K, since the peer A/B runs those kernels. Keep shared integer boundaries rounded to slab_gran units, complete disjoint coverage, the every-thread kernel-selection pre-check, and all fallbacks. (2) Give the cne1 census at the served verify widths (2-5, from verify ids): n_active, m̄ and c_max. Use it to show the makespan of HEAD's equal-unit partition against the proposed one. (3) State the width gate: HEAD's slab covers ids->ne[1] 2..8, but the statement says N=2..5. The rest stands and should be kept. The BE-order argument is correct: iqk_mul_mat_moe_rows selects the same kernel per (typeA, Ny), and only the owning thread moves. The route is iqk_mmid_dispatch. The scalar fixture's alternating mode at odd widths produces unequal cne1 groups, so the new partition is exercised. Keep the candidate-DSO witnesses, at least 5 serving pairs, the DS41 peer A/B and the kernel-preservation gate.

statement: In ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat_id, change only the N=2..5 direct-kernel slab partition to weight each expert's row-granularity units by its matrix_row_counts multiplicity. The dequant cast cost exceeds the KV bandwidth saving even on the dense 27B (all-full-global KV, where the KV read most rivals weight bytes). statement: At batch-1 long context the KV read adds materially to bytes/token, so q8_0 KV-quant (-ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa 1) raises single-stream decode throughput.

outcome.refusal_reason: MEASURED NEGATIVE and mechanistically explained. The +9.823% proxy used a SYMMETRIC 64x64 tile grid where row-grouping has real headroom; the real MMQ surface is a batched pp=32 / tg=8 / pl=128 / n_kv=5120 decode whose tile grid is strongly M-heavy. With few N tiles the DEFAULT linear order already captures full activation reuse in a short window, so grouping M by 8-32 can only ENLARGE the concurrently-resident weight footprint -- predicting hit rate DOWN at flat read volume, which is exactly the measured -7.455 pts at +0.201% reads. Reinforcing: the CDNA MMQ path is PERSISTENT STREAM-K and already owns tile assignment (the r1 pilot was a literal no-op because the remap sat outside that path), and Q4_K decode weights stream with WGM0 hit rate already at 67.304%. Source: handoffs/active/autokernel-research-loop.md section 23.1 finding F3.

statement: Grouping MMQ tile rows (workgroup-mapping / swizzle, the G17 +9.823% proxy result) raises L2 hit rate and MMQ throughput on the real decode surface.

The current 32 contiguous 4-byte accesses already form coalesced 128-byte regions; widening each lane to 16 bytes does not reduce total HBM bytes or physical memory transactions, so a pure bandwidth-bound kernel cannot gain 30-60% from the claimed transaction-width effect. outcome.refusal_reason: The occupancy mechanism is not supported by the supplied profile. __launch_bounds__(256,2) specifies a minimum launchable residency, not a two-block cap, and no VGPR allocation or achieved-occupancy measurement shows that the current kernel is limited to two blocks/CU. Also, a reused single LDS buffer needs synchronization both before consumption and before the next token overwrites it; one __syncthreads per token permits an inter-token read/write race, so bit-identical output is not guaranteed. Each block contains exactly one 64-thread wave and processes exactly one 2048-element tile; different tiles are independent blocks and can execute concurrently, so the single barrier does not prevent the next tile's loads from issuing. Changing that barrier to wave scope is therefore semantically equivalent, and per-wave double buffering cannot overlap loads with conversion because one wave executes those instructions in lockstep unless a distinct producer wave or a supported asynchronous-copy primitive is specified. statement: The Q8_0 -> f16 staging converter (convert.cu:44, dequantize_block_q8_0_f16<need_check>, 10.66% of the live profile, 992 calls) is the biggest patchable symbol on this surface that has no prior attempt in the store. It is the producer of the f16 B-operand for the ~63% Tensile GEMM share: per call it runs one 64-lane wavefront per 2048-element tile, stages the full tile through LDS with scalar 4-byte global loads, then a __syncthreads that fully serializes the load phase against consumption, then 16 iterations of two 2-byte LDS reads (a broadcast scale and a char2, bank-conflicted at 2B granularity on the 32-bank gfx90a LDS), one __hmul2 and one 4-byte half2 store. Each tile is thus one barrier-serialized load->LDS->convert->store chain with the next tile's loads unable to issue until the previous tile's barrier clears, capping in-flight bytes per wave at one tile and leaving the kernel latency-limited rather than DRAM-limited; the need_check=true path (k % 2048 != 0, which is the rule at ne00=5120) adds a per-iteration bounds test to both loops on top. Restructure to a per-wave tile pipeline inside one block: each 64-lane wavefront owns one tile, double-buffers the LDS staging so tile t+1's global loads issue under tile t's convert/store, syncs only at wave scope instead of block scope, reads LDS at 4-byte granularity and stores 8 bytes per lane, and hoists the need_check bounds test out of the inner loop. The op is strictly elementwise (y[i] = d * qs in fp16), so any schedule that keeps that per-element multiply emits a bit-identical buffer: the MUL_MAT oracle is unaffected by construction and the run-9 failure class (shared dequantize.cuh, cross-TU ggml_cuda_cast, changed dispatch/type rows) does not apply, because kernel and launcher are static in convert.cu and only the Q8_0 row of the fp16 staging table selects them. It fires only on Q8_0 prefill (the confirm rung's and the profiled production model's staging path); the 1.5B screen never launches it, so a screen turn on this mechanism is compile/oracle smoke only.

statement: Rewrite dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 (convert.cu:44, the Q8_0 arm of ggml_get_to_fp16_cuda used by the fp16 batched-mul-mat path that feeds the Tensile GEMMs; 10.66% of the champion profile, 992 calls) so each 2048-value slab is decoded straight from global memory with zero-waste, naturally-aligned loads instead of the shipping LDS-staged shape: the current kernel reads 576 ints = 2304 B per 2176-B slab through a +WARP_SIZE-int lattice window (5.9% HBM read slack), stages it in __shared__ behind a __syncthreads, then runs 16 short dependent iterations that each re-read scale and qs from LDS and store one half2 per lane. New shape: tile the slab as 34-B block_q8_0 pairs; each 68-B pair tiles exactly into 17 aligned 4-byte dwords (pair base is 4-mod-4 under the same int-view assumption the shipping kernel already makes), so every qs byte and both 2-byte scales are fetched exactly once at full wave width (4 B/lane = 256 B per wave instruction). This removes the alignment trap that killed the previous char4 draft: no load is ever issued at a 2-mod-4 address (even-block payload bytes are reached through the pair's aligned dword lattice and redistributed in registers), so the code is legal on every backend convert.cu compiles for and needs no __HIPCC__ split. Each block's half scale is loaded once by the lane holding its dword and broadcast to the block's lanes via __shfl_sync (no per-lane scale re-read), LDS and the barrier are deleted, and stores stay coalesced half2 to y2[iy/2+t]. Per-element arithmetic is unchanged (__hmul2(make_half2(qs.x, qs.y), __half2half2(d))), so output is bit-identical and MUL_MAT numerics cannot move; the ragged tail keeps the existing need_check predicate. Faster if the kernel is issue/latency-bound rather than HBM-saturated (its ~128.4 ms over 992 calls implies sub-saturation): the rewrite cuts HBM reads ~5.9%, removes the barrier/LDS round trip, and shortens the load-to-store dependency depth per value. At 10.66% share a 15-20% kernel gain is ~2% device, above the 0.973% floor; if the kernel is already HBM-bound the gain caps near the traffic cut (~0.6% device) and the A/B records a bounded null.

statement: dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 is the largest patchable kernel below the vendor GEMM rows in the live pp512 profile of the current champion (10.66% of device time, 992 calls, ~129 us avg): the Q8_0-to-f16 staging dequant feeding the Tensile GEMMs on the production model (Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0). convert.cu:513-521 launches it as <<<num_blocks, WARP_SIZE>>> with WARP_SIZE=32 (common.cuh:46) even on HIP, and gfx90a executes wave64: every 32-thread block occupies a wavefront with lanes 32-63 idle, so each LDS-staging load and half2 store moves 128 B instead of 256 B per instruction and only ~1024 of 2048 lanes/CU can be resident (CDNA2 workgroup-slot granularity), leaving this streaming kernel at roughly 0.6 TB/s on 80 MB 5120-class slabs (all 992 calls take the need_check=false instantiation: k % 2048 == 0 exactly) - about 40% of HBM peak. Numerics are bit-identical: identical LDS contents, identical __hmul2(make_half2(qs.x, qs.y), __half2half2(d)) per element, identical output order; type selection and dispatch tables untouched. Carries forward the run-26 candidate akm-q8-0-f16-dequant-wave64-lanes, which was abandoned with no verdict when the champion advanced; the one Q8_0-dequant-family record (akm-q8-dequant-u16-half2, a different half2-packing mechanism) was A/B'd at dec-b4 where this kernel never dispatches under the champion's MMVQ routing, so that null is an observation-window miss, not evidence about lane width.

statement: gated_delta_net_cuda (13.62% of the live profile, 96 calls x 1.71 ms) assigns ONE 64-lane warp per state column (col = blockIdx.z*4 + threadIdx.y, block (64,4), grid.z = S_v/4 = 32), but its per-token k_t/q_t row vectors depend only on (head, seq, token), never on the column: lanes load rows i = lane, lane+64 identically in all 4 block warps and all 32 z-blocks, so per (head, seq, token) 128 warp-instances issue the same 512B k + 512B q global load streams (32x the unique 1KB/head/token), and each warp's kv-reduce/state-update/attn-reduce chain is a single dependent 6-step 64-lane butterfly with no intra-warp parallelism to hide shuffle and memory latency across the 512-token serial t-loop (recurrence on s_shard; launch_bounds only 8 wave64/SIMD). Per token: k/q load instructions and L1/L2 request streams fall 4x (128 -> 32 streams per head/seq/token) and the four independent kv/attn update+reduce chains interleave to hide the shuffle/load latency that paces the serial recurrence. outcome.refusal_reason: The scheduling/HBM premise is contradicted by the actual workload geometry and unsupported by the profile. Qwen3.8-27B has H=48 value heads and 16 q/k heads, not H=128; the current grid therefore has 1536 blocks, with same-head column groups 48 positions apart, and q/k are additionally shared across three value heads via iq1=h_idx%16. At the emitted 28 VGPRs and four waves/block, many column groups are resident concurrently, so the claim that each q/k pair misses to HBM about 32 times after 5+ separated generations is not established. The arithmetic is consequently wrong: raw q+k load requests are about 0.805 GB per kernel call and unique q+k data about 8.4 MB, not 2.0 GB and 150 MB; the supplied profile also gives 164163362 ns/96 = 1.71 ms per call, not 1.34 ms. Device time alone supplies no HBM or cache-miss evidence, and L2 retention cannot be inferred by dividing cache size by peak bandwidth. Reordering block indices may be testable, but the stated >=30% falsifier and 60-75% prediction do not follow from the available evidence. | The hotspot share is material and the experiment is falsifiable, but the bandwidth premise is unsupported. The 129 us figure is 128.4 ms / 992 aggregate invocations, while those invocations cover heterogeneous tensor and KV shapes; it cannot be combined with the bytes of one 5120x5120 tensor to infer ~630 GB/s. The existing loads are also fully coalesced at 32 lanes x 4 B = 128 B per instruction, so scalar load width does not establish half-rate HBM transactions, and the proposed staging still performs the same LDS write/read round trip per input byte. Full-wave execution may reduce issued instructions and inactive-lane work, but the claimed memory-bandwidth cause and 20-40% prediction need dispatch-size-correlated timings or memory/issue counters. Also, MUL_MAT alone does not cover the stated quantized-KV FA route. Reframe the mechanism around wave issue efficiency, provide shape-specific timing evidence, and add correctness coverage for every affected route. | Already measured. Commit 719a8529d and upstream PR #24561 implement this same non-KDA, S_v=128 FLA-style chunked GDN prefill mechanism with tiled GEMMs, triangular solve, chunk-state propagation, and recurrent decode fallback. On gfx90a, the 512-token kernel was measured at 1253.73 us recurrent versus 1009.67 us chunked, with full-model prefill gains also recorded. Prior tuning found C=16 fastest; larger chunks lost to CxC work and gfx90a's 64 KB LDS limit. Re-running the mechanism against a newer champion would be a replication, not a new hypothesis.

statement: gated_delta_net_cuda<128,false,false,float> is the top patchable row on the live profile (13.62%, 96 calls, 164163362 ns/96 = 1.71 ms per call) and it walks a strictly serial recurrence: the grid is (H=48, n_seqs, 32 column-groups) = 1536 blocks, and every block loops t = 0..n_tokens-1 (512 at pp512), doing per step two dependent 64-lane warp_reduce_sum chains plus a broadcast (kv_col, then attn_col) around the rank-1 state update s_c(t) = g_t(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) s_c(t-1) + beta_t k_t v_t[c]. The per-call work is of order 1.6e9 FMAs (tens of us) plus tens of MB of unique traffic (state 2x ~3 MB, q/k/v/y streams), so the measured 1.71 ms per call is structural serial latency (roughly 512 steps x a ~1000+ cycle dependent shuffle chain x residency rounds), not work. The mechanism is the standard chunked transform of this linear recurrence family, which the kernel file itself flags as the intended next step ('TODO: Add chunked kernel for even faster pre-fill', ggml/src/ggml-cuda/gated_delta_net.cu:191): split the token axis into chunks of C tokens; compute once per (head, chunk) the chunk transition and the chunk-decayed key products from k/g/beta (shared by all 32 column-group blocks of that head, which currently re-derive the same S_v-dim products per block per token); then each block needs only n_tokens/C inter-chunk propagation steps (each a few independent S_v-dim matvecs whose shuffle latency overlaps across columns/dots) plus C-parallel intra-chunk output math. The serial chain collapses from 512 dependent reduce/broadcast hops per block to ~8-16, attacking exactly the residue that dominates per-call time. Only prefill launches (n_tokens >> 1; the hot instantiation has keep_rs=false so no per-token state snapshots are needed) take the chunked path; n_tokens=1 decode keeps the existing kernel byte-for-byte. Algebraically the chunked form is the identical recurrence re-expressed (fp32 reassociation only), so the numerics statement is a reordering, and test-backend-ops has test_gated_delta_net cases as the correctness gate.

statement: In gated_delta_net_cuda<128,false,false,float> (13.62% of the pp512 profile, 96 calls, 1.71 ms each, a 512-token serial recurrence) every wave owns one state column and per token runs TWO dependent warp_reduce_sum<64> shuffle ladders: kv = sum_i S[i]*k[i], then - after the state update S' = g*S + k*delta - a second ladder for attn = sum_i S'[i]*q[i]. The second ladder does not need the updated state: attn = sum_i (g*S[i] + k[i]*delta)*q[i] = g*(S.q) + delta*(k.q). Accumulate the three lane-local sums A = S.q, B = k.q, C = S.k over the pre-update state and pass ONE 6-step ds_bpermute ladder (3 values) per token; then delta = (v[col] - g*C)*beta, attn = g*A + delta*B, and the state update runs off the attention path. This removes one full dependent shuffle ladder plus the dependent update FMAs from the per-token critical chain (~35-45% of its length, verified algebraically to ~2e-11 relative in fp32; the recurrence state is bit-identical, only the attn output aggregation is reassociated, inside test-backend-ops tolerance). Non-KDA branch only (the profiled instantiation); KDA/keep_rs, grid, launch, dtype untouched - type-selection/dispatch rows untouched. This re-forms the superseded akm-gdn-single-phase-triple-reduce (never measured; champion advanced at keep time) against champion b0eb4fab4. The recorded GDN nulls (register prefetch +0.305%, halfwave-pack +0.79%, two-col-wave, eight-lane) were A/B'd on dec-b4 of Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0, a surface that never dispatches the GDN kernel - observation-window misses, not evidence, per the loop's own rule.

statement: dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 (convert.cu:43-82, launched with 32 threads/block at :517) is the CUDA-legacy B-operand dequant that materializes the f16 operand for the Tensile HSS GEMMs: 10.66% of the live profile (992 calls), the biggest fully-ours slice behind the ~62% vendor wall, and untouched by every prior keep (git history on convert.cu is upstream-only). It is structurally wrong for gfx90a in three compounding ways: (1) blocks are WARP_SIZE=32 threads (common.cuh:46) on a 64-lane-wavefront machine, so every global/LDS instruction issues on a half-masked wave; (2) the 34-byte q8_0 blocks are staged through LDS plus __syncthreads (:52-64) purely to dodge misalignment on CUDA - a barrier round trip and LDS traffic the direct path does not need; (3) output is one 4-byte half2 store per lane per iteration (:76) with the scale re-read from LDS every iteration. Rewrite as a 256-thread (4x wave64), LDS-free kernel: aligned 4B/16B windowed loads of the raw quant stream into registers (windows straddle the 34B block boundaries; scale extracted per window and exchanged by wave shuffle), per-element f16(d)*f16(q) kept bit-identical - the operation is a pure elementwise broadcast multiply with no reduction or reassociation, so MUL_MAT numerics are unchanged by construction, answering the run-9 dequant-path hazard - and output written with 8B-per-lane f16 stores. The kernel today moves its 1.06B-read/2B-written-per-weight profile at well under gfx90a achievable bandwidth; removing half-idle waves, the barrier, and scalar-width store issue should recover ~20-50% of kernel time, i.e. ~2-5% of this surface, 2-5x the prefill floor.

outcome.refusal_reason: The mechanism is unsupported and its source accounting is incorrect. The current tile contains exactly 64 * 34 = 2176 input bytes (544 ints), not 2304 bytes or 576 ints; the extra WARP_SIZE term accounts for the 128 scale bytes, not HBM over-read. WARP_SIZE is 32, so the launch is a 32-thread block, not a 64-thread block. More importantly, assigning one whole 34-byte q8_0 block to each lane makes corresponding dword loads stride by 34 bytes and 8-byte stores stride by 64 bytes across the wave, replacing the current contiguous, coalesced lane accesses with scattered transactions. The claimed eight aligned q-loads are also impossible generally because packed 34-byte blocks alternate modulo-4 alignment and qs begins at offset 2. Multi-wave tiles do not repair that access pattern. Finally, the proposed first falsifier is the missing evidence: no MemUnit/STREAM measurement currently establishes the asserted half-copy-class bandwidth or that LDS/barrier serialization is the limiter. Run that probe first, then reformulate around a coalesced direct-load/store mapping if it shows headroom. | The proposed transform is not algebraically supported as written. Per state column, the recurrence is s_t = g_t(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T)s_{t-1} + beta_t v_t k_t, so chunk propagation requires products of token-dependent rank-1 matrices, not merely prefix products of scalar g_t and precomputed <s_start,k_t> terms. The hotspot profile establishes importance but supplies no stall/latency evidence showing serial depth, rather than memory traffic, is limiting; the proposed rocprof pass is prerequisite evidence, not a post-patch falsifier. | The 64-thread re-tile now preserves contiguous loads, stores, and element mapping, but the required prerequisite evidence is still missing. Moving that probe into the falsifier does not satisfy the prior instruction to run it before reformulating. statement: dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 (convert.cu:44, 10.66% of the live profile, 992 calls at ~129.4 us each on the pp512 surface) is launched as 32-thread CTAs (convert.cu:517) on gfx90a, whose physical wavefront is 64 lanes (common.cuh:366). statement: dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 (convert.cu:44, launched with WARP_SIZE=32 threads = a HALF-populated wave64 on gfx90a) stages one 2048-element tile through LDS with 17 rounds of scalar 4-B global loads per lane and drains it with 32 rounds of one 4-B half2 store plus two LDS reads per lane. Every global/LDS instruction this kernel issues moves data for only 32 of 64 lanes, and each instruction transfers at most 128 B (4-B/lane). The kernel is instruction-slot/LDS-pipe-bound, not DRAM-bound: ~130 memory instructions per tile (49 global + 81 LDS) moving 2176 B in + 4096 B out. Fix: keep the LDS-staging structure and the exact per-element scale*qs multiply (bit-identical output, no arithmetic touched, no type-selection change), but run each block as ONE FULL 64-thread wave64 covering TWO consecutive 2048-element tiles (4352 B in, 8192 B out). Geometry is exact: 2 tiles = 1088 ints = 17 ints/lane -> 4 rounds of alignment-safe int4 global loads (16 B/lane, 1024 B contiguous per wavefront round; tile stride 2176 B is a multiple of 16, so every 2-tile base is 16-B aligned) plus one 4-B tail round; output = 2048 half2 over 64 lanes = 32 half2/lane -> 16 rounds of half4 (8-B) global stores (512 B contiguous per round; y base 16-B aligned, half4 never crosses a 32-element block boundary). LDS reads keep the existing 2-B char2/scale access class (no new bank-phase hazard), and with a single wavefront per block __syncthreads is still free. This cuts the memory-instruction count per byte roughly 3x (34->5 staging instructions per 2 tiles, 64->16 store rounds, full-lane payloads on every DS/vmem slot) and halves the wavefront count the GPU must schedule for the same bytes. Launcher (dequantize_block_q8_0_f16_cuda, convert.cu:513) keeps need_check=true fallback for k % 4096 != 0, matching the existing fast/slow split at k % 2048. statement: Restructure the token loop of gated_delta_net_cuda (the <128,false,false,float> instantiation, 13.62% / 96 calls, the largest patchable kernel in the live profile) so the post-update attention reduction no longer sits on the recurrent critical path. Today each token serially executes: reduce_kv (6-level 64-lane shfl_xor) -> delta = (v - g*kv)*beta -> s_shard = g*s_shard + k_reg*delta -> reduce_attn (another 6-level shfl_xor) -> store: two dependent full-warp shuffle chains straddle every recurrence step, with only ~6 FMAs/lane between them, and the state stays register-resident across the (n_tokens=512) loop so per-token state BW is zero. Use the identity attn = (g*s + k*delta) dot q = g*(s dot q) + delta*(k dot q): accumulate a_shard = s_shard*q_reg and b_shard = k_reg*q_reg alongside kv_shard = s_shard*k_reg, run the three reductions concurrently (all depend only on pre-update values), then after delta arrives update s_shard as before and have lane 0 store g*a_col + delta*b_col. Only reduce_kv remains on the delta->s' recurrence chain, cutting one 6-level shuffle reduction (~half the serial depth) out of every one of the 512 iterations. kv, delta and the s_shard recurrence are bit-identical (same per-lane FMA products, same reduce order); only the fp32 association of the output dot changes (~1 ulp), so the oracle is the ordinary one. Why this family and not memory: the champion's memory-side variants on this kernel all measured null (coltile +0.084%, shared q/k loads, register prefetch), and here the sequential t-loop holds the whole state in registers, so the residual structural cost per token is exactly the two dependent 64-lane shuffle chains; a 64-lane reduce costs 6 shfl levels on gfx90a, and S_v=128 with warp=64 leaves only 2 rows/lane between reductions. KDA=true analog: attn = sum(e_i*s + k*delta)*q distributes the same way with e_i = expf(g_i) reused from the update, no extra expf.

The Q4_K pp512 FORCE_MMQ null (+0.105%, screen rung) does not settle this leg: it was gated by the :309 K-type special-case and measured on the Q4_K screen model, and the seed's own rung tag states the Q8_0 confirm-rung question is unmeasured; a null here is still the bounded answer that closes the seed.

statement: On the current champion's pp512 profile (Q8_0-dominant hybrid), `dequantize_block_q8_0_f16` (convert.cu:44) is the second-largest in-tree kernel at 10.66% / 992 calls / ~129 us each, and it is launched with 32-thread blocks (convert.cu:517/520, `WARP_SIZE` = 32, common.cuh:46) on a wave64 device: each CDNA2 wave is formed per workgroup, so every wavefront executes with 32 of 64 lanes idle. The kernel is store-dominated (it writes 64 B of f16 per 34 B of q8_0 read), and its aggregate achieved bandwidth over the profile period is ~670-810 GB/s, roughly half of the write-mixed roofline of a 1.6 TB/s part - the signature of half-width LSU wavefronts (each global store retires 128 B instead of 256 B per wave). Mechanism: widen the launch to one full wave64 per block (64 threads, still one 2048-element tile per block) and re-parameterize the kernel's two `WARP_SIZE`-stride loops (LDS staging at convert.cu:55, store loop at convert.cu:67, plus the `+WARP_SIZE` staging margin) onto `blockDim.x`, which is thread-count-agnostic and therefore bit-identical to today on CUDA (32-thread warps) and on gfx90a for every element: the per-element formula (scale d and char2 qs index are pure functions of the output element index e = iy + 2*threadIdx.x) is unchanged, so values, order and the `__hmul2` math are byte-identical - no numerics drift, no MUL_MAT risk, no type/dispatch change. Halving the wavefront count and issuing full-width 256 B stores should roughly double kernel throughput if it is LSU-issue-limited rather than DRAM-limited. This kernel has never been touched by the loop (no AutoKernel commit touches convert.cu), it is not the run-9 shared-header trap (local edit, no new cross-TU calls), and it is not the prefetch family that measured net-negative.

Mechanism: (1) extend the Q8_0 case in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq (mmvq.cu, the b0eb4fab4 site) from ne11<=4 to ne11<=8 so dense Q8_0 at the spec-width dec-b8 is served by the multi-column mul_mat_vec_q templates; and (2) extend the y-stream-amortize rows_per_cuda_block rule in calc_rows_per_block (mmvq.cu:807, currently restricted to GCN && GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 && ncols_dst==4 && !small_k) to ncols_dst==8, with the same rpb=4 -> r2_fallback guard for nrows_x%4!=0 that the champion added for ncols_dst==4. The rows-per-block doubling cuts the per-block re-read of the 4/8-column q8_1 activation row from ~2.1x to ~1.06x of weight bytes (the champion's own kept-comment arithmetic), raising the kernel's L2-read ceiling toward the ncols_dst=1 kernel's. The two b8 routing nulls this epoch (akm-cdna2-q8-b8-mmvq-route -0.233%, b8 mmq crossovers) were measured on dec-b4 windows where a ne11 in 5..8 gate never engages (their records cite the 1.142% dec-b4 floor, not the 1.753% dec-b8 floor), so the dec-b8 MMQ-vs-MMVQ-rpb4 comparison has never been measured where it runs. Pure launch/dispatch change: no weight or activation arithmetic is altered, per-element fp32 dots are unchanged, and only the cross-thread accumulation grouping of an already-existing kernel moves, exactly as in the two kept predecessors.

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured. The identical pre-update triple reduction and algebraic attention reconstruction were implemented as akm-gdn-single-round-reduce (+0.253%) and akm-gdn-preupdate-attn-single-reduce (-0.166%); both were inside the 1.142% floor. Extending the same algebra to KDA does not distinguish the profiled hot instantiation <128,false,false,float>. If kernel-level pp512 timing is still desired, re-profile the preserved patch rather than writing it again. | Already measured as akm-gdn-next-token-register-prefetch. Its preserved patch performs the same one-token-ahead register double-buffering of k/q/v/beta/g in gated_delta_net_cuda while preserving arithmetic and reduction order; it passed compile/correctness and measured +0.305% over 5 alternating Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0 pairs, inside the 1.142% floor. The stale epoch preserves the fact that this mechanism was tried. If pp512 kernel timing is still wanted, re-profile the preserved patch rather than write it again. | Already measured. Commit 719a8529d / upstream PR #24561 implemented the same non-KDA, S_v=128 chunked GDN prefill using tiled GEMMs, a lower-triangular solve, chunk-state propagation, and recurrent fallback. On gfx90a at 512 tokens, kernel time fell only from 1253.73 us to 1009.67 us (about 1.24x), failing this hypothesis's required >=2x speedup; prior tuning found chunk size 16 fastest. The proposed algebra is also incorrect: for d_t = beta_t(v_t - g_t kv_t), the coupling coefficient is beta_t*g_t*G_{i+1,t-1}(k_i.k_t), not beta_i*g_i*G_{i+1,t-1}(k_i.k_t), and the nilpotent identity is (I+W)^-1 = (I-W)(I+W^2)(I+W^4)..., not the stated plus-first product.

statement: gated_delta_net.cu:74-169 runs the decode-style sequential token loop even when one call carries a whole prefill ubatch (the profiled row gated_delta_net_cuda<128,false,false,float> = 13.62% of device time, 96 calls at pp512). Each token walks a dependent chain - expf, a 64-lane warp_reduce for kv, the rank-1 state rewrite, a second warp_reduce for attn - repeated L times, leaving ~1-2 warps/SIMD (the grid is only H x 32 blocks), so wall time scales as L x chain latency, not as parallel work. The three measured-null GDN micro-opts attacked the per-step constant, not the chain length; the file's own TODO ('Add chunked kernel for even faster pre-fill') names this gap. For the scalar-gated KDA=false case the chunk is exactly solvable: with G_t the scalar cumprod of exp(g_t), kv_t = G_{1,t-1} S0^T k_t + sum_{i<t} G_{i+1,t-1} (k_i.k_t) d_i and o_t = g_t G_{1,t-1} S0^T q_t + g_t sum_{i<t} G_{i+1,t-1} (k_i.q_t) d_i + (k_t.q_t) d_t, where d_i = beta_i (v_i - g_i kv_i). The intra-chunk delta coupling is a strictly-lower-triangular (hence nilpotent) matrix W with W_{t,i} = G_{i+1,t-1} beta_i g_i (k_i.k_t), so the per-position solve is (I+W)^-1 rhs and, since W^L = 0, (I+W)^-1 = (I+W)(I+W^2)(I+W^4)... computed in ~2*log2(L) dense LxL products per head instead of an L-deep dependent walk. Every heavy step - the S0-fed contractions, the masked decay-weighted Gram, the two interaction GEMMs, the final state S_L = G_{1,L} S0 + sum_i G_{i+1,L} k_i d_i^T - is a dense [L x S_v] or [S_v x S_v] contraction parallel over heads and rows, keeping the existing transposed state layout and changing numerics only by fp32 summation order. Implementation is a new sibling kernel plus a dispatch branch in launch_gated_delta_net, active only for KDA=false, keep_rs=false and large n_tokens; the n_tokens=1 decode path and the keep_rs snapshot path keep the existing sequential kernel unchanged (guards, not payoff).

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured on the current epoch: the identical Q8_0 CDNA2 pp512 MMQ routing change produced -0.190%, inside the calibrated 1.142% floor, and was recorded as a measured null. | Already measured on the current epoch. akm-q8-dequant-f16-wave64-lanes tested the same 32-to-64-lane dequant launch mechanism and measured -0.179%, inside the 1.142% floor. The 4096-element/full-wave variant akm-q8dequant-tofp16-fullwave64 also measured +0.021%, inside the same floor. These bounded nulls directly falsify the claimed wave-issue bottleneck; the separate Q8_0 MMQ-routing null is not needed for rejection. | The profile establishes only that gated_delta_net_cuda is hot; it does not establish the claimed q/k refetch bottleneck. A fresh 1 KB row per token implies compulsory misses for the first accessor, not that all four neighboring warps miss L1 or generate four independent L2 reads. Their identical, near-concurrent accesses may be cache hits or merged requests. Also, safe single-buffer LDS reuse requires synchronization both before overwriting the buffer and after loading it, adding two block barriers per serial token step; the statement accounts for only one and does not bound that cost. Run the proposed L2/cache-policy or timing probe first and show approximately four independent q/k fetches per block, or revise the mechanism to target demonstrated load-instruction/L1 pressure rather than asserted L2 latency.

statement: gated_delta_net_cuda (13.62%, 96 calls, 128.4 ms - the largest patchable our-source slice after this epoch's bounded nulls on the Q8_0 dequant/MMQ levers) refetches the full per-head q/k row pair (128+128 floats = 1 KB) on every one of the 128 column-warps of each (head, token): q_t/k_t addresses depend only on (seq, t, head) (gated_delta_net.cu:75-76) and not on col = blockIdx.z*4+threadIdx.y, and the four warps inside each block (blockDim = 64x4) read identical bytes. Because the t-loop streams a fresh 1 KB per token, each warp's 4 loads miss L1 every token, so the ~L2 latency sits on the serial per-token chain (load -> kv 6-hop reduce -> delta -> s update -> attn 6-hop reduce) of every column-warp, and the same lines are requested ~4x per block from L2. Fix: stage the token's q/k rows in LDS once per block per token (single warp cooperative load, ~1 KB static shared, stride-1 conflict-free), __syncthreads, and let all four column-warps source k_reg/q_reg from LDS (~25 cyc, deterministic) instead of global. This dedups the block's identical line fetches, cuts L2 read traffic ~4x on the dominant q/k stream, and removes the L1-miss latency from the per-token critical path. FP is bit-identical: staged values are the same bytes, per-lane partials and the 64-lane butterfly are unchanged, so the ordinary test-backend-ops oracle applies (not a MUL_MAT-path change). Decode dispatches (state-HBM-bound, n_tokens small) are touched only benignly; the win is on the prefill-shaped ~1.34 ms/dispatch instances in the profile.

statement: The current champion's bs=1 decode profile is Q8_0 GEMV (mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,1> fused 46.25% + plain 29.33%) with one quantize_q8_1_1d launch per GEMV (5.58% of device time; 55,857 calls = exactly the 55,857 mul_mat_vec_q calls), because ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q's requant-elision cache (mmvq.cu:2118-2119) whitelists only GGML_TYPE_Q4_K/Q6_K (the screen rung it was measured on, +2.135%/+1.315% tg128 keeps). Within one captured HIP graph, dense-attention q/k/v/o projections multiply the identical layer-input tensor, so 4 bit-identical f32->q8_1 conversions of the same bytes are issued per layer. Extending the eligibility whitelist to GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 makes the 2nd..4th consumers of a shared src1 reuse the 1st consumer's quantize-node output: the cache key is the src1 tensor identity+shape+layout and is valid only within one capture_id, the elided kernel's output is bit-identical, and the captured graph's node dependencies keep the mmvq kernels ordered after the one surviving quantize node on every replay (fresh content every token, no staleness possible). This deletes roughly 3 of every ~6 requant dispatches per layer on the Q8_0 decode path - the same class of fixed per-op launch+small-kernel tax the Q4_K keep already removed - with zero change to any kernel numerics.
