statement: The live profile is a Q8_0 bs=1 decode: mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0> is 75.25% (18,576 fused + 37,281 plain calls) and quantize_q8_1_1d is 5.80% at exactly 55,857 calls, i.e. ONE 4.6us activation re-quantize launch per MMVQ launch, each on the serialized per-layer decode chain. The champion already owns a q8_1 graph-reuse cache built to collapse exactly this 1:1 pairing for matmuls that share a src1 activation column (kept dd161d519 +2.135%, c0d42d81c +1.315%), but its eligibility gate at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu:2119 whitelists only Q4_K/Q6_K, a 1.5B-Q4_K-era choice; Q8_0, the workload this profile was taken on, is excluded. Dense decode graphs give q/k/v the identical attention-norm output column (same src1 ggml tensor and pointer), so per layer q/k/v currently fire 3 identical f32->q8_1 quantizations where 1 suffices. Mechanism: add GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 to the cache_eligible type list under the existing guards (ne11==1, ne12/ne13==1, ids==null, stream 0, capture active). At capture time the shared src1 then records ONE quantize node; every replay executes it once and all consumers (q, k, v) read that single q8_1 buffer, dropping quantize launches toward the unique-src1 count (qkv triples collapse 3:1) and removing the redundant global round trips. Numerics are bit-identical: the surviving quantize is the same kernel on the same f32 input, so every consumer sees exactly the bytes it computes today; no kernel body, layout, rounding or dispatch-of-dot change, so the MUL_MAT oracle risk class is empty. Expected ~1.0-2.5% on tg128 (each collapsed 4.6us launch removed from the per-layer critical path; collapse ratio is graph-topology-bound, measured not assumed), measured against champion 445e93a8c at 20 alternating pairs.

outcome.refusal_reason: Baseline gfx90a ISA already compiler-CSEs the shared Q8_1 operand in the fused Q8_0 kernel: one activation dwordx2 load and one activation-scale load feed both output and gate dp4a chains. The source also computes kby/kqs once outside both calls. A dual helper therefore would not remove the claimed duplicated activation loads, scale read, or index derivation; only the distinct output/gate weight loads remain. | Already measured as akm-q4k-cta-q8-fused-prologue and akm-q4k-inline-q8-active-mask-all-routes, with severe decode regressions. The unchanged flaw is cross-CTA duplication: the standalone kernel quantizes each activation once globally, while this design requantizes the full activation independently in every output-row CTA, potentially hundreds or thousands of times per MUL_MAT. LDS only shares within a CTA, and overlap with weight loads does not restore cross-CTA reuse. Extending the same mechanism to Q6_K does not address that failure. | The proposed fallback is not implementable by mirroring the b4 cell: for ncols_dst==1, small_k=true returns nwarps, which is 4 for Q8_0 on GCN, not the current R=1. Adding the stated !small_k cell therefore leaves no R=1 instantiation for nrows_x%4!=0 and risks out-of-bounds rows unless a separate template discriminator is designed. Also, MMVQ_PARAMETERS_GCN covers GCN and all CDNA generations, not CDNA2 alone, contradicting the claimed architecture scope. Restate an explicit CDNA2-only selection and a concrete R=1 fallback path.

statement: Rows 1-2 of the champion profile are mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0, ncols_dst=1> decode (fused 46.01% + plain 29.24%); on gfx90a both launch one output row per 256-thread CTA (calc_rows_per_block returns 1 for Q8_0 ncols_dst=1 non-small_k), so every row-CTA re-reads the whole Q8_1 activation vector (y = ~1.125 B/weight incl. ds, vs 1.0625 B/weight for x) from L2/L1 and pays the full 4-warp LDS cross-warp reduction + syncthreads + address prologue once per row. Change: add a CDNA2 (GCN-table) cell returning rows_per_cuda_block=4 for type==Q8_0 && ncols_dst==1 && !small_k, with a host-side nrows_x%4==0 gate (fall back to the current R=1 launch otherwise), exactly mirroring the kept akm-cdna2-q8-b4-y-stream-amortize cell (ncols_dst==4, +10.098% dec-b4) which added rows=4 to amortize the same y re-read. With R=4 each thread's fixed k-chunk iterates 4 output rows, making the y-block loads (same y address across the unrolled row loop, independent of row index) structurally CSE-able per k-step - the identical compiler-CSE property already proven for the shared Q8_1 operand in the fused gate kernel - cutting per-row y L1/L2 load traffic ~4x (1.06x to ~0.27x of weight bytes) and amortizing the cross-warp reduction ceremony and block prologue over 4 rows; x HBM traffic, per-row k-order and the butterfly per-row reduction are unchanged, so each output is bit-identical to today and test-backend-ops (1139/1139) is untouched. One cell in calc_rows_per_block covers both the fused and plain instantiations (both go through calc_launch_params); no other quant/width/arch is affected, and this is not the settled LDS-prefetch mechanism (no DMA, no buffers).

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured. akm-q4k-cta-q8-fused-prologue implemented this same F32-to-Q8_1 per-CTA LDS prologue, skipped quantize_q8_1_1d, and regressed tg128 by 59.182%; the closely related akm-q4k-inline-q8-active-mask-all-routes regressed by 61.926%. LDS is CTA-local, so the activation is redundantly requantized once per output-row CTA rather than once per matmul, and that cost was not hidden by weight-load latency. | The proposed one-table-row change is not safe for general Q8_0 ncols_dst=1 calls. With R=2 or R=4 and nrows_x not divisible by R, the final CTA still executes vec_dot_q_cuda for every rows_per_thread entry and reads weight rows past nrows_x; only the final stores are bounds-checked. The existing ncols_dst=4 optimization required an explicit host fallback for exactly this reason. Revise the hypothesis to include an analogous ncols_dst=1 tail fallback or guarded valid-row loads. Also correct the byte accounting: at K=5120, Q8_1 y is 5760 B versus 5440 B for Q8_0 weights. | The widened route exposes Q8_0 ncols_dst=5..8 templates to general CDNA2 MUL_MAT calls without a tail fallback. On the GCN table these templates use rows_per_thread=2, but their weight loads are not guarded by nrows_x; only stores are bounds-checked. An odd nrows_x therefore makes the final CTA read a weight row past the logical tensor. Add an R=1 tail fallback or guarded valid-row loads before widening the dispatch. | The widened route exposes Q8_0 ncols_dst=5..8 templates on CDNA2 without the required tail fallback. These GCN templates use rows_per_thread=2, while weight loads are not guarded by nrows_x; for odd nrows_x, the final CTA can read one weight row past the logical tensor. Add an R=1 tail fallback or guard valid-row loads before widening the dispatch.

statement: On gfx90a the CDNA2 branch of ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq routes Q8_0 decode to MMVQ only at ne11<=4; ne11 5..8 (the MTP verify widths; dec-b8 is n-max 8) falls through to MMQ's mul_mat_q, which pads to J=8 and runs occupancy-1 128-row stream-k tiles that re-read weight tiles per output column. Raise the Q8_0 bound from 4 to MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE (8) so ne11 5..8 MUL_MATs take the existing multi-column mul_mat_vec_q templates, where each quantized weight block is loaded once and accumulated into ncols_dst register accumulators, amortizing the HBM weight stream across the verify batch. This is the same dispatch-only mechanism as the kept Q4_K ne11<=8 crossover (7d2ea88b, +5.097%) and the kept Q8_0 ne11<=4 route (b0eb4fab4, +23.339%); the 'July crossover' that parked Q8_0 ne11>=5 on MMQ predates both keeps and the ncols_dst 5..8 Q8_0 templates have never been A/B'd against MMQ at these widths on CDNA2. One constant changes; no kernel body is touched; both kernels are oracle-correct, so the ordinary MUL_MAT oracle applies and the diff cannot creep.

outcome.refusal_reason: The profile does not support the proposed scope: both dominant symbols are mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8>, which is Q8_0; Q4_K and Q6_K are enum values 12 and 14. More fundamentally, quantize_q8_1_1d quantizes each activation once per matmul, while the resulting small Q8_1 row is reused by every output-row CTA and can remain cached. The proposed prologue would instead repeat the full quantization in every CTA and read the 4x larger F32 activation row per CTA, so the claimed removal of a serialized 5.8% cost ignores substantially duplicated work. The implementation description is also inconsistent: register-resident Q8_1 blocks cannot enter the existing vec-dot loop unchanged because it consumes block_q8_1 pointers. This needs reformulation around the actual Q8_0 hotspot and a reuse strategy that quantizes once, not once per output CTA. | Already measured and present in the current champion. Commit 1e44b833 changed CDNA2 Q8_0, ncols_dst=1 from nwarps=2 to 4, which on wave64 is exactly 128 to 256 threads (2 to 4 waves), and measured 28.99 to 30.32 t/s (+4.6%) on the 27B Q8_0 single-stream surface with MUL_MAT 1103/1103 passing. The current code already returns 4 for this route; its nwarps counts physical wave64 warps, so the statement's nwarps=4=128-thread premise is incorrect. A literal nwarps=8 would be 512 threads, and that point was also tested and lost to nwarps=4 due to reduction overhead. | The proposed fallback is invalid: for GCN Q8_0 with ncols_dst=1, calc_nwarps returns 4 and calc_rows_per_block(..., small_k=true, nwarps=4) also returns 4, not R=1. Thus rows not divisible by 4 can still read past the final row. Also, MMVQ_PARAMETERS_GCN covers GCN and all CDNA generations, so a calc_rows_per_block table entry is not CDNA2-only. This same four-row mechanism was already refused at formation; it must be reformulated with an explicit R=1 template discriminator and CDNA2-only host selection.

statement: The two dominant decode symbols (mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8, 1, fused=true/false>, 75% combined device time) run with rows_per_cuda_block=1 on CDNA2 (mmvq.cu calc_rows_per_block GCN !small_k -> 1), so every one of the ~5120-27648 output-row CTAs re-reads the full row-independent Q8_1 activation (y, kby=kbx, no row dependence) from L2/L1 on each K sweep: y L2 traffic is ~1.0x the weight bytes per matrix at bs1, so L2 read traffic is ~2x the DRAM stream on the two top kernels. The champion's own last keep (445e93a8c) proved the same class of change on this rung/quant: at ncols_dst=4, rows_per_cuda_block 2->4 cut y re-read traffic ~2x per weight byte and measured +10.098% on dec-b4. Extend exactly that lever to ncols_dst=1 for GCN Q8_0: launch rows_per_cuda_block=4 (rows % 4 == 0; else fall back to the small_k R=nwarps instantiation as the b4 commit does), so each CTA covers 4 output rows and one y pass is shared across the row group (u int32 loads merge across the unrolled row loop since kby is row-invariant), cutting y L2 traffic ~4x (1.0 -> 0.25 per weight byte, total L2 reads ~2x -> ~1.25x DRAM) and turning the awkward 160-block rows (160 = 2x64+32, third iteration at half occupancy) into exact 640 = 10x64 iterations. Numerics stay bit-identical: the (row, kbx) -> (thread, iteration) mapping and each row's ascending kbx accumulation order are unchanged by the grouping, only the shared y loads move, so the ordinary MUL_MAT oracle decides correctness; fused (gate+up) instantiations inherit the change through the shared calc_rows_per_block path and already run R=4 at the 1536 specialization (mmvq.cu:709-711).

statement: The HIP-graph q8_1 dedup cache in ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q (mmvq.cu) quantizes src1 to Q8_1 once per unique src1 tensor per capture and lets later MMVQ nodes sharing that tensor reuse the buffer - but cache_eligible whitelists only Q4_K/Q6_K at ne11==1. The confirm-rung model (27B Q8_0) is whitelisted out, so its decode graph re-quantizes the same activation tensor per node: the live profile shows 1:1 launch parity (55,857 quantize_q8_1_1d calls = 18,576 + 37,281 mul_mat_vec_q calls) and 5.80% device share, with the q/k/v projections (and any other MMVQ ops sharing one x, e.g. norm outputs) requantizing identical F32 data 3x per layer. The q8_1 buffer content depends only on src1, never on src0 type, so widening eligibility to Q8_0 (and to the dec-b widths, ne11<=8, which the ne11==1 gate also blocks) deletes ~2 of every ~6 quantize launches per layer from the replayed graph plus their inter-kernel bubbles, at byte-identical numerics - mirroring the +2.135%/+1.315% the same cache already measured on Q4_K/Q6_K; expected decode gain ~+1.5-2.5% (quantize share 5.80% -> ~3.9%).

statement: At ncols_dst=1 decode, the non-small-k Q4_K MMVQ template (large K, e.g. FF-down at K=8960: 35 weight superblocks > the 32-block single-pass threshold, so calc_rows_per_block mmvq.cu:823 returns 1) launches one CTA per dst row. The q8_1 activation (y) row does not depend on the dst row, so every CTA in the grid re-streams the same y row from L2 once per dst row; at K=8960 the y row is 280 blocks x 34 B = 9.5 KB versus 5.0 KB of x per row (~1.9x), i.e. y-side L2 read traffic is ~2x the HBM weight traffic. Raising rows_per_cuda_block to 2 for this instantiation (GCN, ncols_dst==1, !small_k) halves the grid and makes the second dst row's y loads L1 hits, cutting the kernel's L2 read stream ~in half; per-row accumulation order and thread k-partition are unchanged, so numerics are bit-identical. This is the exact mechanism of the sibling keep akm-cdna2-q8-b4-y-stream-amortize (+10.098% dec-b4, rpb 2->4 on the Q8_0 b4 template; its comment quantifies y as 2.1x of weight bytes at rpb=2 -> 1.06x at rpb=4); the small_k/1536 b1 instantiation already amortizes via rpb=nwarps, so only this large-K b1 template is unamortized. Odd dst-row counts take a host-side fallback to the existing rpb=1 instantiation (the kernel's dot loop has no row bounds guard on x reads - only the epilogue store at mmvq.cu:1357 is guarded - mirroring the b4 keep's r2 fallback). Applies to both hot instantiations (fused and unfused), which together are 75.25% of the decode profile.

statement: On the current champion decode profile the single largest kernel is the fused bs=1 Q8_0 MMVQ instantiation mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8,1,true,false,0,false,false> at 46.01% of device time, ~110 us/call over 18576 calls, while its unfused sibling <...,1,false,...> is 29.24% at ~35 us/call over 37281 calls. A fused gate+up call moves ~2x the weight bytes of an unfused q/k/v call, so the fused row runs at roughly half the per-byte rate of the unfused row (~29% vs ~45% of the 1638 GB/s peak) - the biggest per-byte anomaly on the whole surface. The fused kernel was inherited from the Q4_K fusion campaign, but that campaign landed as compile-time-specialized flavors that are Q4_K-only by static_assert (bias_only and gate_only_swiglu templates, plus the fixed-1536 unroll) and hold a single row-stream live per K iteration; Q8_0 fusion exists only as the generic runtime-fusion template, whose per-lane K loop keeps two row-stream live-sets (gate row and up row: dual accumulators plus two in-flight weight operand vectors) - the exact register-pressure signature that, per the standing AK-H-QL-1 knee (<=64 VGPR = 8-wave decode fast band, >64 = 6 waves), cost the other quants' fused variants their occupancy. Mechanism: restructure the fused Q8_0 bs1 dot in mmvq.cu so each K pass holds a single row-stream live - sequential gate-then-up passes over the same L2-resident q8_1 y row with two scalar accumulators carried across the passes - plus a Q8_0 compile-time specialization selected at dispatch, targeting the register/live-range profile of the unfused instantiation. Numerics are bit-identical per output row: same ascending-K dot and same scale application for each row; only the interleaving of two independent rows changes, and the correctness gate is the ordinary MUL_MAT/MUL_MAT_ID oracle. If the per-byte gap is real, this is worth up to ~15% of decode (110 us toward 70 us on 46% of device time); if it is not, the measurement below says so cheaply.

statement: Extend the kept y-stream-amortization family (rows_per_cuda_block=4 at ncols_dst=4, +10.098% on dec-b4) to the batch-1 Q8_0 MMVQ kernels that are the top two rows of the champion decode profile: fused mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,1,true,...> 46.01% and unfused 29.24% (~75% of device time, 27B-Q8_0 surface). At ncols_dst=1 every output row re-walks the same Q8_1 activation row y (~5760 B at ne00=5120, ~1.06x the per-row weight bytes) as a separate 256-thread block (nwarps=4), so y is pulled from L2 once per row. rows_per_cuda_block=2 (rows_per_thread=2, one row pair 2b, 2b+1 per block) halves the block count: the row-1 pass consumes the y lines the row-0 pass just fetched from L1, halving L2->L1 y traffic, and each thread carries two independent weight-load streams per kbx step. Per-row accumulation order is unchanged (same kbx sequence, same reduction), so outputs are bit-identical; only launch geometry and block->row mapping change. Two critic defects are resolved by construction: (1) the fused gate is NOT a hardcoded constant - the patch first builds with R=2 emitted for the three new instantiations (unfused, generic-fused, swiglu-fused), then reads .vgpr_count from the NT_AMDGPU_METADATA note of the gfx90a ELF in mmvq.cu.o's .hip_fatbin (champion R=1 fused measures 25 VGPR, R=4 small_k fused 40); each instantiation's R=2 dispatch is enabled iff its own measured count is <= 64 (8-wave rung), else that instantiation ships R=1 with a matching grid - default is OFF until the number is recorded in the commit. (2) The unfused R=2 launch is gated only on nrows_x % 2 == 0 (x row reads are unguarded; the store guard alone would mask OOB) and is never dragged by the fused gate. CDNA2 scoping: the rows=2 rule is keyed on CDNA2 (compile-time defined(CDNA2) for the device-side constexpr, cc == GGML_CUDA_CC_CDNA2 for the host launch params, the same pattern as the existing gfx90a gates), not on the MMVQ_PARAMETERS_GCN table id, so GCN and CDNA1/CDNA3 devices keep rows_per_cuda_block=1 and bit-identical launch geometry to the champion.

statement: The profile's top kernel, mul_mat_vec_q<Q4_K,1,true,...> (46.01% of decode device time, runtime-fused: gate_only_swiglu=false, bias_only=false), dots the main matrix and the gate matrix with TWO separate vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1 calls per 256-weight block (mmvq.cu:1240 and :1244-45) whenever fusion.gate != nullptr. Both calls consume the SAME q8_1 activation block and re-issue the y-side loads (u0, u1, ds8: 3 loads per QR4_K step), the bq8_1 address arithmetic, and the ds/sum unpack for the identical byte range. The tree already contains vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_dual (mmvq.cu:97, gfx90a-specialized: shared u0/u1/ds8 loads, scale/perm work hoisted, elementwise-packed FMA), which is exactly this dedup - but it is only reachable under the constexpr gate converged_q4_K_dual = small_k && gate_only_swiglu (mmvq.cu:1158), so the runtime-gated generic template that owns 46% of the profile never sees it. Change: in the generic has_fusion inner loop, replace the two sequential vec_dot calls with a runtime-uniform branch that calls vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_dual when use_gate is true (same condition as today's second call), accumulating dots.x into tmp and dots.y into tmp_gate; keep the single-dot path for use_gate==false. This is NOT a launch/occupancy change (calc_nwarps, nwarps, rows-per-block untouched - the refused 4-to-8-wave widening is a different mechanism); it is instruction dedup inside the existing launch. Numerics are bit-identical: the dual executes each matrix's dp4a/scale/FMA chain in the same order as two sequential single dots (it is the same audited function the static SwiGLU path already runs through the 1139/1139 oracle), so no MUL_MAT-value change and no type-selection change. Mechanism of the win: bs1 decode GEMV is issue/latency-bound (screen surface runs at ~20% of the HBM roofline, per the standing record), so removing 8-12 duplicated load/issue slots and the y-address recompute per 8-step block iteration from the kernel that is 46% of device time should move decode; the y-side dedup is worth ~5-15% of the fused kernel's dot-loop instructions. Risks stated up front: +4-6 VGPR from holding both matrices' v0/v1/scale live (must verify against the 64-VGPR / 8-wave occupancy knee with llvm-objdump BEFORE the build; if the instantiation sits at >64 VGPR today or crosses it, abandon), and the change is confined to mmvq.cu (not the shared dequantize.cuh), so the cpy.cu undeclared-identifier hazard class does not apply.

statement: On the current champion profile the two Q8_0 MMVQ instantiations are 48.22% (fused, 18,576 calls) and 27.13% (unfused, 37,281 calls) of decode: 115.1 us/call vs 32.3 us/call, a 3.56x ratio. Cause: the fused body interleaves two weight matrices in one unrolled k-loop, holding 8 live row-accumulators (tmp[4] + tmp_gate[4]) and touching 8 weight-row streams + y concurrently per CTA, pushing the register footprint against the CDNA2 64-VGPR/8-wave knee and interleaving two DRAM streams at ~2 KB granularity; the unfused 4-row kernel the lane just kept (cabac2563) has half that live state and 4 weight-row streams. Mechanism: for CDNA2 Q8_0 ncols_dst=1 small_k fused launches, split the non-fixed k-loop into two sequential full-K passes - pass 1 accumulates all 4 up rows into tmp, pass 2 re-walks k accumulating the 4 gate rows into tmp_gate (y is 5.76 KB and L2-resident, so the second y read is near-free; per-row accumulation order in kbx is unchanged, so every output is bit-identical to the champion and the MUL_MAT oracle is the ordinary one). This halves the live accumulator set per pass, shrinks the unrolled body, and presents one weight stream at a time to the memory system, targeting parity with the unfused instantiation's ~913 GB/s - worth up to ~40% of the 48% fused share. Probe before authoring: (1) per-launch byte census (tensor table + launch trace) to confirm fused calls carry ~2x unfused per-call work - if not, the 3.56x ratio has a shape explanation and the premise dies; (2) llvm-objdump VGPR count of the fused vs unfused instantiation - if the fused kernel is already <=64 VGPR at 8 waves resident, the register arm is dead and the stream-locality arm alone is predicted null.

statement: Extend the kept mmvq q8_1 graph-reuse cache (ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q, mmvq.cu:2134) from src0 types {Q4_K, Q6_K} to also include GGML_TYPE_Q8_0. outcome.refusal_reason: The mechanism replicates a once-per-launch quantization across every 4-output-row CTA. At ne00=nrows_x=5120, the external kernel quantizes one activation row once, while the proposed path requantizes it in about 1280 CTAs. Each CTA replaces roughly 5.76 KB of reusable Q8_1 reads with 20.48 KB of f32 reads plus 160 max-reductions and rounding, nearly doubling the per-CTA weight-plus-activation traffic before ALU cost. This staging must precede the dependent dot products, so overlap with the weight stream is unsupported. The provided history already rejects this same 4-row-CTA quantization-multiplicity mechanism; the new gate does not supply evidence that changes that dominant cost. | The cross-CTA publication protocol is not valid as stated. A release/acquire flag provides memory visibility but does not guarantee that CTA 0 is resident before polling CTAs; HIP may schedule blocks in any order, so polling CTAs can occupy all resident slots and deadlock. The scratch flag also retains its ready value across graph replays: other CTAs may observe the previous launch's value before CTA 0 resets it, read stale Q8_1 data, and no reset-then-publish sequence can close that race without a unique launch generation or a grid-wide barrier. statement: On the champion's dense CDNA2 batch-1 Q8_0 path - mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,1,has_fusion,small_k=true> (mmvq.cu:999), the fused row at 48.22% (18,576 calls) plus unfused at 27.13% (37,281 calls) = 75.35% of this profile - the four-row small_k CTA (rows_per_cuda_block = nwarps = 4, from the kept akm-cdna2-q8-b1-four-row-cta) has all four warps stride over every row and then pays a serialized cross-warp epilogue per CTA: warps 1-3 stage 4 rows x 64 lanes x 4B (doubled under GLU fusion with the tmp_gate accumulator) into tmp_shared, a __syncthreads, the staged warps exit, and warp 0 re-adds and re-reduces (mmvq.cu:1267-1309, 1346). The tree's own sweep already fingered this epilogue: nwarps=8 lost to nwarps=4 as 'reduction-overhead-bound' (mmvq.cu:716-717), and the loop's two kept DPP-final-reduce mechanisms (akm-q4k-halfwave-dpp-final-reduce +1.451%, akm-q6k-single-row-dpp-final-reduce +1.783%, __gfx90a__-gated reduce_q*_gfx90a helpers) exist exactly to replace LDS cross-warp staging with intra-warp DPP - but neither is instantiated for Q8_0 at ne00=5120. Effects: (i) the per-CTA serial barrier+LDS tail disappears; (ii) per-lane accumulator count drops 4x, targeting the <=64-VGPR/8-wave occupancy knee so more CTAs stay resident per SIMD and hide the y-stream latency that holds these launches at ~0.87-1.3 TB/s against the ~1.5 TB/s STREAM-achievable ceiling (fused 13824-row FFN half near ~85%, unfused 5120-row attention-projection half ~55%). Cost side: x (Q8_1 activation) is re-read per warp instead of per CTA; sibling warps issue the same blocks in the same iterations, so the 4x x traffic should be L1-served - if it spills to L2 the A/B turns negative and the falsifier fires. statement: In the decode graph, every fused or unfused `mul_mat_vec_q<Q4_K>` launch is paired 1:1 with a standalone `quantize_q8_1_1d` launch (55,857 quantize calls = 55,857 MMVQ calls in the champion profile; ~4.4 us each on a ~24-CTA grid, launch-bound) that re-reads the producer's f32 row from HBM and writes a fresh Q8_1 copy. The norm-fed activations (attn-norm feeding q/k/v, FFN-norm feeding the fused up+gate pair) have only MMVQ consumers, and `rms_norm_f32` (norm.cu) is one-CTA-per-row over the full ncols, so each 32-element Q8_1 block's d/s reduce is local to the CTA that already holds those normalized values in registers. Change: give rms_norm_f32 a Q8_1-store variant that writes i8 + half2(d,s) directly into the q8_1 scratch owned by the existing mmvq graph-cache registry (keyed by the norm dst pointer, the same key the consumer looks up), and make `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q` (mmvq.cu) skip its quantize_row_q8_1_cuda launch when the registry holds that row. Quantization multiplicity stays 1 per row per step -- the producer already streams x exactly once, so the b1-eight-row-cta per-CTA-replication objection does not apply -- and each matmul's f32-write/f32-read/Q8_1-write round trip plus one launch pair disappears. Numerics: same 32 values, same roundf/127 mapping, but the d/s reduce tree differs from quantize_q8_1_1d's xor-shuffle order, so Q8_1 s can differ by <=1 ulp fp32 -> MUL_MAT-tolerant but not bit-identical; this is a value-level, not type-selection, change, so it is in the class the oracle catches. Gross ceiling on the screen rung: the 5.56% quantize_q8_1_1d share (433 launches/execution) minus a small norm-side ALU increase (~1-2% on the 3.96% norm share), i.e. roughly +3-4% on tg128 decode.

outcome.refusal_reason: The hotspot is misidentified: ggml_type 8 is Q8_0, while Q4_K is ggml_type 12 (ggml/include/ggml.h:398,402). Therefore the proposed Q4_K-only dual path cannot affect the cited 49.32% kernel, and the profile supplies no device-time share for the generic fused Q4_K instantiation. The analogous Q8_0 dual-dot mechanism was already measured as akm-cdna2-q8-swiglu-dual-dot and regressed tg128 by 4.428%. | The traffic premise is false in the current champion. gfx90a ISA already CSEs the invariant Q8_1 operands across all four output rows and both fused x/gate dots: one activation dwordx2 load plus one ds load feeds the repeated dot chains. Therefore y is fetched once per CTA k-step, not once per row or fused dot, and LDS staging cannot reduce requests by the claimed rows-per-CTA factor or remove three global loads per dot. Equivalent byte-verbatim CTA-local Q8_1 staging was also measured repeatedly on Q4_K/Q6_K and regressed tg128 by 1.632% to 9.531%. The dec-b4 1.06x observation reflects four distinct activation columns versus four weight rows, not redundant batch-1 row sweeps, so it does not support this mechanism. | Current gfx90a ISA contradicts the load premise: the hot unfused Q8_0 kernel already combines get_int_b2 into global_load_dword instructions at offsets 2 and 6, so the payload is not lowered as pairs of 16-bit loads and repacking cannot deliver the claimed roughly 4x instruction reduction. The remaining global_load_ushort operations are wave-issued scale loads; identical lane addresses are already coalesced, so leader loading would not remove a wave-level VMEM instruction. Also, MMQ separates scales and quants only while loading raw blocks into per-launch shared-memory tiles; there is no existing CUDA buffer-load repack machinery to mirror. statement: The bs=1 Q8_0 decode surface pays a standalone f32->Q8_1 requant kernel per MMVQ node (quantize_q8_1_1d, 3.51% of device time, profile row 3) that materializes the activation row to global q8_1 and forces a dependent-kernel serialization before mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0> (fused-gate 49.66% + plain 27.54%, both small_k instantiations) can dp4a it. In the four-row small_k CTA each 32-element act block is owned by exactly one 4-lane group (8 contiguous elements per lane), so the quantization can be relocated from the separate kernel into the point of use: the group loads the 32 f32 activation values, reduces block max over its 4 lanes (fmaxf is order-insensitive), and derives d = amax/127 and q = roundf(xi/d) with the same fp32 operations quantize_q8_1_1d performs - single fp32 divide, same rounding - so the resulting int32 operand words are bit-identical to the materialized q8_1 and vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1 consumes them unchanged. This deletes the quantize kernel, its global write/read round trip, and the per-node stream dependency from decode; act bytes then travel from L2 only, amortized across the CTA's 4 rows and, in the gate-fused variant, across both dot streams. Host side (ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat_vec_q dispatch) skips the quantize launch and cache insert for this case and passes the raw f32 src1 as y with an in-kernel requant flag. Gated to gfx90a, type Q8_0, ncols_dst==1, ne11==1 (the is_1d shape that dispatches quantize_q8_1_1d), dense (ids==null); MMQ, dec-b* widths, MoE/expert, other quant types and the graph q8_1 cache keep the materialized path unchanged. The changed paths are exactly profile rows 1-3. Win is capped by the ~3.51% kernel share plus removed serialization; the in-kernel conversion adds ~40 ALU ops per thread per visited block, so honest expectation is +1.5-3% on tg128, with a null below the floor as a live possibility.

statement: On the decode surface, the two mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,ncols_dst=1,small_k> instantiations (~77% of device time) consume Q8_1-quantized activations produced by quantize_q8_1_1d (~33.5k in-graph node executions, 3.51% of device, ~277 nodes per decode step at ~4.45us each for a ~25 KB payload). The kernel body is already mined (DPP-64-CTA keeps) and same-tensor duplication is already deduped by the mmvq q8_1 graph cache (akm-q8-1-graph-local-reuse + akm-q8-0-q8-1-graph-cache-row keeps); what remains is one requantize node per unique activation tensor per step, and its cost is per-node dispatch/ramp, not work. Consumer-side fusion (quantizing f32 y inside the MMVW prologue) is structurally redundant: with rows_per_cuda_block=4 every one of the ~nrows/4 CTAs walks the full K range, so each CTA would requantize the entire row from f32 (~20 KB x CTA-count of L2 rereads). Producer-side fusion is 1x: the rms_norm_f32 kernels (rms_norm_f32<1024>/<256>: 2.67%+1.06% = ~137 calls/step) that emit these activation rows hold the normalized values in registers. Extend their epilogue to additionally write the Q8_1 side buffer (32-group |x| max, d = max/127, per-element round, sum s - exact reference formulas of quantize_q8_1_1d), allocate the side buffers through the champion's existing mmvq_q8_1_graph_cache machinery (keyed on the src1 tensor, capture-scoped, already proven), and let the MMVQ pair read them. Because max/sum reductions are order-independent and the register value written to f32 is the exact value stored, the side buffer is bit-identical to the reference kernel's output, so MUL_MAT inputs are unchanged and the numeric-identity hazard class does not apply; Q8_0's vec_dot consumes only d (__low2half(ds)) but the full block is written. Net: ~137 quantize nodes/step (~0.6-0.9 ms of the 1.23 ms/step tax) disappear at a few us of extra epilogue per norm call - roughly -1.0 to -1.8% decode on this surface, with the same pattern extendable to the remaining producers (adds/GDN outputs) toward the full 3.51% tax. This is the operator's Tier-1 L1 lever (mi210-q8-dequant-gemv-roofline) placed at the only point where the requantize work is done exactly once.

Change: give the eight_warp cell an effective vdr=4 (per-thread dp4a width 2->4, threads per 32-int8 block qi/vdr 4->2), making blocks_per_iter 256 >= 160 so the whole row is consumed in one k-pass: per-row loop trips halve, the 384-lane idle second pass disappears (vdr=2 parks 384 lane-iterations per row; vdr=4 parks 192 from the start and never issues a second pass), and each live lane issues its weight/y/scale loads once per row as a 4-deep independent dp4a chain, raising per-thread MLP on a kernel whose achieved bandwidth is MLP/latency-limited (calc_nwarps comment :808-815; the kept 3->2-pass nwarps=8 widening of this same cell gained +2.031%, the 2->1-pass version of the same lever is unmeasured). Containment: the kernel already carries the eight_warp_q8_cdna2 constexpr; use it to select vdr=4 with explicit impl<float,vdr> v/u loads (existing pattern mmvq.cu:1077-1084) only on this cell - every other Q8_0 route (dec-b* wide batch, has_ids, shape-triggered small_k, non-CDNA2) keeps vdr=2, and rows with blocks_per_row_x > 256 (down-projection widths) remain multi-pass at any vdr, so no single-pass claim is made for them. Not claimed: barrier savings (this kernel has no in-loop barrier) and no numerics identity: dp4a products are exact int but per-block f32 scale application regroups from 4 threads to 2, so results are numerically-valid-not-bit-exact (same class as the nwarps=8 keep, MUL_MAT oracle expected to pass).

statement: The profile's top route is decode MMVQ with Q8_0 weights (ggml_type 8 - Q8_0, not Q4_K): mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8,1,true,true,0,false,false,true> (fused-gate GLU cell, 49.03%) plus the has_fusion=false twin (27.01%) = ~76% of device time, both the CDNA2 dense bs=1 four-row small_k cell kept in 1d1f825dc (akm-cdna2-q8-b1-eight-warp-four-row). Mechanism: that cell runs nwarps=8 (512 threads), vdr=2 (VDR_Q8_0_Q8_1_MMVQ, 2 dwords = 4 int-dp4a per thread per block, 4 threads per Q8_0 block), so blocks_per_iter = vdr*nwarps*warp_size/qi = 128 and a ne00=5120 row (160 Q8_0 blocks, the shape cited in the champion's own commit) takes ceil(160/128) = 2 k-passes; pass 2 carries only blocks 128..159, executed by the 32 thread-groups with kbx0<32, i.e. warps 0-1 (25% of threads) do a second dependent load+dot round-trip on the same row accumulator while warps 2-7 idle at the cross-warp reduction barrier. Sibling evidence that pass count is the lever at this exact shape: the champion commit measured +2.031% for exactly the 3-pass (nwarps=4) -> 2-pass (nwarps=8) reduction. This takes the next rung by folding the k-split: a cell-local 4-dword Q8_0 dot (vdr=4: 2 threads per Q8_0 block, kqs = 4*(tid%2), kbx0 = tid/2, blocks_per_iter = 256) covers the 160-block row in ONE k-pass with 320 of 512 thread-slots live, deleting the second pass, its loop/branch, barrier wait and the 32-block tail; x bytes moved are unchanged, per-thread x loads become one 16B (split 2x8B) read per row-dot instead of two 4B reads (same bytes, half the load instructions), and y (Q8_1) dword loads per block drop from 4 threads x 8B to 2 x 16B. Numerics: int dp4a partials stay exact; only the per-block fp scale-multiply granularity changes (2-way -> 4-way per block), the same non-bit-exact tolerance class the eight-warp keep already accepted with test-backend-ops MUL_MAT green - the per-row accumulation structure, thread->row mapping and DPP quad-row reduce are untouched. The patch follows the existing per-cell dot-variant precedent (vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_b4 / _dual) confined to this CDNA2 b1 four-row instantiation so the ncols_dst=4, MUL_MAT_ID and non-small_k Q8_0 routes keep vdr=2 geometry untouched. Main risk to check before the A/B: the payload registers double (x dwords in flight: 8 -> 16 plain, 16 -> 32 fused), which can push VGPRs past the point where the 512-thread CTA drops below its current 8 resident waves - the occupancy knee that has cost every prior over-64-VGPR rung.

statement: On gfx90a only, raise the Q8_0 MMVQ dot values-per-thread from 2 to 4 (VDR_Q8_0_Q8_1_MMVQ, threaded consistently through vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1's v/u arrays and dp4a loop, the kernel-side block math kbx0 = tid/(qi/vdr), kqs = vdr*(tid % (qi/vdr)) and blocks_per_iter = vdr*nwarps*warp_size/qi, and get_vdr_mmvq; all of these are per-arch compile-time, so RDNA/CUDA/gfx908 keep vdr=2). Arithmetic at the champion's Q8_0 bs1 decode cell, which owns the two top profile symbols (49.03% + 27.01%, mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8, 1, ...> with fusion on and off, both eight-warp four-row small_k CTAs at ne00=5120 = 160 Q8_0 blocks/row): at vdr=2 the per-thread k-loop makes two passes of 128 blocks per row (blocks_per_iter = 2*8*64/8 = 128) and the second pass runs only 128 of 512 lanes for the 32-block tail (160 = 128 + 32), while each 32-weight block's f16 scale is loaded and f32-converted by 4 threads; at vdr=4 blocks_per_iter becomes 256, the whole 160-block row is consumed in one pass (320/512 lanes), per-block scale handling halves (2 threads per block), and each thread's serial dp4a chain per row doubles (2 -> 4 wide). The Q8_0 GEMV achieves ~47-49% of peak HBM against an fp16 ceiling of ~62%, so per-weight-byte issue overhead is a plausible binding constraint rather than bytes: this change moves identical bytes through half the k-loop re-entries, half the scale loads/converts, and half the address arithmetic per byte (the qs reads stay 2B-granular, forced by the half-scale-before-qs block layout; the mechanism does not claim to widen loads), with twice the in-flight dp4a work per thread. Numerics: the integer dp4a dots per (block, word) are bit-identical; only fp32 accumulation grouping across lanes shifts, the numerically-valid-not-bit-exact class already precedented in-tree (mmvq.cu:811-812 and the dpp keeps), so test-backend-ops MUL_MAT 1139/1139 must pass. No dispatch table, type-traits row, or dequant path changes (avoids the known-dangerous classes; numerics-identical claim is at the integer-dot level only). VGPR audit required before build: v/u live registers grow ~4-6 per row chain; if the four-row CTA crosses its current occupancy rung the mechanism is dead before measurement.

Numerics: each row's fp32 sum regroups across lanes, numerically-valid-not-bit-exact, the same class as the eight-warp and vdr=4 keeps (MUL_MAT oracle required; no type, traits or dispatch change; the branch is host-gated to CDNA2 dense bs=1 Q8_0 so dec-b4/dec-b8 wide-batch MMQ routes are untouched by construction).

statement: The decode profile is a q8_1-activation chain: the top two kernels (mul_mat_vec_q<GGML_TYPE_Q8_0,1,..>, fused GLU 49.40% + unfused 26.69%) consume activations as global block_q8_1 columns that quantize_q8_1_1d (row 3: 3.61%, 33,505 calls, ~262 per token) materializes from the fp32 columns that rms_norm_f32 (rows 4.17% combined over 27K calls) wrote immediately before. Each decode step therefore pays, per quantized column: one extra kernel launch, an fp32 store, a full reload, and a q8_1 store - all on the critical path into 76% of device time. Mechanism: give rms_norm_f32 a q8_1 output mode whose epilogue forms block_q8_1 directly from its own register-resident fp32 row, using quantize_q8_1_1d's exact per-32 construction (d = amax/127 with amax/amax-sum over the 32 lanes, same rounding), so the q8_1 blocks are bit-identical and every downstream dot is untouched by construction (Q8_0 x Q8_1 consumes only __low2half(ds), so even the block-sum's inert tail cannot move results); the host pairing site that emits (norm-fp32 -> quantize_q8_1_1d -> MMVQ/fused-MMVQ) for the FFN-input and attention norms collapses to (norm-q8_1 -> MMVQ), deleting the quantize kernel, its launch, and the fp32/q8_1 global round trip from every decode step feeding the top kernels. This is the producer side of the endorsed seed-02 L1 lever, is the same q8_1-side class as the kept akm-q8-1-graph-local-reuse (not the weight-dequant side that killed run 9), and leaves type selection, dispatch tables and all quantized-matmul weight reads alone.

statement: On the champion's decode profile, the top Q8_0 route pays a separate quantize_q8_1_1d kernel launch before every bs=1 mul_mat_vec_q (quantize_row_q8_1_cuda called from ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q, mmvq.cu:2427): 33,505 launches, 150.0 ms, 3.61% of device time at ~4.5 us/call. The kernel work is ~1 us of ALU on a 20 KB row; the rest is launch/ramp/sync latency serialized on the decode critical path (the kept q8_1 graph caches already deduped cross-consumer requants; this residual is one requant per fresh activation per step and cannot be cached away). Mechanism: fold the Q8_1 requantization of the activation row into the champion's four-row Q8_0 b1 cell (mul_mat_vec_q eight_warp_q8_cdna2 instantiation, mmvq.cu:1118, both has_fusion and unfused). Each lane pair that owns a 32-lane Q8_1 block loads its 16 f32 of the src1 row, exchanges partial |x| maxima with one shfl, computes d = amax/127 and q = roundf(x/d) in-register, and hands vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1_impl its u[] ints directly - no Q8_1 global write, no separate kernel, no Q8_1 readback. Per-CTA requant is ~1280x redundant across the grid, but the cell is HBM-bound with idle issue slots (the kept vdr=4 change doubled per-lane dp4a for +0.892%), so the ~100 added ALU ops/lane hide under weight-load stalls while 33.5k launches disappear. Best case ~+3.5% of the decode surface (up to ~15% of an unfused call's 29.7 us is its quantize share). Gated host-side and exact: CDNA2, Q8_0, ne11=1, dense, nrows_x % 4 == 0, four-row cell; Q4_K/Q6_K, has_ids/MoE, dec-b* widths and non-CDNA2 keep the standalone quantize, so the shared MUL_MAT path is untouched outside the gate. Numerics: d is an exact order-free fmax over the same 32 values, q = roundf(x/d) divides IEEE-identical operands, so every byte the dot reads is bit-identical to today; the ds.s field (fp32 sum) sums in a different association order and is the one non-bit-exact byte - written but never read by vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1_impl, which consumes only qs and __low2half(ds). Does not touch quant types, type-traits rows or dispatch tables; the quantization function itself is not modified, only relocated.

outcome.refusal_reason: The claimed halving counts per-lane work, but gfx90a issues instructions per wave. Predicating the FP tail on odd lanes only changes EXEC; it does not remove the wave-issued conversions, multiplies, FMAs, or scale-load instructions because pair leaders remain distributed across every SIMD16 quarter. Champion disassembly already shows the unfused four-row tail compacted to 4 i32-to-f32 conversions, 2 packed multiplies, and 2 packed FMAs, while duplicate lane addresses are served by the same coalesced VMEM instructions. The proposed path therefore retains those instructions and memory transactions while adding an integer cross-lane dependency and masking. The mechanism is unsupported unless pair results are compacted into packed operands within fewer issued instructions and objdump demonstrates a net tail-instruction reduction. | Already measured. akm-q4k-cta-q8-fused-prologue implemented the same per-CTA F32-to-Q8_1 LDS prologue, removed quantize_q8_1_1d, passed MUL_MAT 1139/1139, and regressed tg128 by 59.182%; related inline variants regressed 36-65%. The current eight-warp four-row Q8_0 cell does not remove that failure cause: a 5120-row matrix still launches 1280 CTAs, each requantizing all 160 activation blocks instead of sharing one global quantization. That repeats the quantization about 1280x and reads 20 KB of F32 per CTA, not 10 KB, or about 25.6 MB per matmul. LDS staging and a cache side-write provide no cross-CTA reuse. The old magnitude is stale-epoch evidence, but the fact that this mechanism was tried is formation-authorized and requires rejection. | The mechanism is already disproven by the supplied champion disassembly evidence: the unfused four-row Q8_0 kernel already has one activation dwordx2 load and one activation-scale load/conversion, while the fused kernel has one set per runtime gate branch, not one per row or dot. LLVM has already hoisted/CSE'd the claimed invariant bq8_1/u/ds loads, so the proposed source restructuring has no supported instruction reduction and fails its own step-zero precondition.

statement: Profile rows 1-2 are the champion's CDNA2 dense bs=1 Q8_0 eight-warp vdr4 small_k cell: mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8, 1, true, true, 0, false, false, true> (fused, 49.40%) and its has_fusion=false twin (26.69%), together 76% of device time. In the vdr4 branch of the k-loop (mmvq.cu:1380-1406), the Q8_1 activation block pointer bq8_1, its quants u[vdr] and its scale __low2half(bq8_1->ds) are loaded inside the `for (int i = 0; i < rows_per_thread; ++i)` row loop (line 1370) even though they depend only on the pass index kbx (y[j*stride_col_y + kby], j=0, ncols_dst=1): the same vdr-wide activation fetch is issued once per row, i.e. four times per pass per lane in both instantiations (and the fused gate chain at 1397-1404 consumes the same per-row u). Restructure the branch so each active lane loads bq8_1/u/ds exactly once per (j, kbx) pass into registers and reuses them across the four value rows and the gate chain; this removes three of every four activation fetch issues plus the per-row kby/address math from the pass, on a cell that re-reads its 5.3KB y row from L1 up to 4x per CTA. It reorders no FP operations and changes no accumulation order, so output stays bit-identical to fe881991f (oracle MUL_MAT 1139/1139 is expected to hold unchanged); it is confined by constexpr to the eight_warp_q8_cdna2 cell, so Q4_K/Q6_K routes, wide-batch ncols_dst>1, has_ids and non-CDNA2 paths are untouched. Whether LLVM has already hoisted these loads under this cell's register pressure is the open question the falsifier settles.

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured as akm-cdna2-q8-b1-inline-requant against champion fe881991f with the same eight_warp_q8_cdna2 vdr=4 fused/unfused route, host quantize bypass, lane-pair F32-to-Q8_1 register quantization, and direct u[] operands. It passed compilation and MUL_MAT 1139/1139, but decisively regressed tg128 by 17.129% over 20 alternating pairs (0.638% floor). The per-CTA prologue redundantly requantized the activation across roughly 1280 output CTAs; that L2 and ALU cost was not hidden by the weight stream. | The mechanism is contradicted by fresh gfx90a disassembly of champion fe881991f. In both eight_warp_q8_cdna2 instantiations, the compiler does not implement each get_int_b2 operand as two global_load_ushort instructions plus pack ALU. It SLP-vectorizes each four-operand weight chunk into an unaligned global_load_dwordx4 at offset:2, with no v_alignbit/shift-or packing; the current code also issues one redundant scalar global_load_dword for the first operand. Thus the claimed 8 -> 4/5 weight-load reduction does not exist: the proposed aligned reconstruction would replace the current two load instructions per row chunk with 4 or 5 loads plus alignbits. The hotspot share and falsifier are valid, but the instruction-level premise supporting the optimization is false. | Rejected at step zero: the profiled symbols' final template argument is true, selecting the existing eight_warp_q8_cdna2 specialization. On gfx90a, calc_nwarps(..., true) returns 8 and block_dims uses the 64-lane physical warp size, so this dense bs=1 Q8_0 path already launches 512-thread CTAs, not 128-thread CTAs. The same widening mechanism was already measured and kept as akm-cdna2-q8-b1-eight-warp-four-row (+2.031% tg128 over 20 pairs, commit 1d1f825dc), and is present in the current champion.

statement: On the current champion's decode profile the Q8_0 bs=1 GEMV is the whole top of the table: mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8,1,...> at 49.40% (18576 calls, ~110us each) and 26.69% (37281 calls, ~30us each) = 76.09% of device time, plus quantize_q8_1_1d (3.61%) feeding it. Mechanism: widen the dense bs=1 Q8_0 mul_mat_vec_q CTA from 4 to 8 32-thread warps (128->256 threads, i.e. 2->4 wave64 waves) with rows-per-CTA unchanged, transplanting upstream ggml PR #26843 (25ae3a9b3, 2026-08-18) whose CUDA table shows +6.28% on Q8_0 bs=1 dense decode -- its largest row (Q4_K_M +5.03%, Q6_K +5.68%) -- while guarding OFF MoE/expert rows and small-K shapes exactly as upstream does (gfx90a launch-geometry nulls in our record were all 1536-width Q4_K/Q6_K K-split/row-remap cells on the screen rung; Q8_0 at 5120-class widths is an untried cell, and two keeps from the same family - smallk-wave-row +2.5%, 1536-unroll +2.15% - show shape-correct geometry cells do pay here). Why faster: the per-thread serial chain (load weight chunk -> dp4a -> accumulate) over the K slice is halved in trip count and the number of independent global load streams per CTA doubles, raising loads-in-flight per SIMD on a kernel whose achieved BW is well under STREAM ceiling; numerics are untouched by construction (launch constant only, no MUL_MAT risk class). Step zero, before any diff: disassemble/confirm the dense bs=1 Q8_0 instantiations actually launch 128-thread CTAs - the tree contains eight_warp_q8_cdna2 variants for other shapes, and if this path already launches 256 threads the mechanism is pre-empted and closes as a no-op. Expected ceiling: even half the CUDA delta on the 49.40% row alone is ~+1.5% surface-level.

Multiple 20-pair tg128 runs were null (-0.290%, -0.472%, -0.626%, -0.808%, and +0.865% against a 1.188% floor), while an LDS-staged variant regressed -3.205%. The standing rules allow stale-epoch records to establish that a mechanism was tried, so re-anchoring it to the current Q8_0 profile does not make it new. The stated 2-3% ceiling is also unsupported: 16,641 main RMSNorm calls versus 33,505 quantize calls bounds norm-fed coverage near 49.7% before excluding final norms, for at most about 1.79% of device time before the added packing cost. | The proposed payoff shape is absent from the profiled workload. Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0 has FFN-down K=17408, not 14336, giving 544 Q8_0 blocks. With vdr=8, blocks_per_iter=512, so this row still executes a second pass for 32 blocks with only 32 of 512 lanes active; the other relevant K dimensions are already <=256 blocks. Therefore the new gate does not make the actual wide-K row single-pass, and the aggregate 49.40%/26.69% profile rows do not support the claimed mechanism. Also, loop passes process distinct kbx values, so they do not duplicate the underlying y payload bytes. | The 49.40% hotspot is misattributed. The confirm GGUF has no wide projection biases: its only 48 bias tensors are 48-element ssm_dt.bias rows, while every block has 5120x17408 Q8_0 ffn_gate and ffn_up weights that enter this template with fusion.gate != nullptr. Therefore a bias-only dispatch cannot address a material fraction of the profiled row. Additionally, the generic kernel already selects the four-chain DPP reduction when use_gate is false; it does not execute the eight-chain variant on bias-only calls.

statement: The 49.40% profile row is the fused Q8_0 bs=1 instantiation mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8, 1, true, true, 0, false, false, true> - the generic gate-capable has_fusion template, because the only leaner variants (bias_only, gate_only_swiglu) are compile-time gated to Q4_K (mmvq.cu:1126 static_assert, dispatch branches at mmvq.cu:1744-1758), and Q8_0 fused calls can never take them. That template pays, in every CTA of the widest row class on the profile: (a) tmp_shared_gate is sized by the template flags (mmvq.cu:1436), so 7 KB of LDS is reserved per CTA unconditionally - the fused kernel's 14 KB vs the unfused 7 KB - plus (b) the tmp_gate[4] register array, the per-slot runtime use_gate dot branches (mmvq.cu:1395-1406) and the fused 8-chain DPP epilogue variant, all dead when the call is bias-only. Mechanism: relax the bias_only static_assert and instantiate/dispatch a bias_only Q8_0 variant for dense bs=1 calls whose fusion args are bias-only (fusion.gate == nullptr, probed per call in mul_mat_vec_q_switch_fusion), so those rows halve per-CTA LDS to 7 KB, drop the tmp_gate registers and gate branches, and use the 4-chain DPP reduce; the bias epilogue in the dpp_q8_0_quadrow_reduce case must reload x_bias per row (pattern already at mmvq.cu:1562-1564) so results stay bit-identical - no summation order or type selection changes anywhere, so the run-9 MUL_MAT hazard class does not apply. Rationale: the champion's own keeps show this cell is load-throughput/occupancy-limited (eight-warp +2.031%, vdr4 single-pass +0.892% each cut per-CTA overhead), the fused row is the largest single share at 49.4%, and it is the only top-profile cell still carrying a static gate-side LDS/register load it does not always use; 14->7 KB LDS and the register relief raise achievable resident CTAs/SIMD for that row class, which is the same Little's-law lever the eight-warp keep proved.

statement: In the CDNA2 dense bs=1 Q8_0 four-row cell (eight_warp_q8_cdna2, mmvq.cu), shrink the k-split CTA from 8 warps (512 threads) to 5 warps (320 threads) by returning 5 from calc_nwarps() under that flag. Mechanics: at the vdr=4 single-pass geometry kept in fe881991f, blocks_per_iter = vdr*nwarps*warp_size/qi = 4*5*64/8 = 160, which is exactly blocks_per_row_x = 5120/32 for every 5120-wide dense tensor (up/gate fused MLP = the 49.4% kernel, plus attn/down = the 26.7% kernel). Today at nwarps=8 the pass covers 256 slots, so kbx0 = tid/2 maps warps 5-7 (192 threads) to kbx >= 160 and they execute NO k work, write exact-zero partials through the full-width 7-warp LDS round trip, and burn 3 of the CTA's 8 wave slots and 3/7 of the tail's tmp_shared traffic before warp 0 runs its dpp trees. The 8-warp keep only ever needed more threads to shorten the old 3-pass vdr=2 loop; once single-pass was reached, warps beyond 5 are pure overhead. nwarps=5 keeps the identical per-thread vdr=4 work and per-warp kbx bands (warp w still owns blocks 32w..32w+31), cuts the cross-warp LDS tail from 7 to 4 writing warps, and a 320-thread CTA doubles resident-CTAs per SIMD at <=102 VGPR, letting one CTA's barrier+tail overlap another's k-phase. Numerics: per-thread accumulation and per-warp reduction order are untouched; only the cross-warp combine of exact +0.0f contributions from the dead warps disappears (bit-identical except the sign-of-zero corner), same safety class as the eight-warp keep. Rows wider than 5120 (down-projection, if the model has one) stay multi-pass at either width and tie on engaged slots, so the change is scoped to where the cell's arithmetic is an exact fit. This is the completion of the direction the lane's last four keeps took (four-row +1.5%, eight-warp +2.0%, dpp tail +0.74%, vdr4 +0.89%), not a fresh remap: the refused 8-row-CTA changed rows-per-CTA (rpb=8) and the historical launch-geometry nulls were Q4_K/Q6_K at 1536-width (6 superblocks of 256 per row, a different block-count regime), neither of which this touches.

outcome.refusal_reason: The bit-identity premise and its falsifier are invalid. At ncols=5120, the current <1024> kernel assigns each thread indices tid+k*1024; contiguous float4 loads necessarily regroup those terms as 4*tid+j, changing partial-sum and reduction order, so the RMS scale may change even if writeback FMA order is preserved. Also, test-backend-ops uses an NMSE tolerance (default 1e-7), not bitwise f32 comparison, so a green RMS_NORM oracle cannot prove bit identity. Restate the claim as tolerance-preserving with the existing oracle, or add a true bitwise before/after check; the vector tail and modulo-wrap guards must also be explicit. | The profile supports the target, but not the claimed mechanism. The current source does not perform four 32-bit weight loads per 16-byte slice: get_int_b2 performs two 16-bit loads per element, so vdr=4 expresses eight 16-bit loads; current-champion ISA must establish the actual VMEM instructions before attributing the gap to request width. More importantly, an in-place Q8_0 upload repack cannot be limited to these MMVQ consumers: the same GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 storage is consumed by MMQ, dequantization, copies, get-rows, and other kernels. Keeping the standard representation requires a sidecar that roughly duplicates the 27B weight storage, while replacing it requires updating every consumer and enters the physical-layout/type hazard class. The proposed aligned y stream also requires a distinct Q8_1 quantizer/output layout, which is not specified. Generic LSU-active plus below-STREAM counters would not isolate request granularity from latency, occupancy, or scale-stream effects. Refine with current ISA evidence and a concrete representation/consumer plan, including memory cost and an aligned Q8_1 layout, before admitting a patch. | The proposed graph predicate excludes its claimed target. In Qwen2, the weighted FFN RMS-normalized tensor feeds two distinct MUL_MAT nodes (up and gate); the existing gate/up optimization issues one fused MMVQ host call but does not rewrite them into a single graph consumer. Therefore an 'exactly one dense consumer' pattern cannot fold the MLP norm responsible for the 49.40% fused row. The profile call counts also do not establish the claimed single-consumer fraction. This producer-side RMSNorm-to-Q8_1 fusion family was already measured repeatedly as akm-rmsnorm-q8-sidecar (multiple 20-pair nulls and one regression); omitting the otherwise-dead f32 store is not enough evidence for a distinct 2-4% mechanism. Finally, test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT does not exercise an RMS_NORM+MUL+MUL_MAT graph fusion, so the stated NMSE gate cannot validate the folded path.

statement: On the decode profile the two Q8_0 bs=1 mmvq instantiations (49.40% + 26.69%) are fed by a per-matmul activation chain of two small serialized kernels: rms_norm_f32 (3.05% + 1.12%, 16,641 + 10,320 launches) writes the f32 norm row to global, then quantize_q8_1_1d (3.61%, 33,505 launches, launched at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu:2427 via quantize_row_q8_1_cuda, quantize.cu:514) reads it back and writes the block_q8_1 row that every mul_mat_vec_q CTA then re-reads. Each decode step pays these two launches plus a full f32 row round-trip once per normed matmul. Mechanism: extend the existing graph-fusion pass (ggml-cuda.cu ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_vec_q family) with one new pattern - an RMS_NORM node whose output tensor is consumed by exactly one dense (no ids) Q8_0 ne11==1 mul_mat_vec_q (the MLP norm feeding the fused up/gate launch that owns the 49.40% row); the host call ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q (mmvq.cu:2280) receives the pre-norm tensor, the norm weight and eps through the existing ggml_cuda_mm_fusion_args plumbing and replaces the (rms_norm_f32, quantize_q8_1_1d) pair with one new fused rms_norm_q8_1 kernel in quantize.cu that emits the exact block_q8_1 ds=(d,sum)/qs layout the mmvq kernel already consumes (d=amax/127, q=roundf(xi/d), same 32-contiguous-element groups as quantize_q8_1_1d). One launch and one L2 round trip instead of two, with the 76%-share mmvq kernels themselves byte-for-byte untouched. Numerics are tolerance-preserving, not bit-identical: the row rms reduction and the 32-lane amax/sum reductions reorder relative to the separate kernels (~1 ulp), so bit-identity is not claimed and the NMSE oracle plus a live-output probe is the bar (same class as the accepted vdr4 keep). Multi-consumer norms (norm1 feeding q/k/v) are deliberately excluded - the champion q8_1 graph-cache dedup already owns them - and any non-matching pattern falls back to the current path unchanged; this touches no type-traits row and no dispatch table, so it stays out of the reclassification hazard class; new code goes in quantize.cu/mmvq.cu/ggml-cuda.cu, never in shared headers. Removing the single-consumer half of the 7.78% rms+quantize share from the decode stream is worth roughly 2-4% of device time if the small kernels serialize as their per-call times (7.6us rms_norm<1024>, 3.8us quantize) suggest.
