The profile does not establish the claimed runtime widths. In these symbols, <1024> and <256> are block_size template arguments: the dispatcher uses <1024> for the broader ncols>=1024 bucket and <256> for the broader ncols<1024 bucket. Without an ncols census or dispatch trace, ncols==1024 and ncols==256 special cases cannot be credited with the full 4.17% share, so the proposed patch may miss some or all profiled calls. The <256> arithmetic also conflicts with the supplied profile: it reports 10,320 calls (~4.49 us/call), not 8,256 calls (~5.6 us/call). Establish the exact ncols distribution for both symbols, recompute the affected share, and include an RMS_NORM correctness oracle in addition to the stated MUL_MAT and 1536 guards. | The profile does not support the claimed one-quantize-per-GEMV premise: the two gated MMVQ symbols total 55,857 calls, while quantize_q8_1_1d has 33,505 calls, and the existing graph cache can share one Q8_1 result across consumers by setting reuse_src1_q8_1 and skipping quantization. More importantly, the proposed work is replicated per output CTA, not performed once per activation row. At width 5120, every four-row CTA would read and quantize the same 20,480-byte f32 row, replacing about 5,760 bytes of cached Q8_1 reads per CTA with 3.6x more activation traffic plus repeated fabs/max/divide/round/pack work. Thus the patch does not merely exchange a 4.5 us fixed launch for one small GEMV prologue, and the stated +2-3.5% expectation is unsupported. Attribute the quantize calls to the gated route and account for CTA-replicated bytes and ALU before resubmitting. | Already measured. `akm-q8-0-static-gate-swiglu` implemented the same Q8_0 pure-SwiGLU compile-time dispatch and measured +0.300% over 20 tg128 pairs, below the 0.638% floor, with MUL_MAT passing 1139/1139. The champion-relative corrected eight-warp candidate, `akm-cdna2-q8-b1-fused-gate-constexpr`, already added the required constexpr gate arm and measured +0.144% over 20 pairs; that run was drift-flagged and calls for rerunning the preserved patch, not authoring this mechanism again. The added bias-only arm does not make the proposal distinct: the confirm model has no material wide projection biases; its fused FFN launches carry `fusion.gate`, while its biases are 48-element `ssm_dt.bias` tensors. Thus the material arm is the already-tested gate-only split, and the bias-only arm targets negligible profile share.

statement: The champion's Q8_0 bs1 decode surface is one cell in two template flavors: mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,1,true,small_k,0,false,false,eight_warp> (49.4% of device time, fused) and the same with has_fusion=false (26.7%), both the eight-warp four-row single-pass vdr=4 CTA. The fused instantiation compiles the UNION of both fusion arms and picks between them with runtime branches: it statically allocates 8 row-accumulator chains (tmp[4]+tmp_gate[4]), two 7 KB LDS staging planes (tmp_shared and tmp_shared_gate), and both epilogues (gate/glu switch vs bias reload), and its eight-warp k-loop guards the gate chain behind a runtime use_gate (mmvq.cu:1395). But the host dispatch already HAS compile-time arms for exactly this: bias_only and gate_only_swiglu, which the Q4_K route selects on the same shapes (kept akm-mmvq-static-bias-only +3.45%, akm-mmvq-static-swiglu-gate +2.74%). Both are refused to Q8_0 by a Q4_K-only host gate (mul_mat_vec_q_switch_fusion, mmvq.cu:1744) and a bias_only-requires-Q4_K static_assert (mmvq.cu:1126), and even if instantiated, the eight-warp inner loop has no gate_only arm that forces use_gate true at compile time, so the dead arm's code would remain. Mechanism: extend the compile-time arm dispatch to the Q8_0 eight-warp small_k cell - relax the Q4_K-only asserts, add a constexpr forcing of use_gate under gate_only_swiglu / use_bias under bias_only in the eight-warp branch (and an i-indexed bias epilogue for rows_per_thread=4), instantiate <8,1,true,true,0,true,false,true> and <8,1,true,true,0,false,true,true>, dispatch them from switch_fusion on the pure arm shapes (gate!=null && no biases -> gate-only, i.e. the FFN; x_bias!=null && no gate -> bias-only), and keep the generic template only for co-occurring gate+bias. Every Q8_0 fused call then executes a kernel whose dead arm - dead accumulators, dead LDS plane, dead epilogue branches and glu switch - is not compiled, lowering the 512-thread CTA's static VGPR/LDS and its issue count on the hottest symbol of the profile. Numerics are untouched: each arm executes the identical loads and fp32 sum order it executes today under its runtime branch, so output is bit-identical; the correctness gate is the ordinary MUL_MAT oracle. Step zero (cheap, do before authoring): a fusion-arg census of the fused symbol's launches (log fusion.gate/x_bias/gate_bias once per launch) and an llvm-objdump VGPR/LDS comparison of the shipped fused vs unfused instantiations, which sizes the dead-arm register cost and the expected effect before the build.

task_key.target_symbol: mul_mat_vec_q<GGML_TYPE_Q8_0,1,has_fusion,small_k,...> (eight-warp four-row cell) plus host dispatch in mul_mat_vec_q_switch_fusion

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured three times against champion fe881991f under equivalent five-warp, vdr=4, 5120-wide exact-fit mechanisms. All used 20 alternating tg128 pairs and decisively regressed by 1.931%, 2.280%, and 1.789% versus the 0.638% floor. The mechanism is closed; do not rebuild. | Already measured as akm-q8-b1-fused-lds-stream: the same raw.buffer.load.lds dual-stream fused Q8_0 path passed MUL_MAT 1139/1139, then regressed tg128 by 42.933% over 20 alternating pairs versus the 0.638% floor. The current geometry does not create a new mechanism: keeping 2176B tiles reintroduces three barriered tile iterations with only 128 of 512 consumer threads active, while double-buffering the full 256-block pass for four up rows plus four gate rows requires about 139KB of LDS before activation and reduction storage. Thus the proposed overlap is either the already-measured mechanism or infeasible as stated; the mechanism is closed. | The profile template arguments are block sizes, not runtime widths. On this Qwen3.8-27B profile, the dominant rms_norm_f32<1024,...> traffic is primarily ncols=5120, so one float4 per thread would require 1280 threads, exceeding the 1024-thread limit; the claimed 1024->256 launch therefore does not target that row. The <256> symbol likewise establishes only ncols<1024, not ncols==256. Moreover, the dominant register-resident float4 x/mul direct-index mechanism was already measured as akm-rmsnorm-5120-float4-singlepass: it passed the oracle but gained only +0.525% over 20 alternating tg128 pairs, inside the 0.638% floor. The direct-index-only generalization was also measured at +0.184%, inside the same floor. The remaining <256> row is only 1.12% of device time and cannot support the stated +1.5-2.5% expectation. Reformulation would require a runtime-width census and a genuinely different mechanism for the residual small-width calls.

statement: The mul-fused rms_norm instantiations at the top of the current profile - rms_norm_f32<1024,true,false,false> (3.05%) and rms_norm_f32<256,true,false,false> (1.12%), the GDN chunk norms of the Q8_0 27B decode - run the generic scalar path (norm.cu:195): one element per thread at block 1024/256, a per-element fastmodulo(col, mul_ncols_packed) on mul, scalar x and mul loads, a second read of x after the reduction barrier, scalar stores. The champion already keeps a float4 register-block specialization of this same kernel (akm-rmsnorm-1536-float4-384 + akm-rmsnorm-1536-direct-mul-index), but rms_norm_mul_f32_cuda gates it behind 'ncols == 1536 && mul_ncols == 1536 && mul_nrows == 1 && mul_nchannels == 1 && mul_nsamples == 1' (norm.cu:414), so the widths this profile dispatches can never reach it. Mechanism: generalize that direct_mul/vec4 arm to every ncols % 4 == 0 with full-width per-channel mul (mul_ncols == ncols; mul row/channel/sample broadcast-1 or a one-time per-thread row offset applied via fastmodulo once, not per element), launching threads = ncols/4 (1024 -> 256, 256 -> 64; 1536 keeps 384). Each thread loads one float4 of x (16B), squares it into the reduction, and after the barrier reuses the same register-resident x4 for scale*x*mul with one float4 mul load and one 16B store - no per-element index math, no second x read. This cuts per-row wavefronts 4x, shrinks the block-reduce tree/barrier stages, and gives the small per-call grids (decode launches these per row-group) more independent blocks for latency hiding. Numerics: the direct mul load is value-identical to fastmodulo indexing when col < mul_ncols == ncols; only per-thread square-accumulation order inside a row changes, so results are numerically-valid-not-bit-exact - the exact class the two 1536 keeps were accepted under (RMS_NORM oracle must pass). Expected: the two rows are 4.17% of device time and are body-bound at 7.6us/4.5us per call; recovering 40-60% of their per-call cost is +1.5-2.5% on tg128 against the 0.638% floor.

outcome.refusal_reason: NOT RESOLVED — the instrument drifted during the run (anchor +0.713%, candidate +0.950%, floor 0.638%). The raw effect was +0.429%, but an arm that is still moving resolves nothing. This mechanism is UNTESTED, not unpromising — re-run it rather than abandoning it

statement: The top decode route is the CDNA2 dense bs=1 Q8_0 four-row cell, mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8,1,*,true,0,false,false,true> at 76.1% of device time (fused-gate instantiation 49.40%, 110.4 us/call, 100% use_gate=true; unfused 26.69%). In the fused instantiation every CTA ends in a store epilogue (mmvq.cu:1507-1597) that is fully unrolled into FOUR exec-masked single-lane regions running serially on lane 63 only: after reduce_q8_0_quadrow_gfx90a leaves all four row totals and their gate totals bit-replicated on lanes 60-63, each region still costs ~130 instructions (champion gfx90a code object, lane6-dis/fused_q8.asm) - the runtime active_glu switch with all GLU cascades inlined, v_exp_f32/v_rcp_f32 chains, a vmcnt(0)-stalled 4-byte x_bias/gate_bias reload, and a scalar 4-byte store - i.e. ~520 serial single-lane issue slots plus four exposed memory waits per CTA on the retirement critical path, while warps 1-7 have already returned at mmvq.cu:1456 and the co-resident CTA only partially hides it. Mechanism: collapse the four tails into ONE common SIMD epilogue in which lane 63-i owns row i, selecting its row and gate totals from the registers the DPP tree already replicated onto lanes 60-63 (no retarget needed), rebasing the x_bias/gate_bias pointers per lane so the four 4-byte bias loads and the four dst[row0..row0+3] stores each coalesce into one 16-byte transaction, and evaluating the uniform GLU switch once instead of four times. Per-row FP operations, order and operand values are unchanged, so each output element is bit-identical to the champion; the branch is constexpr-gated to the dpp_q8_0_quadrow_reduce fused Q8_0 instantiation (has_fusion && !bias_only && !gate_only_swiglu), leaving the unfused instantiation, dec-b* wide-batch MMQ routes and all other types untouched by construction. It does not touch the HBM load stream, so it cannot reproduce the interleaved-k-sweep memory-schedule regression; the residual risk is only that the tail is already fully overlapped, which the A/B resolves.

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured against champion fe881991f under equivalent exact-fit mechanisms. akm-cdna2-q8-b1-fivewarp-exactfit and akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-exactfit used nwarps=5, vdr=4, rows_per_thread=4, and an ncols_x==5120 host gate; both passed MUL_MAT 1139/1139 but regressed tg128 by 1.931% and 2.280% over 20 alternating pairs, beyond the 0.638% floor. A third five-warp variant measured -1.789%. The proposed <=160 gate is identical on the claimed production cell and does not create a new mechanism. The 76.1% share claim is also overstated because the model census shows ffn_down K=17408, not 5120. | Already measured under equivalent VDR4 mechanisms. akm-cdna2-q8-b1-fivewarp-exactfit variants used four elements per thread, 8-lane reductions, packed output, and an ncols_x==5120 gate; they passed MUL_MAT but regressed tg128 by 1.931%, 2.280%, and 1.789% over 20 pairs. The proposed CTA64 indexing and scalar tail do not establish a materially different mechanism or explain those regressions. The premise also incorrectly treats all decode rows as 5120, while the model census includes ffn_down K=17408. | The formation evidence is contradicted by the fe881991f device ELF: AMDGPU metadata reports 54 VGPR for the fused instantiation and 53 for the unfused, not 53/52. More importantly, the fused use_gate path does not issue all eight up/gate weight vectors and scales up front: it consumes each up vector between load groups while retaining the four gate vectors for later dots, so the asserted eight-vector live set is absent. A two-row pipeline therefore has no demonstrated path to remove the 14/13 registers needed to reach <=40, and restructuring only the described fused body cannot satisfy the falsifier for the unfused instantiation. Re-form the mechanism from the actual live ranges and show why the <=40 threshold is attainable.

statement: The champion's Q8_0 bs=1 CDNA2 four-row eight-warp cell is register-file-bound at 4 waves/SIMD, and the 49.4% fused instantiation (mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8,1,true,true,0,false,false,true>, mmvq.cu:1118) compiles to 53 VGPR, the 26.69% unfused to 52 (AMDGPU metadata, fe881991f device ELF; 4-warp variants: 42/43). gfx90a: 16384 VGPR/SIMD -> floor(16384/(56x64)) = 4 waves/SIMD at 53 VGPR, so the 8-wave CTA tiles at exactly 2 CTAs/CU (16/16 slots, ~100% regfile). Cutting allocated VGPR to <=40 raises the budget to 6 waves/SIMD and, because 8-wave CTAs divide 24 slots evenly, permits 3 CTAs/CU (24/24): +50% resident waves and proportionally more in-flight weight loads per CU on a kernel whose k-loop is a single latency-exposed pass (160 blocks < 256 slots; 62.5% lane-active) achieving ~49% of paper DRAM peak. Wave-slot tiling is demonstrably the governing occupancy structure on this exact cell: the kept nwarps=8 change (+2.031%) tiles 4+4 cleanly while nwarps=5 (5 waves/CU-fragment) regressed -1.9..-2.3% - but every prior attempt moved nwarps/rows/vdr; none changed VGPR allocation at fixed 512-thread/4-row/vdr=4 geometry. The 11-13 excess registers are the hoisted in-flight operand set of the fully-unrolled 4-row body: disassembly shows all 8 weight dwordx4 + 8 scale ushort loads (up and gate streams) issued up-front per iteration. Mechanism: software-pipeline the fused k-loop body at row-pair granularity - issue the second row-pair's up/gate loads before the first pair's dp4a chains consume (keeping 4 rows of loads in flight, not 8) - bounding live weight operands to 2 rows' (v[4]+gv[4]x2) and landing allocated VGPR <=40 with zero spill on both instantiations. Per-row dp4a chains, scale application and accumulation order are untouched; no numerics change beyond the scheduling already admitted by the eight-warp/vdr4 keeps (numerically-valid-not-bit-exact class), so the oracle (MUL_MAT 1139/1139) is the ordinary gate.

task_key.target_symbol: mul_mat_vec_q (eight_warp_q8_cdna2 vdr=4 branch at :1380-1406 of the <GGML_TYPE_Q8_0,1,has_fusion,small_k,0,false,false,eight_warp> instantiations; fused k-loop body restructured to row-pair software pipelining, host geometry unchanged)

outcome.refusal_reason: The amortization model is wrong. The separate kernel quantizes each activation row once and the kept graph cache shares that Q8_1 row across consumers; the proposed kernel would requantize it independently in every output CTA and every MMVQ consumer. The profile itself contradicts 'before every MMVQ': 33,505 quantize launches feed 55,857 Q8_0 MMVQ launches. At ne00=5120, a four-row CTA currently reads 5,760 B of Q8_1 activations plus 21,760 B of weights, or 43,520 B with a fused gate. Replacing that row with 20,480 B of f32 adds 14,720 B, increasing load bytes by about 53.5% unfused or 29.9% fused, not approximately 5%. Producing the quants in one pass also requires retaining 16 floats per thread until the block maximum is known, adding at least 16 VGPRs and substantially more than 20 scalar operations; otherwise the f32 values must be loaded twice. No occupancy/VGPR bound is supplied. Finally, test-backend-ops is tolerance-based and cannot establish the claimed bit identity after changing the 32-lane max-reduction shape. The hotspot is real, but this in-CTA mechanism does not preserve the existing graph-level amortization and its traffic/issue premise is unsupported. | Already measured three times against champion fe881991f with the same nwarps=5, vdr=4, 320-lane exact-fit geometry: akm-cdna2-q8-b1-fivewarp-exactfit (-1.931%), akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-exactfit (-2.280%), and akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-singlepass-fit (-1.789%), each over 20 alternating tg128 pairs with a 0.638% floor. The hypothesis is also self-falsified by existing pre-change disassembly: the eight-warp cell uses 53-54 VGPR, so two 8-wave CTAs already co-reside; the claimed >64-VGPR, 1-CTA/CU premise is false. The revised width gate does not create a new mechanism and is exact-fit only at 160 blocks. | Already measured as akm-rmsnorm-5120-float4-singlepass on 2026-09-05. That candidate targeted the same 5120-wide rms_norm_f32<1024,true,false,false> route, retained x in registers across block_reduce, and reused it for the multiply/store pass; it also vectorized the direct mul path. It passed compilation and MUL_MAT 1139/1139, then measured +0.525% over 20 alternating tg128 pairs, inside the then-calibrated 0.638% floor. The numeric result is stale-epoch, but the fact that this mechanism was tried remains admissible. Also, 5120/1024 is five scalar elements per thread, not five float4 vectors; five float4 values per thread would cover 20,480 elements.

statement: The profile rows 5+10 are rms_norm_f32<1024,true,false,false> (3.05%, 16,641 calls) and rms_norm_f32<256,true,false,false> (1.12%, 10,320 calls) - 4.17% combined, the largest patchable share on this decode surface that this lane has NOT mined (the two kept rms mechanisms, akm-rmsnorm-1536-float4-384 and akm-rmsnorm-1536-direct-mul-index, are host-gated to ncols==1536 only). Mechanism: in norm.cu the rms_norm_f32 kernel's non-384 branch (the one the 5120-wide CONFIRM-rung tensors actually instantiate) reads every x element from global memory TWICE - once in the ss accumulation loop (norm.cu:139 chunk loop) and again in the apply/multiply loop that writes dst. At decode bs=1 each call is a single CTA (grid (nrows=1, nchannels=1, nsamples=1)) of 1024 threads over a 5120-wide row, so the per-call ~7.7 us is two serial global round-trip chains capped at one CU's bandwidth slice; removing the second x re-read is ~2/3 of the traffic and one full latency chain. Change: generalize the kept 384 exact-fit trick to the chunked instantiation - each thread loads its 5 column chunks (5120/1024) as float4 vectors into registers ONCE before the ss reduction, accumulates ss from the register copy, and produces dst from the same register-resident values (the mul weight read stays global). Register cost is ~20 VGPR/thread (5 x float4), trivial for a 1024-thread CTA that is already the only CTA resident. Numerics are bit-identical: identical x values, identical per-thread accumulation order, identical scale arithmetic; no type/dispatch/table change, kernel-local to norm.cu, and the ncols==1536 path is untouched. Expected: rms kernel time down ~30-45%, i.e. ~1.2-1.9% end-to-end on the 27B tg128 surface, from halving the x global traffic and collapsing two dependent global sweeps into one.

outcome.refusal_reason: effect -0.480% did not clear the 0.638% noise floor

statement: On the captured tg128 decode surface every MMVQ node quantizes its own activation: ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q (mmvq.cu:2507-2511) launches quantize_q8_1_1d (rocprof row 3: 3.61% device, 33505 calls, ~4.5us each) unless the committed q8_1 graph cache (mmvq.cu:2499, keep akm-q8-0-q8-1-graph-cache-row +0.818%) already holds that src1. On the norm-produced edges - pre-attn/pre-ffn rms_norm feeding the fused-gate cell (49.40%) and the qkv/o/down cells (26.69%) - that quantize launch is serial latency between producer and matmul: rms_norm writes f32 to global, quantize re-reads it and writes padded block_q8_1 rows, mul_mat_vec_q reads them back (mmvq.cu:1296). Fold the quantize into the producer by adding SEPARATE producer-only kernel variants (rms_norm_f32_q8_1_out, l2_norm_f32_q8_1_out) in norm.cu that write both the f32 dst and the block_q8_1 rows in one launch, bit-identical to quantize_q8_1_1d (d = amax/127 over each 32-lane group: amax is order-free so the reduction is exact; the per-lane quantize formulas are replicated), and register the buffer in the existing graph cache so the consumer skips its launch. This answers both standing rejections by construction: (1) the existing rms_norm_f32/l2_norm_f32 kernels, signatures, launch sites and f32 outputs stay byte-identical for every unmarked node - the producer kernels are new instantiations selected only for marked producers, so the default path and all non-captured execution are untouched; (2) the capture lookahead marks a norm only when it counts at least one consumer actually dispatched as a compute MMVQ node in this capture (same gate as the committed cache keep: HIP-graph capture active, stream 0, ids==null, type in {Q4_K,Q6_K,Q8_0}, ne11==1), so graph-output/dead norms are never marked. Numerics are exactly preservable (no reassociation, no type-traits change), so the MUL_MAT oracle is a valid gate. Expected effect: up to the full 3.61% row minus the added norm epilogue, ~+1.5-3% decode, and the mechanism is quant-agnostic so the 1.5B Q4_K screen rung (identical norm->Q8_1->MMVQ shape) is the cheap A/B arm.

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured three times against champion fe881991f under equivalent five-warp, vdr=4, 5120-wide exact-fit mechanisms. All used 20 alternating tg128 pairs and decisively regressed by 1.931%, 2.280%, and 1.789% versus the 0.638% floor. | The mechanism incorrectly counts per-lane work as wave-issued instructions. On gfx90a, the scale loads, f16-to-f32 conversions, and multiplies are already single wave instructions executed across the lanes; restricting them to even lanes only changes EXEC masking and does not halve their static or issued instruction count. The existing reduction tree also executes the same instructions when odd-lane values are zero. The patch would instead add an i32 DPP merge and masking/control overhead. Consequently, the mandatory llvm-objdump pre-check cannot show the claimed halving, and this scale-elision formulation was already rejected in the current epoch under akm-cdna2-q8-b1-parity-u32-vloads for exactly this reason. A viable variant must compact useful work into the vacated lanes or pack independent blocks/rows so the number of emitted scale instructions actually falls. | The mechanism still counts lane executions as wave-issued instructions and fails its own objdump precheck. At vdr=4, kbx0=tid/2 places the 160 blocks in five active waves; vdr=8 with kbx0=tid places them in three active waves, so the claimed unchanged 20-blocks-per-warp split is impossible. The scale chain remains one static instruction sequence per unrolled row, not two sequences that objdump can show falling to one. Dynamic scale-chain issue would fall only from five waves to three, while the unrolled load and v_dot4c body doubles from 4 to 8 operations, increasing wave-issued dots from 20 to 24 and potentially load groups from 5 to 6. Alternatively, preserving a 20-block-per-warp split keeps all eight waves issuing under sparse EXEC masks and removes no issue slots. Therefore the stated scale-chain halving is unsupported, and the mandatory llvm-objdump falsifier cannot observe the claimed mechanism. Reformulation requires one concrete lane/block mapping and a whole-loop wave-instruction accounting, not per-block lane counts.

statement: Extend the champion's own last keep on the two dominant decode instantiations (fe881991f akm-cdna2-q8-b1-singlepass-vdr4, +0.892%): that commit doubled the Q8_0 eight_warp small_k cell from vdr=2 to vdr=4, halving threads per 32-int8 block (qi/vdr 4->2) so the per-block f32 scale chain (v_cvt_f32_f16 of the block scale d, v_cvt_f32_i32 of the int sum, v_mul, v_fmac against the shared activation scale) is emitted by 2 lanes per block instead of 4, and its own comment frames the arithmetic as 'regrouped 4 threads to 2'. The next step on the same axis is vdr=8 (qi/vdr=1): one lane per full 32-int8 q8_0/q8_1 block, so each thread runs 8 chained v_dot4c over the whole block into a single i32 (exact, no rounding change: block sums were per-half scaled twice into the same f32 accumulator, now summed in i32 first), and the scale chain is issued once per block-row instead of twice by two different lanes - cvt_f16(d)+v_mul+v_fmac per weight block roughly halves. Same numerics class as the vdr=4 keep (numerically-valid-not-bit-exact, the int sum over a full block is exact so rounding count per block falls 2->1). The champion gfx90a disassembly emits global_load_dwordx4 offset:2 directly from the misaligned Q8_0 qs addresses: five x4 loads in the unfused target (one activation plus four weight rows) and nine in the fused target (one activation plus four value and four gate rows). The scale remains a separate global_load_ushort even with two planes, so repacking does not remove that read. Any duplicate qs dword load is a distinct compiler/load-expression issue, not evidence for an SoA layout limiter. statement: block_q8_0 is 34 B (2 B f16 d + 32 B int8 qs), so qs starts at byte 34b+2: 4 B aligned only for odd block index, 8 B aligned for b=3 (mod 4), 16 B aligned for b=7 (mod 8). The 32 B payload that dominates the decode weight stream can therefore never be read as aligned dwordx4 per block, and the 2 B d forces a second narrow global read every 34 B. The two mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8, 1, ...> instantiations are 76.1% of device time and run at ~49% of peak HBM BW, below the ~62% ceiling measured with 16 B-aligned f16 weights. Mechanism: at set_tensor, repack every Q8_0 row into two 16 B-aligned planes (d[] and qs[]; identical byte count, pad <1%), and route all readers (vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1, the MMQ Q8_0 block loader, dequantize_block_q8_0) through one plane-reading helper so MMVQ decode, MMQ and dequant+Tensile share the single repacked buffer (K19: no second 28 GB copy). Layout-only, so numerics are bit-identical; this is not the fp16_act_route family (activations untouched). The decode dot then issues one aligned dwordx4 per 32 weights instead of misaligned narrow accesses plus a d read. Unlike every tried row/geometry variant (quadrow-vec-tail +0.30%, 3/3), this changes the on-disk-adjacent layout axis, which no measured mechanism has touched. Step zero is free: objdump the champion's Q8_0 mul_mat_vec_q and count load widths on the qs stream before any patch is written.

outcome.refusal_reason: Already measured, three times today against the current champion fe881991f with this exact mechanism (calc_nwarps eight_warp_q8_cdna2 arm 8->5, vdr=4, four-row CTA, 160-block single-pass exact fit at ne00=5120): akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-exactfit (2026-09-07T09:03Z, tg128 -2.280%, 20 pairs, floor 0.638%), akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-singlepass-fit (11:12Z, -1.789%, 20 pairs) and akm-cdna2-q8-b1-five-warp-exact-fit (13:22Z, -2.272% raw; unresolved due to instrument drift). Two decisive negatives and one drift-confounded negative, all in the same direction; the arithmetic (4*5*64/8 = 160 blocks/iter) is correct but the 320-thread CTA measurably loses to the 512-thread one on gfx90a, plausibly because 5 waves pack unevenly across the CU's 4 SIMDs and the 3 idle waves cost nothing on the memory-bound stream. Several later formations (vdr8-fullblock, vgpr40-sixwave, fused-y-quant) were already refused for restating this point. Nothing in this hypothesis says what is different from those runs; it is the identical geometry under a new name. Do not re-propose nwarps=5 on this cell without new evidence (e.g. a rocprofv3 occupancy/wave-slot receipt explaining the three negatives). | The mechanism has nothing to unroll on the champion. Since akm-cdna2-q8-b1-singlepass-vdr4 (fe881991f), the CDNA2 dense bs=1 Q8_0 cell runs at vdr=4 with nwarps=8, so blocks_per_iter = 4*8*64/8 = 256 >= 160 blocks per 5120-wide row and the runtime k-loop at mmvq.cu:1348 executes exactly ONE trip per thread (the kernel comment at :1140-1152 states this: 'the whole row is consumed in one k-pass'; threads with kbx0 >= 160 fall out on the first compare). A static ne00==5120 specialization mirroring the 1536 path (:1307-1313, kbx_iters = ceil(160/256) = 1) would therefore produce the identical single-trip body with the loop compare folded to a constant predicate: the same 4 dwordx? loads and 4 dot4 per row per thread, no additional independent loads or dot4 operations exposed, and no runtime address arithmetic removed beyond one integer compare and one branch per thread per launch. The claimed benefit ('exposes more independent loads and dot4 operations across kernels holding 76% of device time') is unsupported by the code as it stands; the expected effect is well inside the 0.638% floor. Note also that the kept 1536 specialization's value came from the Q4_K/Q6_K multi-trip loop (kbx_iters > 1 at 1536 with vdr=2/nwarps=4), which is not the situation here. If the planner wants a static-K lever on this cell it must first show, e.g. via llvm-objdump of the champion's mul_mat_vec_q<Q8_0,1,...> code object, that the single-trip loop still emits material runtime k-index arithmetic or a non-trivial control-flow structure that a constant K would delete; absent that receipt the hypothesis is a no-op restated as an optimization. | Mechanism unsupported by the physics of this cell and by the record it cites. Re-mapping to 512 lanes x 2-3 dwords leaves the CU's in-flight request count identical (1280 dword loads per row either way) and the weight bytes identical, so on a stream that is memory-bound (the loop's own note: '3 idle waves cost nothing') the saving is one load issue + one dot4 per wave, a few VALU cycles against microsecond memory latency, well inside the 0.638% floor. (2) The map costs more than it saves: 192 extra lanes each add a block d (ushort) load and a Q8_1 y ds load plus y qs loads, so per-row L1/LDS traffic rises ~60% on the activation/scale side; the 3+3+2 / 2+2+2+2 split is lane-divergent inside a wave (waves covering 3-lane blocks still execute the 3-op maximum with a third of lanes masked on the last op), and it breaks the uniform constexpr vdr template (vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1_impl<float, vdr> at :1084/:1386) into per-lane variable dword counts, i.e. predicated loads and a runtime-indexed fragment table, which the rejection of the 5-wave family already flagged as the class of change that measurably loses here. (3) No receipt: the hypothesis gathers nothing itself (no rocprofv3 MemUnitStalled vs VALU-busy split, no llvm-objdump of the champion's Q8_0 code object showing the per-lane chain is on the critical path), so the claim that shortening a 4-op chain to 2-3 ops moves a 76%-share BW-bound kernel is a prior, not evidence. Re-propose only with a profile receipt showing this kernel is issue/VALU-limited rather than MemUnitStalled, or an objdump showing a genuine load->dot serial dependency that the map would break.

statement: For dense ne11==1 Q8_0 on gfx90a, add an f32-activation mul_mat_vec_q variant and bypass quantize_q8_1 only when every consumer of that cached activation row is eligible; otherwise retain the champion path. Cover both fused and unfused instantiations, passing ggml_cuda_mm_fusion_args_device through the unchanged bias/gate/SwiGLU epilogue. The four-row CTA reads each 16-value activation fragment through four aligned global_load_dwordx4 operations, immediately packs one float4 at a time with v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32, and reuses the resulting half2 pairs across its four weight rows. Q8_0 bytes are sign-extracted with v_bfe_i32, converted with v_cvt_f32_i32, packed with v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32, and accumulated using v_dot2_f32_f16. This deliberately trades the current one v_dot4_i32_i8 per weight dword for roughly 4 extracts, 4 converts, 2 packs, and 2 dot2 operations. It also raises activation traffic per CTA from 5.8 KB Q8_1 to 20.5 KB f32, while leaving the 21.8 KB weight stream unchanged: +14.7 KB per CTA, +53% total vector bytes, and about +19 MB L2-to-L1 traffic per 5120x5120 matmul. The bet is that the small activation remains L2-resident across CTAs and mandatory dwordx4 loads keep VMEM instruction count near the Q8_1 path, while weight HBM latency hides the added VALU. Process one float4 at a time so activation temporaries do not accumulate; accept the specialization only if llvm-objdump confirms dwordx4 activation loads, <=64 VGPR, and no added LDS, preserving the 512-thread occupancy geometry. Suppressing the shared quantize launch only after all its Q8 consumers use this variant targets the measured 3.67% ceiling without changing activation types, type traits, or dispatch-table entries.
